A mutual pair (each impacts what the other changes) is a cycle the skill does not tell the orchestrator how to break; it fell out of the fixture design and was avoided rather than answered. Adjacent, not blocking.

title: Extract the explanatory prose to references/: Operating principles, the Phase 4 report spec, and the tier rationale
description:
Even after the content-reducing beads land, `bead-bonanza/SKILL.md` is over the
~20,000-byte re-injection cap and the operative procedure is still on the wrong
side of it.

Arithmetic, measured 2026-08-10 (body 45,983 bytes):

| Removal | Bytes |
|---|---|
| Phase 0 mechanics -> pre-flight script | 3,047 |
| Phase 2 deleted | 4,280 |
| Dispatch-plan lean-path branches deleted | 2,145 |
| **subtotal (sibling beads)** | **9,472** |
| Operating principles -> references/ | 7,749 |
| Phase 4 report specification -> references/ | 3,105 |
| **total** | **20,326 -> 25,657 remaining** |

Still ~28% over. The remainder has to come from the tier-selection rationale
and the main-loop fallback (`SKILL.md:447-522`, ~4 KB), which are explanatory
rather than executable.

The principle that decides what moves: **everything an orchestrator EXECUTES
stays above the cap; everything that explains WHY moves out.** After a
compaction the orchestrator needs the execution loop, the close ceremony's
ordering, the acceptance check, the circuit breaker and the script interfaces.
It does not need the essay on why batching beats sequential — it needs the
rule, and it can read the essay on demand.

This is the pattern the skill already uses successfully for `recovery.md` and
`subagent-prompts.md`.
design:
Move, do not rewrite. The target is a faithful relocation with a one-line
pointer left behind, not a re-authoring — re-authoring in the same pass makes
the diff unreviewable and risks losing rules nobody notices are gone.

**Stays above the cap (the executable core):**
- The post-compaction re-read instruction (already at the top).
- Phase 0 as reduced: two blocks, the pre-flight script, the draft-PR question.
- Phase 1 queue resolution; Phase 1.5's gate steps and the mid-run scope test.
- Phase 2.5's classification, the four dispatch modes, the tier RULES (not the
  rationale), push policy.
- **All of Phase 3**: the execution loop, the post-return verification steps,
  the skip reconciliation, the acceptance check, the circuit breaker.
- The Reference-files table and the three (soon four) published script
  interfaces. These are published *because* the scripts are declared "executed,
  not read"; an agent that must open a script to learn how to call it has
  already been sent to read it.

**Moves to `references/`:**
- Operating principles (`:692-802`, 7,749 bytes) -> `references/operating-principles.md`.
  Keep a short list of pointer-lines in SKILL.md naming each principle in five
  words, so the orchestrator knows what exists to look up.
- Phase 4's report specification (`:629-690`, 3,105 bytes) ->
  `references/final-report.md`. Phase 4 in SKILL.md becomes: drain, then produce
  the report per that file, then the sprint retro.
- Tier-selection rationale and the main-loop fallback (`:447-522`) ->
  `references/tier-routing.md`. The RULES that survive in SKILL.md: resolve
  tier via the lineup, never dispatch below tier, escalate one tier on repeated
  failure, never downgrade, record every escalation. The rationale — the
  over-routing asymmetry, why zero escalations is not a clean bill of health,
  the degradation notice for the no-Agent case — moves.
- Phase 1.5's grooming rationale (`:163-178` and the prose in step 4) — move the
  *why*, keep the gate steps and the three qualifying shapes of emergent work.

**Rules for the move:**
1. Every moved section gets a row in the Reference-files table with a "load
   this WHEN" condition, matching the table's existing form.
2. No rule may exist only in a reference file if an orchestrator must obey it
   without being told to load that file. When in doubt, leave the one-line rule
   above the cap and move the paragraph explaining it.
3. Do not renumber phases. Other documents and beads cite them.
4. New reference files carry the same header conventions as the existing ones
   (Contents list, purpose line, 80-column wrap).
5. `scripts/sync-shared-references.sh --check` must still pass — do not move
   anything into or out of `references/shared/`, which is generated.

Sequence this bead AFTER the pre-flight, Phase 2 and dispatch-plan beads: it
extracts from whatever content remains, and doing it first means doing it twice.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Operating principles live in references/operating-principles.md, with five-word pointer lines remaining in SKILL.md
- [ ] The Phase 4 report specification lives in references/final-report.md and Phase 4 cites it
- [ ] The tier rationale and the main-loop fallback live in references/tier-routing.md; the tier rules remain in SKILL.md
- [ ] Phase 3's execution loop, post-return verification, circuit breaker and the script interface table are all still in SKILL.md
- [ ] Every new reference file has a row in the Reference-files table with a load-this-WHEN condition
- [ ] Phase numbering is unchanged
- [ ] scripts/sync-shared-references.sh --check passes and nothing under references/shared/ was moved
- [ ] No normative rule exists solely in a reference file that an orchestrator must obey without being told to load it

metadata.tier_reason: Large relocation across five files where the recurring judgment — is this rule executable or explanatory — decides whether a rule survives compaction. Faithful-move discipline under a size target.

title: dispatch.md is the sprint plan: write it unconditionally, enumerate the beads, add a run manifest and an amendments log
description:
`dispatch.md` is the sprint plan. Three defects make it unfit for the one job
that matters most — being the thing a recovering orchestrator reads instead of
re-deriving the run.

**1. It is optional.** `SKILL.md:370-391` skips the formal plan when the queue
is under 5 beads, when all beads land in one bucket, or when the user gave an
explicit ID list — replacing it with a one-line statement in chat. Chat is the
one store that does not survive. Recovery does not care how large the run was;
a two-bead run interrupted at bead one needs the plan exactly as much as a
twenty-bead run does.

**2. It identifies scope by filter, not by enumeration.** The plan is produced
from `bd ready --label <x>` and the table is described as the output of that
query. Two failures follow. Beads get added to an epic or gain the label during
the sprint, and a filter re-evaluated later silently pulls them in. And
`references/recovery.md`'s recovery path — reinforced by the orchestrator-death
procedure being added in a sibling bead — instructs a recovering orchestrator to
"read `dispatch.md`; this is the plan; do not re-derive it". **A filter
re-evaluated at recovery returns a different queue than the one the run
committed to.** That is not a stale plan; it is a silent scope change during the
least-supervised moment of the run.

**3. It is written once and never amended.** Observed twice in run
`1786121603-ri`: wave 5 was planned as one shared batch (`9kb.6`, `9kb.7`,
`9kb.9`) and re-decided mid-run as strictly sequential; the re-decision was
recorded in the epic's tracker notes because the skill offered no home for it.
Separately the plan's wave ordering and the commits' actual ordering diverged
(`.6` 21:34, `.7` 21:58, `.8` 22:17, `.9` 22:24 against a plan that had `.8`
alone after the batch). A plan that silently stops describing the run is worse
than no plan, because recovery trusts it.

Framing recorded 2026-08-10: the plan is the sprint plan, and it is written for
whoever picks the sprint back up — which may be an agent with no memory of
having written it.


## Retro — implementation

### Findings

- `scripts/check-skills.sh` treats any backticked token that looks like a
  filename as a path to resolve relative to the file it appears in. Naming
  `pre-flight-check.sh` in prose inside `references/dispatch-plan.md` was two
  hard errors, not a warning. Written as `../scripts/pre-flight-check.sh`
  instead. Nothing in the bead or in the skill's own conventions warns that
  prose mentions of a sibling script must be spelled as resolvable paths.
- The Design's line anchors (`SKILL.md:370-391`, `:534-558`) were already stale
  by the time this bead ran: the sibling bead in the same batch
  (`agent-plugins-92q.3`) rewrote Phase 0 first and shifted everything below
  it. Matched the regions by text instead. Line anchors in a bead that shares a
  file with another bead in the same batch cannot be trusted.

### What I tried that did not work

- First cut kept an abbreviated wave-table template inline in SKILL.md and
  moved only the manifest and amendments log to `references/`. That reproduces
  the format in two places, which is exactly the drift the amendments rule
  exists to prevent — and Design item 4 already says the format is a
  dispatch-time lookup. The whole format now lives in
  `references/dispatch-plan.md` and SKILL.md carries only the three
  load-bearing rules plus the pointer.

### What I decided silently

- Put the new `### The dispatch plan` section at the END of Phase 2.5, where
  the conditional "When you write the formal plan" section was, rather than at
  the start where the deleted lean path sat. The plan's columns (class, bucket,
  tier, push mode) are all decided by the subsections between those two points;
  an unconditional write instruction placed first would reference columns the
  reader has not met yet.
- Kept the decisions-doc lean path in the Operating principles bullet and
  narrowed the bullet to it, rather than deleting the bullet. Only the dispatch
  plan lost its exemption; nothing in this bead touches the decisions doc.
design:
Three changes to Phase 2.5, all in `SKILL.md`.

**1. Delete the lean path** (`SKILL.md:370-391`, 919 bytes) and the conditional
"When you write the formal plan" framing (`:534-558`, 1,226 bytes). The plan is
unconditional. Replace both with one instruction and a pointer to the template.
Net effect on file size is negative — the two deleted branches are larger than
the instruction that replaces them, and the template itself moves to
`references/`.

**2. Enumerate, and freeze.** The plan's bead table SHALL list explicit bead
ids. State why, in one sentence, so a later editor does not re-introduce the
filter form:

> The plan names beads, never a filter. The filter produced the queue; the plan
> IS the queue. A filter re-evaluated later — at recovery, or at the next wave —
> returns a different set than the one this run committed to, and admits beads
> nobody scoped.

Beads discovered mid-run enter the plan only through Phase 1.5 step 4's scope
test, recorded as an amendment.

**3. Add a run manifest and an amendments log.** The plan gains a header before
the wave table, carrying what a recovering orchestrator needs and cannot
re-derive:

```
run id, RUN_DIR, branch, base sha, the resolved gate profile, the gate
baseline (from pre-flight), the environmental ledger, the resolved model
lineup, the standing authorization the user granted, and the enumerated
bead list with wave / class / bucket / tier / push mode / reason
```

Most of these come straight from `pre-flight-check.sh`'s stdout block (sibling
bead) — the plan is where that output lands durably.

And an append-only amendments section:

> `dispatch.md` is **append-only and amendable**. WHEN the plan changes mid-run
> — a wave resequenced, a bucket reclassified, a bead admitted or bounced, a
> tier escalated — append a dated entry under `## Amendments` stating what
> changed and why, AND update the wave table in place. The plan on disk SHALL
> describe the run as it is actually being executed. Mirror one line of each
> amendment to the tracker note that carries the RUN_DIR pointer, so a reader
> who has only the tracker knows the plan moved.

**4. Move the table template to `references/`.** The plan's format is a
dispatch-time lookup, not something the orchestrator holds in context. Put it
with the other dispatch material and cite it from the Reference-files table.

## Interaction with sibling beads

- The RUN_DIR pointer and the `.bonanza/<run-id>/` backup are separate beads;
  this one only requires that the manifest exists and names `RUN_DIR`.
- The environmental-ledger *admission rule* (entries cite the command that
  proved them) is a separate bead that edits the same ledger section — expect a
  textual collision and sequence accordingly.
- Keep "Don't ask for approval — just print and proceed." The plan is not a
  gate; it is a record.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] SKILL.md contains no lean path for the dispatch plan and no conditional on queue size or bucket count
- [ ] The plan is stated to name explicit bead ids, with the one-sentence rationale against filter-identified scope
- [ ] The plan format includes a run manifest carrying run id, RUN_DIR, branch, base sha, gate profile, gate baseline, environmental ledger, model lineup and standing authorization
- [ ] The plan format includes an append-only '## Amendments' section, and the rule requires updating the wave table in place as well as appending
- [ ] The amendment rule requires mirroring one line to the tracker note
- [ ] The table template lives in references/ and is cited from the Reference-files table
- [ ] 'Don't ask for approval — just print and proceed' is retained
- [ ] Net SKILL.md byte change for this bead is zero or negative

metadata.tier_reason: Bounded rewrite of one phase with the new format fully specified; the judgment (why enumeration beats a filter) is settled in the description.

title: Delete SKILL.md Phase 2: the readiness gate owns decisions, and refinement does not run inside the sprint
description:
`SKILL.md` Phase 2 — Decisions (`:266-361`) is **96 lines / 4,280 bytes, 9.3% of
the file**, and every byte of it sits inside the ~20,000-byte window that
survives compaction. It therefore competes directly with Phase 3's execution
loop and the close ceremony for the context an orchestrator actually needs, and
wins, because it comes first in the file.

What it does: re-reads every bead with `bd show`, classifies each one's
decision state as `explicit` / `implicit` / `none`, writes a `decisions.md`,
issues `AskUserQuestion`, and bakes the answers back into bead descriptions
with `## DECISION (<date>)` sections — then forbids any further questions.

**All of that is refinement, running inside the sprint.** It is a leftover from
an early version of the skill that did not have a readiness gate. Phase 1.5 now
gates the whole queue against the Definition of Ready before anything is
dispatched, and Phase 1.5 step 4 already routes mid-run admissions through the
same gate. Once the DoR requires decisions to be closed (sibling bead), a bead
that reaches Phase 2 with an open decision is a bead that should have been
bounced at Phase 1.5 — so Phase 2's explicit-decision path is unreachable by
construction, and its implicit-decision path is either an acceptance-criteria
gap (also a readiness failure) or a choice that belongs in the retro.

The mechanism that keeps the sprint honest is unchanged and lives elsewhere:
the gate bounces what it cannot clear, and the user resolves bounced beads
before the run — once, up front, as admission decisions rather than as a
mid-flight questionnaire.

Framing decision recorded 2026-08-10: a bead-bonanza run is a sprint. Ceremony
that grooming already owns does not belong inside it.
design:
Delete Phase 2 in full (`SKILL.md:266-361`, heading through Step 2c) and
redistribute the three things worth keeping.

**1. Into the Phase 1.5 readiness gate**, as one bullet in the cheap-check list
(`SKILL.md:181-192`):

> - no open decision — no `decision-required` label, no "DECISION REQUIRED" /
>   "TBD" / unresolved options list. This is DoR check 9; a bead that fails it
>   is bounced, not questioned mid-run.

**2. Into Phase 1.5 step 3 (Bounce what grooming can't clear)**, one sentence
making the user-facing consequence explicit: bounced beads are surfaced with
their open question at the end of the gate, the user resolves them (or grooms
them) before dispatch, and the run proceeds with the Ready remainder. This is
the single decision point of the run and it is an *admission* decision.

**3. Into Phase 1.5 step 4 (Admitting emergent work mid-run)**, one sentence:
a bead admitted mid-run goes through grooming, and grooming includes closing
its decisions; a groomed prerequisite that still lands a `decision-required`
label stops for the user under the standing-authorization terms. (The last
clause already exists at `SKILL.md:252-253` — keep it, it is now the only
mid-run stop.)

**4. Silently-made choices** are already the retro's job. Ensure the retro
template's "what you decided silently" item survives — that is the sibling
retro-reshape bead's territory, so cross-reference rather than duplicating.

otherwise dangle. At minimum:

- `SKILL.md:44-52` run checklist — remove item 2, renumber.
- `SKILL.md:120-123` — the run-directory contents list names "the decisions doc".
- `SKILL.md:686-688` Phase 4 item 3 — "Implicit decisions made — extract from

- `SKILL.md` Operating principles — "Surface implicit decisions, don't bury

title: Definition of Ready: require decisions to be closed, and narrow the sanctioned hedge in the Design check
description:
The Definition of Ready has eight checks and **none of them requires a work
order's decisions to be closed.** The gap is not an oversight in the list — the
standard actively permits an open decision:

`plugin/skills/spec/references/work-order-definition-of-ready.md:70-74`
(check 3, `## Design` present):

> Anything past a one-liner needs a Design: the chosen approach and the
> decisions that would otherwise get re-litigated by a time-pressured agent.
> It's mutable and **may hedge** ("leaning toward X because Y; fall back to Z
> if the API can't do it").

"Leaning toward X; fall back to Z" is an open decision, sanctioned by the
standard. `grep -in "decision" work-order-definition-of-ready.md` returns
exactly that one line — there is no other mention in the document.

Downstream, `bead-bonanza` compensates for the gap with an entire phase.
`SKILL.md` Phase 2 (`:266-361`, 96 lines / 4,280 bytes) re-reads every bead,
classifies its decision state as `explicit`/`implicit`/`none`, writes a
decisions document, batch-asks the user, and bakes the answers back into bead
descriptions — mid-sprint, after the readiness gate has already declared the
queue ready. That is backlog refinement happening inside the sprint.

A run is a sprint; grooming is refinement. Decisions belong to refinement. The
readiness gate should be able to state flatly that a groomed bead carries no
open decision, and today it cannot, because the standard it enforces says the
opposite.

This bead closes the standard's gap. The sibling bead deletes the phase that
exists to compensate for it, and cannot land first: deleting Phase 2 while the
DoR still sanctions hedged Designs would remove the safety net and leave the
hole it was covering.

Ownership: the `spec` skill owns this standard. `bead-bonanza` and
`groom-beads` carry generated copies under `references/shared/`, regenerated by
`scripts/sync-shared-references.sh` — the copies must never be hand-edited.


## Retro — implementation

### Findings
- The standard was not the only place sanctioning a hedge. `plugin/skills/spec/references/work-order-template.md:160` carries the same permission as a normative MAY ("It MAY hedge (\"leaning X because Y; fall back to Z...\")") in the `## Design` authoring comment, and it is vendored into two more skills. The bead's Design enumerated the files to touch and did not include it; landing check 9 without it would ship a template that instructs authors to write exactly what the gate now bounces.
- The bead's own worked Example 1 hedged: its Design read "Leaning on golang-jwt/jwt v5". The standard would have failed its own example. Rewritten to state the choice and the rejected alternative.
- groom-beads' checklist at SKILL.md:121 is a phase list (0-7), not an enumeration of the DoR's checks as the Design describes it. Its items are cross-referenced by number elsewhere in the file ("phase 6", "phase 4", "phase 2"), so a new numbered item cannot be inserted without breaking those references.
- Landing this bead's first draft pushed `plugin/skills/groom-beads/SKILL.md` from 19,554 to 20,195 body bytes, tripping the byte gate that the immediately-preceding sibling bead (agent-plugins-92q.2) installed. Two beads in one batch, the second's normal-size prose addition made red by the first's new threshold. The additions were compressed to ~275 bytes; the file now sits at 19,828, only 172 bytes under.

### What I tried that did not work
- First draft added a five-line "An open decision is a bounce, not a guess" paragraph to groom-beads' bounce section plus a two-line checklist sub-item. Correct content, but it is what tripped the byte gate. Replaced by folding the same rule into the existing `blocked-needs-info` bullet as a clause.

### What I decided silently
- The checklist gets a sub-item `2a` rather than a new top-level `9`, to keep the 0-7 phase numbering that the rest of the file cites intact.
- Check 9's title is "No open decisions" (the Contents line and the section heading match), and it is placed after check 8 rather than beside check 3, so the existing eight keep their numbers.
- The template's fix mirrors the standard's wording rather than pointing at it: the comment is read while authoring, when the standard is not open.
- Frontmatter `updated_at` was moved to 2026-08-10 along with the version bump; the bead only named the version.

### Observed pre-fix failure
Not a defect bead. The pre-change state is quoted in the bead's Description: `work-order-definition-of-ready.md:70-74` sanctioned the hedge outright, and `grep -in decision` over the document returned that one line and nothing else.
design:
Edit the source at
`plugin/skills/spec/references/work-order-definition-of-ready.md`, then
re-vendor.

**1. Narrow check 3's hedge allowance.** A Design may still record the
alternatives that were weighed — preserving them is the point of the section —
but it may not leave the choice open. Replace the "may hedge" sentence with a
statement that separates the two cases:

> It records the alternatives that were weighed and the one that was chosen;
> preserving the rejected options is what stops a later agent re-litigating
> them. It SHALL NOT leave the choice itself open. A conditional that a fresh
> agent can resolve mechanically from the repository ("use the API's batch
> endpoint; if it is absent on the pinned version, loop the single-item call")
> is a chosen approach with a stated fallback and passes. A conditional whose
> resolution needs a judgment the order does not supply ("leaning toward X
> because Y; fall back to Z if that does not work out") is an open decision and
> fails this check.

**2. Add check 9 — decisions closed.** Append to the numbered list in Contents
and add the section. Draft, in EARS where normative:

> ### 9. No open decisions
> The work order SHALL carry no unresolved choice. It fails this check WHEN it
> carries a `decision-required` label, a "DECISION REQUIRED" / "TBD" / "open
> question" marker, or an options list with no option marked as selected.
>
> WHERE an open choice would change the order's observable behaviour, it is an
> acceptance-criteria gap and fails check 4 as well — pin the behaviour in the
> AC, not in prose.
>
> A choice a diff-reader would not recognise AS a choice — an internal helper's
> name, the order of two independent guard clauses — is not an open decision
> and does not fail this check. The implementing agent records what it picked
> in its retro.
>
> **This check is why a groomed order is dispatchable without a conversation.**
> An orchestrator that must surface decisions at dispatch time is doing
> refinement inside execution; that work belongs here, at grooming.

**3. Version bump** the standard's frontmatter `version` 1.2 -> 1.3 per
[[template-authoring-standards]].

**4. Re-vendor** with `scripts/sync-shared-references.sh` and confirm the
generated copies under `plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/references/shared/` and any
other consumer now carry check 9 and the updated header version. Then
`scripts/sync-shared-references.sh --check` must pass.

**5. Propagate to `groom-beads`.** Its checklist at
`plugin/skills/groom-beads/SKILL.md:121` enumerates the DoR checks
("- [ ] 5. C4 blast radius tagged..."). Add the new check to that checklist so
grooming actually enforces it; a check the enforcing skill does not list is not
enforced. Also confirm `bd lint`-adjacent guidance and the bounce path treat an
open decision as a bounce-to-human, not a guess.

Do NOT change the tier rubric, the C4 conventions, or any other check.

- [ ] The standard's frontmatter version is bumped 1.2 -> 1.3
- [ ] scripts/sync-shared-references.sh has been re-run and --check passes
- [ ] The vendored copy under plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/references/shared/ carries check 9 and the new header version
- [ ] groom-beads' readiness checklist enumerates the new check
- [ ] No other DoR check, the tier rubric, or the C4 conventions were changed

title: Add pre-flight-check.sh: mechanize Phase 0 on macOS and Linux, and measure what it currently asserts
description:
bead-bonanza's Phase 0 is `SKILL.md:54-142` — **89 lines, ~4,600 bytes**, all of
it inside the ~20,000-byte window that survives compaction, and most of it
mechanical. It spends that budget describing shell commands rather than
judgment, while the judgment-bearing phases sit past the truncation point.

Audit of the six steps, done 2026-08-10:

| # | Step | Mechanical? |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Load `## bead-bonanza gates` + `## model lineup` | detection only |
| 2 | Beads telemetry (`SKILL.md:74-98`, 25 lines) | fully |
| 3 | Run scratch directory + `SCRIPTS` path (`:99-123`) | fully |
| 4 | TaskCreate fallback (`:124-129`) | fully, as detection |
| 5 | Push mechanics (`:130-135`) | fully — and it is currently an untested *claim* |
| 6 | Draft-PR ask (`:136-142`) | detection only |

Steps 2, 3 and 5 together are **3,047 bytes** of pure mechanics.

Step 5 is the sharpest case. It is not an action at all today — it is an
assertion ("the sandbox blocks `.git/config` writes, so `--set-upstream` never
persists") carried forward as prose. Bead `agent-plugins-d6x` establishes that
ledger claims must cite the command that proved them; a pre-flight script is
the mechanism that makes that true for the environment, by measuring at run
start what is currently asserted from memory.

Six checks belong in pre-flight and exist nowhere today:

- `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL` — it overrides the per-invocation `model`
  parameter, so if it is set every tier assignment in the dispatch plan is
  silently ignored and the Phase 4 escalation table is fiction. Verified NOT
  set in this container, so it is a latent trap rather than an observed failure.
- `bd` present, `bd where` resolving to a real database.
- `jq` present (the close script, the harvest and the C4 bucketing all need it).
- **Working tree clean at t=0.** A tree already dirty at run start poisons every
  later `bb-verify-skip.sh` result and every pathspec guard.
- Gate baseline capture — a gate that already fails on an untouched tree must be
  recorded as the baseline, or every bead is measured against "exit 0" and
  reports a failure it did not cause.
- The command permissions in `.claude/settings.local.json`.

One check is deliberately NOT in scope: whether an `Agent` tool exists. That is
a harness property, not observable from a shell, and it is the trigger for the
main-loop fallback — it stays an instruction in SKILL.md.

Environment for portability: the script must run on macOS and Linux.


## Retro — implementation

### Findings

- AGENTS.md's `## bead-bonanza gates` block runs 163 lines here and its
  `- **Label:** \`cmd\`` bullet shape continues into `###` prose subsections
  (the KNOWN RED note, the strata install notes). The bead specified "run the
  gate profile's commands" without saying where the profile ends; a naive
  parse over the whole block produced eleven non-commands. Bounded to the
  bullets before the first `###`.
- AC "--self-test exits 0 on Linux and on macOS, and the retro records the
  observed output of both runs" cannot be satisfied from this container —
  there is no macOS host. Linux run: 26 checks, RESULT: PASS, exit 0. The
  macOS half is unverified; the BSD `stat -f` branch is exercised only by the
  probe's fallback logic, not by a BSD `stat`.
- `dolt` is not on PATH here, so only the absent-dolt branch of the telemetry
  step ran. The present-dolt branch (including the sandbox-refusal detection)
  is unexercised.
- The reduction is smaller than the bead's 3,047-byte estimate: SKILL.md went
  46,485 → 44,617 bytes (-1,868), because publishing the new script's
  interface and its bullet adds ~900 bytes back in the Reference-files
  section, which the estimate did not net out.

### What I tried that did not work

- First cut echoed only the four gate bullets instead of the two AGENTS.md
  blocks. That is not what "load the two blocks" means for a reader who then
  still has to open AGENTS.md for the KNOWN RED exception — so it now echoes
  both blocks whole and the read is genuinely replaced.
- CI detection first used one `ls .github/workflows/*.yml *.yaml`. `ls` exits
  nonzero when either glob matches nothing, so a repo with only `.yml`
  workflows reported `BB_PR_CI=no` — wrong here, where two workflows are
  `pull_request`-triggered. Replaced with a per-file loop.
- The portability self-lint first ran over the whole source and flagged the
  header's own prose ("no `stat -c`, no `sed -i`…"). It now strips whole-line
  comments first, so the header stays free to name the constructs it bans.

### What I decided silently

- **Sandbox:** the script runs WITH the sandbox on. It detects the refused
  `dolt config --global` write, skips it, and prints the single command to
  re-run with the sandbox off. Rationale: the alternative would attach
  `dangerouslyDisableSandbox: true` to an invocation that also runs the whole
  gate suite, to buy one telemetry write that is a no-op wherever `dolt` is
  absent. Stated on the published usage line (`# sandbox ON`) and in the
  script header.
- Added `--gate-baseline` as an opt-in flag (the Design permitted guarding it)
  rather than making baseline capture unconditional; `--self-test` takes no
  run id; a run-id containing `/` or a space exits 2.
- Swept the stale `Phase 0 step 1/1a/4/5` cross-references in SKILL.md,
  recovery.md and subagent-prompts.md to non-numeric ones. They were already
  off by one before this change and renumbering would have made them worse.
design:
Add `plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/scripts/pre-flight-check.sh`, and reduce
`SKILL.md`'s Phase 0 to loading the two AGENTS.md blocks, running the script,
and the one question the script cannot ask.

## Interface

```
pre-flight-check.sh <run-id> [--self-test]
```

Writes a human-readable report to stderr and a shell-evalable block to stdout:

```
RUN_DIR=/tmp/claude/bead-bonanza/<run-id>
SCRIPTS=/abs/path/to/plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/scripts
BB_GATES_BLOCK=present
BB_LINEUP_BLOCK=present
BB_TASKCREATE=banned
BB_SUBAGENT_MODEL_OVERRIDE=unset
BB_PR_CI=yes
BB_TREE_CLEAN=yes
BB_PUSH_NEEDS_REFSPEC=yes
```

Exit 0 = safe to proceed; 1 = a blocking condition (dirty tree, no `bd`, missing
gate profile); 2 = bad invocation. Publish the usage line in SKILL.md's script
interface table alongside the existing three — the scripts are declared
"executed, not read", so an unpublished interface forces a read.

## What it does

1. **Blocks.** Assert `## bead-bonanza gates` and `## model lineup` exist in
   `AGENTS.md`; echo them. On absence, exit 1 naming `references/project-setup.md`.
   Do not draft a block — that is a conversation.
2. **Telemetry.** Probe `command -v dolt` first (it is absent in this container;
   a blind `dolt config` fails with `command not found`). When present, read
   `metrics.disabled` and set it only if unset. Then append
   `"WebFetch(domain:eventsapi.dolthub.com)"` to `permissions.deny` in
   `~/.claude/settings.json` via `jq`, creating the array if absent, idempotently.
   **Sandbox interaction — decide and document:** writing `~/.dolt/config_global.json`
   is sandbox-blocked. Either the script's invocation carries
   `dangerouslyDisableSandbox: true` (state that on the published usage line), or
   the script detects the block, skips, and prints the single command to re-run
   with the sandbox off. Pick one and say which in the retro; do not leave it
   ambiguous for the caller.
3. **Run dir.** `RUN_DIR="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/claude/bead-bonanza/<run-id>"` — always
   the braced default, never a bare `$TMPDIR` (set on macOS, unset on most Linux
   hosts and containers, where a bare expansion yields the unwritable absolute
   path `/claude/...`). `mkdir -p`, `touch "$RUN_DIR/.ok"`, and
   `ln -sfn "$RUN_DIR" "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/claude/bead-bonanza/current"` — the `-n`
   is load-bearing, without it a second run creates the link *inside* the first
   run's directory.
4. **`SCRIPTS`.** Resolve this script's own directory to an absolute path
   without `readlink -f` (absent on older macOS): `cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd -P`.
5. **Push mechanics — measure, do not assert.** Report whether `.git/config` is
   writable, whether an upstream is configured, whether HEAD is the default
   branch (exit 1 if it is), and the remote name. These become ledger lines with
   a cited command instead of prose in SKILL.md.
6. **Environment.** `bd` + `bd where`; `jq`; `git status --porcelain` empty;
   `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL`; `.claude/settings.local.json` allow entries.
7. **CI detection.** Grep `.github/workflows/*.y*ml` for a `pull_request:`
   trigger, so SKILL.md's draft-PR question is asked only where it can pay off.
8. **Gate baseline.** Run the gate profile's commands on the untouched tree and
   record each verdict. Emit them in the stdout block so the dispatch plan's
   ledger can carry them. The bar for every bead becomes "no findings beyond the
   baseline", not "exit 0"; a gate with no recorded baseline is expected to exit 0.
   Guard this behind a flag if the profile's full suite is slow — a pre-flight
   that takes ten minutes will be skipped.

## Portability — bash 3.2 and BSD userland

macOS ships bash 3.2 and BSD coreutils. Hard constraints, each of which has a
counterpart already used elsewhere in this repo or in the RFCs:

- No associative arrays, no `mapfile`, no `${var^^}`, no `declare -A`.
- `stat -c '%Y %n'` is GNU-only; BSD needs `stat -f '%m %N'`. Probe once and set
  a function. (The orchestrator-recovery procedure's liveness one-liner has this
  bug today and will need the same wrapper.)
- `sed -i` needs `-i ''` on BSD — prefer a temp file and `mv`.
- No `grep -P`; use POSIX classes or `awk`.
- No `timeout(1)` on stock macOS.
- `readlink -f` unavailable; use the `cd`/`pwd -P` idiom.
- `md5sum` vs `md5` — avoid both if possible.

`--self-test` runs every probe against a scratch fixture and asserts the
portability wrappers agree with the platform, so the AGENTS.md targeted-test
entry for `plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/scripts/**` ("run the script's own
guards") has something to run. It must exit 0 on both platforms.

## SKILL.md reduction

Phase 0 becomes: load the two blocks; run the script; act on its exit code; ask
the draft-PR question only when `BB_PR_CI=yes`; note that Agent-tool
availability is checked separately because no script can see it. Target ~15
lines from 89.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/scripts/pre-flight-check.sh exists, is executable, and runs clean under 'bash -n'
- [ ] It emits an evalable RUN_DIR= and SCRIPTS= block on stdout and a human report on stderr
- [ ] It probes for dolt before invoking it, and is idempotent on the settings.json deny entry
- [ ] It creates the run dir using ${TMPDIR:-/tmp} and the 'current' symlink with 'ln -sfn'
- [ ] It reports .git/config writability, upstream presence and default-branch identity as measured facts
- [ ] It checks bd, bd where, jq, a clean working tree, CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL, and the settings.local.json allow entries
- [ ] It detects a pull_request CI trigger and captures a gate baseline
- [ ] Exit codes are 0 proceed / 1 blocking / 2 bad invocation, and the usage line is published in SKILL.md's script interface table
- [ ] --self-test exits 0 on Linux and on macOS, and the retro records the observed output of both runs
- [ ] The script uses no bash-4 features, no GNU-only stat/sed/grep/readlink invocations without a probed fallback
- [ ] SKILL.md Phase 0 is reduced to loading the two blocks, running the script, and the draft-PR question
- [ ] SKILL.md states that Agent-tool availability cannot be checked by the script and remains an orchestrator check
- [ ] The sandbox interaction for the dolt config write is resolved one way and stated on the published usage line

title: check-skills.sh: threshold skill bodies on bytes derived from the 5,000-token re-injection cap, not on line count
description:
`scripts/check-skills.sh` warns when a skill body exceeds **500 lines**:

```python
    body = text.split('---', 2)[2]
    n = len(body.split('\n'))
    if n > 500: warn(p, f"body is {n} lines (guidance: under 500)")
```
(`scripts/check-skills.sh:117-118`)

Lines are the wrong unit, and that is why this gate has been firing for weeks
while telling nobody anything useful. The real constraint is the **5,000-token
skill re-injection cap** after compaction, which is a size in tokens, not a
count of newlines.

Measured on `plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/SKILL.md` — 869 lines, 45,114 body
chars, mean line length 51.9:

| Unit | Value | Bearing on the real constraint |
|---|---|---|
| lines | 869 | none — an artefact of the 80-column wrap convention |
| body bytes | ~45,100 | proportional to the tokens the cap counts |
| body tokens | ~11,500 | this is what the 5,000-token cap actually limits |

At 52 chars/line the warning fires at ~26 KB, while the *same content*
rewrapped at 200 chars reads as 230 lines and passes silently at the same
size. So the gate can be satisfied by rewrapping, which changes nothing about
whether the skill survives compaction. Conversely the 80-column convention is
good for diffs and review and should be kept — it is not the problem.

Consequence today: `scripts/check-skills.sh --strict` exits 1 with
`0 error(s), 1 warning(s)` on a clean tree, `bead-bonanza` the sole finding.
That red is carried as a hand-written exception in `AGENTS.md`'s
environmental-failure ledger and is re-copied into every bead-bonanza dispatch
prompt.

**This is a recurrence, not a new finding.** RFC-0004's Resolution deferred
"record the gate profile's baseline verdict" to bead `agent-plugins-1a9`
(theme `gate-baseline`) explicitly blocked on this units question: "the
standard states the body budget in CHARACTERS while `check-skills.sh` measures
LINES." That bead no longer exists in the database and never reached
`.beads/issues.jsonl` on any branch, so the deferral was lost — see the
sibling bead that re-files it. The blocking question now has an answer.


## Retro — implementation

### Findings
- The bead's Design step 4 asks which skills newly trip the threshold. One does: `plugin/skills/spec/SKILL.md` at 21,419 body bytes (~5,354 tokens) — 319 lines, so it passed the line gate silently while being over the real cap. The gate baseline therefore moves from 1 warning to 2, and the second one is a genuine new finding about a skill nobody was watching. No bead owns trimming it.
- The Design's measured figures (45,114 body chars) were counted as `len(str)`; the implementation counts `len(str.encode('utf-8'))`, so bead-bonanza reports 45,317. Not a contradiction, but the bead's numbers do not reproduce exactly against the shipped gate.

### What I tried that did not work
- Nothing abandoned. First reading was the implemented one.

### What I decided silently
- Byte count is of the UTF-8 encoding, not of the Python `str`. The two differ by ~300 bytes on bead-bonanza because of em dashes and arrows. UTF-8 is the right unit: the cap counts what is on the wire, and it errs high, which is the safe direction.
- The threshold is a named module constant `BODY_BYTE_MAX` rather than an inline literal, so the number and its derivation live in one place and the warning string cannot drift from the test.
- The reported token figure is `bytes // 4` (integer division), inlined rather than a second constant — it is an order-of-magnitude aid in the message, not a measurement, and pretending to more precision would invite treating it as one.

### Observed pre-fix failure
    scripts/check-skills.sh --strict
      WARN  plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/SKILL.md: body is 859 lines (guidance: under 500)
      --- 0 error(s), 1 warning(s) ---
      RESULT: FAIL
The unit is the defect: the same body rewrapped at 200 columns reads as ~230 lines and passes, at identical size.
design:
Change the threshold to bytes of body, derived from the re-injection cap.

1. Replace the line count with a byte count of the same `body` string. Threshold
   at **20,000 bytes** (~5,000 tokens at the ~4 bytes/token rule of thumb that
   the cap's own documentation implies for English prose + markdown).
2. Reword the warning so it states the consequence rather than the measurement:
   `body is N bytes (~T tokens); above ~20000 the tail is truncated from
   context after a compaction`.
3. Keep the 80-column convention. Do NOT add a line-length check to compensate;
   this bead narrows the gate to the constraint that exists.
4. Check the other shipped skills against the new threshold before landing, and
   report any that newly trip it — this changes which skills the gate flags, and
   a silent new red elsewhere is the failure mode to avoid:
   `for f in plugin/skills/*/SKILL.md .claude/skills/*/SKILL.md; do ...`
5. Once `bead-bonanza`'s SKILL.md is under the threshold (tracked by the
   measurement-gate bead), the "KNOWN RED, pre-existing" entry in `AGENTS.md`'s
   environmental-failure ledger is retired. Do NOT retire it in this bead — the
   skill is still over at this point and the entry is still true.

Rationale for bytes over a real tokenizer: the gate must run with no
dependencies in CI and on a contributor's laptop. Bytes are a stable proxy and
err in the safe direction for markdown.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] check-skills.sh measures body size in bytes, not lines
- [ ] The threshold is 20,000 bytes and the source states which cap it is derived from
- [ ] The warning message names the consequence (post-compaction truncation), not just the number
- [ ] Every other skill under plugin/skills/ and .claude/skills/ was checked against the new threshold and any newly-flagged skill is named in the retro
- [ ] The 80-column convention is unchanged and no line-length check was added
- [ ] The AGENTS.md 'KNOWN RED' ledger entry is left in place (it is still true at this point)

title: SKILL.md: add a post-compaction re-read instruction above the 5,000-token truncation point
description:
`plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/SKILL.md` is 45,983 bytes / 869 lines. Claude Code
re-injects an invoked skill's body after compaction **capped at 5,000 tokens
per skill, truncating from the START of the file**
(`code.claude.com/docs/en/context-window`). Measured:

```
$ head -c 20000 plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/SKILL.md | wc -l
406            # line 406 == "### Choose a dispatch mode per bucket"
```

Everything after line 406 is absent from a compacted orchestrator's context,
including the three rules whose loss is most expensive:

- `SKILL.md:624-627` — "**Read that file at dispatch** and fill in every
  `{PLACEHOLDER}` before sending. Do not paraphrase a template from memory"
- `SKILL.md:616-618` — the retro anchor "is non-negotiable"
- `SKILL.md:833-837` — the three published script interfaces, published
  precisely because the scripts are declared "executed, not read"

`CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE=80` is set in this cloud environment
(verified in-session: `echo $CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE` -> `80`), so
compaction fires whether or not the orchestrator plans for it.

In run `1786121603-ri` the three beads dispatched after the run's context loss
— `9kb.5`, `9kb.6`, `9kb.7` — are exactly the three that closed with no
progress ledger and no retro anchor, because their briefs were hand-written.
The rule forbidding hand-written briefs had been truncated away.

This bead is the cheap half of the fix and ships on its own, ahead of the
restructuring: a paragraph placed where truncation cannot reach it, telling a
compacted orchestrator that it has lost the procedure and must re-read it.
The restructuring that removes the need for this paragraph is tracked
separately; the paragraph should stay afterwards regardless, because a file
that fits today can grow again.


## Retro — implementation

**Findings:** None. The bead's Design section supplied exact wording and insertion point. No friction encountered.

**What you tried that did not work:** N/A.

**What you decided silently:** N/A.

**Pre-fix failures:** Not a defect bead.
design:
Insert immediately after the opening two paragraphs of the skill body (after
the "Read `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md` once at the start" paragraph, before the
"**This skill is language-agnostic.**" paragraph), so it sits inside the first
~1,500 bytes and cannot be truncated:

> **After any compaction, before dispatching anything:** re-read this file
> from Phase 3 onward and re-read `references/recovery.md`. A compacted
> session re-injects only this file's first ~5,000 tokens, so the per-bead
> ceremony, the published script interfaces and the rule against paraphrasing
> a dispatch template are NOT in your context even though you have "read the
> skill". Then `ls "$RUN_DIR"` and re-run the queue query, to re-derive run
> state from the durable source rather than from a summary of it.

Wording constraints: keep it under 10 lines at 80 columns; name the three
things that go missing rather than saying "the rest of the file", because the
reader's problem is that it does not know what it is missing.

Do NOT also add a warning at the truncated end of the file — a warning that is
not present cannot be made louder, which is the whole point of this finding.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The paragraph exists in SKILL.md and `head -c 1500 SKILL.md` contains it in full
- [ ] It names all three truncated rules: the ceremony, the script interfaces, the anti-paraphrase rule
- [ ] It instructs re-reading from Phase 3 onward AND references/recovery.md
- [ ] It instructs re-deriving run state from $RUN_DIR and the queue query rather than from a summary
- [ ] No warning was added at the end of the file
- [ ] scripts/check-skills.sh reports no new findings against the recorded baseline

title: Harden bead-bonanza: fit the procedure in context, make the sprint plan durable, and close the retro loop
description:
bead-bonanza v1.3 has been exercised over three multi-wave runs (the largest: 23 beads across 10 waves; the most instructive: run 1786121603-ri, 12 beads, killed mid-batch and dead for 2h16m). The spine held every time — the per-bead ceremony landed 23 consecutive beads with zero loss across a container restart. The failures cluster in four places, and three self-authored RFCs plus eight hardening beads have measured them.

1. **The operative procedure does not fit in context.** SKILL.md is 45,983 bytes / 869 lines. A skill body is re-injected after compaction capped at 5,000 tokens, truncating from the start: head -c 20000 SKILL.md lands at line 406. Everything past it — the whole close ceremony, the anti-paraphrase rule, the retro-anchor rule, the script interfaces, Phase 3, Phase 4 and Operating principles — is absent from a compacted orchestrator exactly when it is needed most. CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE=80 is set in this cloud environment, so compaction is not opt-in. Three beads in run 1786121603-ri (9kb.5, 9kb.6, 9kb.7) lost their progress ledger and retro anchor to hand-written briefs, and they are exactly the three dispatched after that run's context loss.

2. **The sprint plan is not durable and not enumerated.** dispatch.md carries the mandate, the wave table and the environmental ledger, but its location survives only in the orchestrator's transcript (the run id is generated and unguessable; grep for it across the tracker, git history and the worktree returns zero). It is written once and never amended, and it identifies scope by filter rather than by an enumerated bead list — so a filter re-evaluated at recovery returns a different queue than the one the run committed to.

3. **The close ceremony and its verification have gaps.** No step verifies a bead's artifacts exist before recording it closed. The tracker ledger is a projection of a shared database, so a subagent's close commit absorbs the orchestrator's concurrent tracker writes regardless of pathspec discipline. bb-close-bead.sh writes no commit trailers, and the amend that adds them invalidates the sha the progress ledger recorded one step later.

4. **The retro channel is inverted.** Measured across run 1786121603-ri: 10 .retro.md files produced 137,146 bytes and yielded 1 cited finding; 34 retro:-prefixed bd comments produced 16,411 bytes and yielded 12 of 12 traceable findings. 8.4x the cost for 1/12 the yield. Separately the prescribed harvest command returns zero on a completed run by two independent causes, so an aggregated retro over an empty set produces a confident, clean-looking artifact.

This epic collects the work to close all four, plus the dispatch-correctness defects found alongside them (worktree-parallel was skipped for a reason that measurement refuted; C4 blast-radius metadata that grooming already produces is never read).

Framing that shaped the scope: a bead-bonanza run is a **sprint**. dispatch.md is the sprint plan; the readiness gate is the boundary of the sprint backlog; the retro is what makes the next sprint better. Ceremony that grooming already owns does not belong inside the run.

## Success Criteria

- [ ] `head -c 20000 plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/SKILL.md | tail -20` shows content after the Reference-files table, so the close ceremony, the script interfaces and the anti-paraphrase rule survive a compaction
- [ ] `scripts/check-skills.sh --strict` exits 0 on a clean tree and the KNOWN RED ledger exception is retired
- [ ] An orchestrator that wakes with no memory of a run can find it from `bd show <epic-id>` or the `current` symlink, read an enumerated plan with its amendments, classify every bead, and resume — without git archaeology
- [ ] No bead can be recorded closed without its retro anchor and a `committed` event, and the recorded sha is reachable from HEAD
- [ ] A findings harvest over a drained run returns a non-zero count matching an independent count, and a sprint retro synthesizes it into grooming, spec, plan and skill findings
- [ ] Phase 2 no longer exists; the Definition of Ready requires decisions closed, and the readiness gate is the run's only decision point
- [ ] Bucketing reads `c4_changes`/`c4_impacts` where the repo declares them
- [ ] Every worktree-parallel skip condition cites the command that established it
- [ ] `bead-bonanza` is at version 1.4 and the plugin version is bumped
design:
Six lanes. The ordering constraint that matters: the content-reducing work (Lane A) must land before the restructure is measured, because it accounts for 9,472 bytes of the ~26,000-byte gap and changes what there is to restructure.

- **Lane 0 — unblock.** The post-compaction re-read paragraph (ships standalone, ~10 lines) and the check-skills.sh unit fix.
- **Lane A — shrink.** Extract Phase 0 mechanics into a pre-flight script; delete Phase 2 (after amending the Definition of Ready); make dispatch.md unconditional and enumerated; extract the explanatory prose to references/; then measure.
- **Lane B — dispatch correctness.** Bucket on C4 metadata; settle worktree-parallel by test; make the mixed-tier rule decidable; invert the TaskCreate default.
- **Lane C — recovery and durability.** Orchestrator-death procedure; per-bead acceptance check; self-describing run-directory backup; durable wake trigger; WIP resume path; trailer support.
- **Lane D — close-ceremony integrity.** Defer orchestrator tracker writes while a claim is held.
- **Lane E — retro.** Reshape the per-bead retro; fix the harvest; add a sprint-level retro at Phase 4.

**SKILL.md is a shared surface.** Roughly fifteen of these beads edit it. The dependency graph encodes only semantic ordering; the rest is a shared-surface batch for the orchestrator to pack, not a fifteen-deep chain.

Sources: rfcs/inbox/bead-bonanza/*.md (three RFCs, 15 proposals), the eight beads labelled bead-bonanza-hardening, and a review session on 2026-08-10 whose four framing decisions are recorded in the child beads that implement them.

title: Establish whether worktree-parallel is safe: isolation:worktree branches from the default branch, not session HEAD
description:
`bead-bonanza`'s worktree-parallel mode assumes each subagent branches from the
run's working branch and that the orchestrator merges back into it. The
platform default is different.

Claude Code docs (`code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents`, frontmatter): setting
`isolation: worktree` gives the subagent "an isolated copy of the repository
**branched by default from your default branch rather than the parent
session's `HEAD`**". And `code.claude.com/docs/en/worktrees`: `"head"`: branch
from your current local `HEAD` ... **Use this when isolating subagents that
need to operate on in-progress work.**

So with the default `worktree.baseRef: "fresh"`, every worktree subagent
branches from `origin/main`. Consequences for a bead-bonanza run:

- Every merge back carries the delta between `main` and the working branch.
- **Any bead built on an earlier bead's commit in the same run silently loses
  that foundation.** Run 1786121603-ri would have been badly hit: 9kb.2-9kb.9
  all build on 9kb.1's model, and the wave plan explicitly sequenced them.

Neither `SKILL.md`'s dispatch-mode section nor the "Worktree parallel notes" in
`references/subagent-prompts.md` mentions `worktree.baseRef` at all.

This is a prerequisite for using worktree-parallel at all. The sibling bead
corrects the false claim that the mode is impossible; this one establishes
whether it is SAFE.


## Retro — implementation

**Findings** (also filed as `retro:` comments on this bead)

1. Conclusions 3 and 4 combine into a merge hazard this bead did not have a
   mandate to fix. All worktree agents share ONE database (conclusion 3), so
   the mandated `bd export > .beads/issues.jsonl` (conclusion 4) makes every
   worktree branch commit a near-identical FULL export of the same shared
   tracker. With no merge driver configured for that file (CLAUDE.md), two or
   more worktree branches in a wave will conflict textually on
   `.beads/issues.jsonl` at merge time — every time, by construction. The
   orchestrator should expect it and resolve by re-exporting on the merged
   tree, the same way a regen step resolves a fixture conflict. This belongs
   with the skip conditions owned by `agent-plugins-92q.9`, not here.

**What I tried that did not work** — nothing failed. No probes were re-run;
the measurements were handed over intact.

**What I decided silently**

- Took the optional pre-flight probe. `pre-flight-check.sh` now reads
  `.worktree.baseRef` from the user-scope settings file (the jq plumbing was
  already there for the telemetry deny) and reports it as an **advisory** line
  plus `BB_WORKTREE_BASEREF`, never a blocker — most runs never dispatch a
  worktree wave, and blocking them on a global setting they do not use would
  be wrong. Verified: self-test PASS (26 checks), live run emits
  `worktree.baseRef: head (advisory)` and `BB_WORKTREE_BASEREF='head'`.
- Cited the fact in SKILL.md through `BB_WORKTREE_BASEREF` rather than by
  naming the settings file and key, so Phase 0's "do not re-assert from memory
  what the script just measured" rule holds and the bullet stays 5 lines.
  Net SKILL.md growth: 43,621 -> 43,986 bytes.
- Structured the reference section as a two-row measured table plus a copy-
  pasteable verification instruction for the first worktree subagent, so the
  orchestrator can paste rather than compose it under load.
- Left Phase 2.5's "Skip this mode if..." list untouched per the handover;
  `agent-plugins-92q.9` owns it.

**Observed results** (measured by the orchestrator; quoted, not re-run)

Session HEAD `0ccc092` on `claude/bead-bonanza-improvements-j6jxjv`, 8 commits
ahead of default branch `main` at `5390f1d`. Two read-only `isolation:
"worktree"` probes. Discriminator: `scripts/pre-flight-check.sh` and the string
`After any compaction` in bead-bonanza's SKILL.md exist only on the branch.

Probe 1 — no `worktree` key in the user settings file:

    git rev-parse --short HEAD                -> 5390f1d   (DEFAULT BRANCH)
    git merge-base --is-ancestor 0ccc092 HEAD -> exit 1    (HEAD not an ancestor)
    git rev-list --count 5390f1d..HEAD        -> 0
    test -e .../scripts/pre-flight-check.sh   -> exit 1    (absent)
    wc -l .beads/issues.jsonl                 -> 105       (main checkout: 128)
    git rev-parse --git-common-dir            -> /home/user/agent-plugins/.git
    ls -d .beads/embeddeddolt                 -> No such file or directory
    bd where -> /home/user/agent-plugins/.beads
                database: /home/user/agent-plugins/.beads/embeddeddolt
    bd worktree info -> Main repo: /home/user/agent-plugins
                        Beads: local (no redirect)
    bd list                                   -> 63 issues

Probe 2 — after setting baseRef to head in user-scope settings:

    git rev-parse --short HEAD                -> 0ccc092   (SESSION HEAD)
    git merge-base --is-ancestor 0ccc092 HEAD -> exit 0
    git rev-list --count 5390f1d..HEAD        -> 8
    test -e .../scripts/pre-flight-check.sh   -> exit 0    (present)
    grep -c "After any compaction" .../SKILL.md -> 1
    wc -l .beads/issues.jsonl                 -> 128       (current)
    ls -d .beads/embeddeddolt                 -> No such file or directory
    bd where -> /home/user/agent-plugins/.beads (main checkout)

Acceptance outcome **(a)**: worktree-parallel is SAFE, conditional on
`baseRef: "head"` plus the per-wave ancestor check. The setting takes effect
immediately — probe 2 ran minutes after the write, in the same session.
Conclusion 3 independently reproduces `agent-plugins-t09` in this repository.

**Limits, stated not papered over**

- Project-root `.claude/settings.json` was NOT tested as a location for the
  key. Only user scope is verified; the docs say so rather than implying the
  project file works.
- This repository has no `.worktreeinclude` (`ls` -> No such file or
  directory), so gitignored-file copying was observed only in its default
  form: `.beads/embeddeddolt/` absent from both worktrees — which turned out
  not to matter, because of conclusion 3.
design:
**Test before trusting either setting.** The docs describe the behaviour; this
run has never exercised it.

1. Dispatch two throwaway worktree subagents from a branch that is ahead of the
   default branch. Have each report `git merge-base --is-ancestor <working-branch-head> HEAD`
   and `git log --oneline -3` from inside its worktree. Confirm whether they
   branched from the default branch or from session HEAD.
2. Repeat with `worktree.baseRef: "head"` configured. Confirm the worktree
   carries the working branch's commits.
3. Establish where the setting belongs. Project-root `.claude/settings.json` is
   NOT read in a multi-root session (verified: `/home/user/.claude` does not
   exist), but user-scope `~/.claude/settings.json` IS honoured here — Phase 0
   already writes a telemetry deny to it. If `baseRef` must be set per-session,
   Phase 0 is the place, and that is a skill change.
4. Also verify the interaction with `.worktreeinclude`: gitignored files are not
   copied into a Claude-created worktree by default, which matters for anything
   the run needs that git does not track.

**Acceptance:** either (a) worktree-parallel is documented as safe with a
stated `baseRef` setting and a verification step in the dispatch template, or
(b) it is documented as unsafe for runs whose beads build on each other, with
the specific reason. Do not enable the mode in `SKILL.md` until one of those
is established.

Depends on the outcome, not the text, of the ledger-correction bead — they can
proceed in parallel but the mode should not be enabled until both land.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Two throwaway worktree subagents were dispatched from a branch ahead of the default branch, and each reported 'git merge-base --is-ancestor <working-branch-head> HEAD' and 'git log --oneline -3' from inside its worktree
- [ ] The observed base ref (default branch vs session HEAD) is recorded with that output
- [ ] The same test was repeated with worktree.baseRef: head configured, and the result recorded
- [ ] Where the baseRef setting must live is established, including whether user-scope ~/.claude/settings.json is required in a multi-root session
- [ ] The interaction with .worktreeinclude for gitignored files the run needs is verified
- [ ] The outcome is one of: (a) worktree-parallel documented as safe with a stated baseRef setting and a dispatch-template verification step, or (b) documented as unsafe for runs whose beads build on each other, with the specific reason
- [ ] worktree-parallel is not enabled in SKILL.md by this bead

title: Correct the false 'worktree-parallel is unusable with bd' claim in both repos' ledgers
description:
Both repos' agent instructions assert that worktree-parallel dispatch is
impossible for any bead that runs `bd`. **The claim is false and was never
tested.** It has been costing real parallelism: every bead of run
1786121603-ri was dispatched sequentially on the strength of it.

Where it lives:
- `/home/user/strata/AGENTS.md:493` — "**Corollary: worktree-parallel dispatch
  is unusable for any bead that runs `bd`** ... `.beads/embeddeddolt/` is
  gitignored, so a `git worktree` does not receive the Dolt DB and `bd` either
  fails or silently re-inits an empty one inside it."
- `.bonanza/1786121603-ri/dispatch.md:7-9` — same claim, run-scoped.

**Measured refutation.** `bd` 1.1.2 resolves the shared database through git's
common directory. From a worktree created off this repo, with `BEADS_DIR`
UNSET:

```
$ bd where
/home/user/agent-plugins/.beads
  database: /home/user/agent-plugins/.beads/embeddeddolt
$ bd worktree info
  Main repo: /home/user/agent-plugins
$ bd list        → 36 issues (identical ID set to the main checkout)
```

No `embeddeddolt/` and no redirect file were created in the worktree. Writes
from the worktree land in the shared DB and are immediately visible from main.
`bd worktree --help` states the mechanism: "Worktrees automatically share the
same beads database as the main repository via git common directory discovery
— no manual redirect configuration needed."

**Concurrency is also safe** (tested in an isolated repo, not the live DB): 8
concurrent `bd create` → 8 successes; 4 concurrent `bd label add` on the SAME
issue → all four labels present, no lost update; 4 concurrent writes across
main + 3 worktrees → all landed; `bd export` afterwards byte-valid, 0
malformed lines. Embedded Dolt takes a process-level lock and serializes at
~2 writes/sec, which is irrelevant next to agent think-time.

The premise (`embeddeddolt/` is gitignored) is true. The inference drawn from
it does not follow, and nobody ran the command.


## Steps to Reproduce

The defect is a false claim in a durable instruction, so the repro is the
command the claim says will fail. From a git worktree created off this repo,
with `BEADS_DIR` unset:

```
$ bd where
/home/user/agent-plugins/.beads
  database: /home/user/agent-plugins/.beads/embeddeddolt
$ bd worktree info
  Main repo: /home/user/agent-plugins
$ bd list
36 issues            # identical ID set to the main checkout
$ ls .beads/
                     # no embeddeddolt/, no redirect file created
```

**Claimed** (strata `AGENTS.md:493`, and the run-scoped copy in
`.bonanza/1786121603-ri/dispatch.md:7-9`): "a git worktree does not receive the
Dolt DB and `bd` either fails or silently re-inits an empty one inside it."

**Actual:** `bd` resolves the main checkout's `.beads/` through git's common
directory. Writes from the worktree land in the shared DB and are immediately
visible from main. Concurrency tested separately in an isolated repo: 8
concurrent `bd create` → 8 successes; 4 concurrent `bd label add` on one issue
→ all four labels present; 4 concurrent writes across main + 3 worktrees → all
landed, `bd export` byte-valid with 0 malformed lines.
design:
**Replace the AGENTS.md bullet** with the corrected version, keeping it a trap
warning rather than deleting the history:

> - **Corollary: worktree-parallel dispatch IS available for beads that run
>   `bd`.** `.beads/embeddeddolt/` is gitignored, but `bd` never looks for a DB
>   inside the worktree — it resolves the main checkout's `.beads/` through
>   git's common directory (`bd worktree info` → "Main repo: ..."; `bd where`
>   in a worktree prints the main path). Reads and writes from a worktree hit
>   the one shared DB with no `BEADS_DIR` and no redirect file, and concurrent
>   writers are lock-serialized (8 concurrent `bd create` → 8 successes;
>   concurrent label writes to one issue all merged; no corruption). The real
>   constraints are git-side, not DB-side — see below.

**Then document the constraints that ARE real**, because they are sharper than
the imagined one and a naive worktree run would hit all three:

1. **A worktree's own `.beads/issues.jsonl` goes stale while `git status`
   reads clean.** Auto-export always writes the MAIN checkout's copy. Measured:
   DB 28 issues, main file 28 lines, worktree file 23 lines, and the worktree
   reported no changes. Any worktree agent MUST run `bd export >
   .beads/issues.jsonl` in its own directory before committing.
2. **Auto-export is best-effort and was observed to miss** — three creates sat
   unexported for 20+ seconds, flushing only on a later main-context write.
3. **`export.git-add: true` stages into the main index from writes issued
   elsewhere.** This is the case the `git commit -- <pathspec>` guard exists
   for; keep commits pathspec-scoped.

**Do NOT enable worktree-parallel dispatch as part of this bead.** Correcting
the claim and enabling the mode are separate: the sibling bead covers the
`worktree.baseRef` defect that must be resolved first.

Note the ledger convention this episode argues for: an entry asserting
something is IMPOSSIBLE should cite the command that proved it. Four such
claims in this session turned out to be untested inferences.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The strata AGENTS.md ledger entry no longer claims worktree-parallel is unusable for beads that run bd, and states the common-directory mechanism instead
- [ ] The corrected entry cites the commands that proved it (bd where, bd worktree info, bd list from a worktree) rather than asserting the conclusion
- [ ] The three real constraints are documented: the worktree's own issues.jsonl going stale while git status reads clean, best-effort auto-export, and export.git-add staging into the main index
- [ ] The entry is preserved as a trap warning rather than deleted, per the existing ledger convention
- [ ] worktree-parallel dispatch is NOT enabled by this bead
- [ ] The run-scoped copy of the claim in any committed dispatch plan is corrected or annotated

title: Reshape the per-bead retro: mechanical description dump, trigger list, and own the retro: comment channel
description:
Measured across run 1786121603-ri by tracing every quoted span >=40 chars in
`rfcs/inbox/feature-blueprint/rfc-0015-implementing-reference-integrity.md`
back to its source:

| Channel | Generated volume | Yield |
|---|---|---|
| 10 `.retro.md` files | 137,146 bytes (~34k output tokens) | 1 item, in *Considered and Not Proposed*. Zero proposals. |
| 34 `retro:` bd comments | 16,411 bytes (~4.1k output tokens) | 12 of 12 traceable Evidence quotes; 5 of 7 proposals |

**8.4x the cost for ~1/12 the findings.** `agent-plugins-9kb.6` — no retro
file at all, one 482-character comment — carries proposal P2. Conversely
`tix`, `ml9` and `j7f` wrote 38,205 bytes of retro files between them and are
cited zero times.

Three structural causes:

1. **The template asks for categories, not triggers.** `findings-capture.md`
   defines a trigger list (record WHEN you needed information the bead did not
   carry, WHEN the bead contradicted repo reality...), which filters.
   `references/subagent-prompts.md:82` asks for a category ("implicit decisions
   you made"), which enumerates. Implicit decisions are the largest bucket
   (32,892 bytes, 39% of retro prose) and produced zero RFC quotes on their own.

2. **The skill does not own the channel that works.** `grep -c
   "findings-capture\|retro:" references/subagent-prompts.md` returns **0**. The
   `retro:` comment instruction reached subagents only because the groomed
   `9kb.*` bead descriptions carried it themselves. `tix`, `ml9` and `j7f` were
   prerequisites outside that groomed plan, which is exactly why they produced
   files and no findings.

3. **The ceremony destroys the instruction.** `bb-close-bead.sh:58` runs `bd
   update --status closed --body-file <retro>`, and `--body-file` REPLACES the
   description. Agents hand-retype the description into the retro file and drop
   content. Verified on `agent-plugins-9kb.1`: the original description (from
   `git show f019922^:.beads/issues.jsonl`) ends with a `## Retro` section
   containing "one `bd comment` per finding, prefixed `retro:` — following the
   findings capture protocol in `rfcs/findings-capture.md`". The current
   description has a `## Retro` heading but no `findings-capture` and no
   `prefixed`. The collision is structural: the bead already has a `## Retro`
   section and the instruction says to append one with the same name.

Standing cost: 79% of description bytes in the committed `.beads/issues.jsonl`
are retro payload, rewritten and re-committed on every close.


## Retro — implementation

### Findings
- AC 8 ("measured retro output on the next run is materially smaller than the ~34k-token baseline") cannot be satisfied by the bead that changes the template — it is an observation about a later run. Closest available evidence, from this batch, which the orchestrator already dispatched under the new shape: 2 retro files totalling 8,552 bytes, ~4,276 bytes/bead against the baseline's 137,146/10 = 13,715 bytes/bead, a 3.2x reduction. That is a proxy, not the AC.
- The template's own prose tripped `check-skills.sh` rule 2: writing `` `bb-close-bead.sh` `` bare in backticks is read as a path that must resolve relative to the citing file, and it errored on both the plugin copy and its `.claude/skills` symlink. The file's existing convention is `{SCRIPTS}/bb-close-bead.sh`, which the regex skips because of the brace. Nothing in the bead or the file says so.
- Step 3 of the same template still says "For any implicit decision you must make, record what you chose (and why) — you'll put it in the retro", which is the broad category framing that the bead's cause 1 argues against. The bead scopes the change to step 5, so it is left as-is and the two now differ in width.

### What you tried that did not work
- Nothing abandoned on the design. The one reversal was mechanical: the first draft's bare backticked script name, replaced with the `{SCRIPTS}/`-prefixed form after the gate rejected it.

### What you decided silently
- The `retro:` comment obligation is stated inside finding item 1 rather than as its own bullet, so the instruction sits where the finding is written and cannot be read as an optional extra step.
- Added a clause naming WHY the comment channel matters ("what downstream retros and RFCs actually read; the file alone does not reach them"). The bead only required the obligation; without the reason an agent under time pressure treats it as duplication of the file it just wrote.
- Item 3 is given a worked contrast (helper name / guard-clause order vs. the approach the bead specified) rather than only the word "narrower" — the bead's measured complaint is that this bucket over-enumerates, and a boundary without an example does not move it.
- Kept the file's existing very-long-line paragraph style rather than wrapping at 80; wrapping only this step would make the diff read as a reflow.

### Observed pre-fix failure
Not a defect bead. The pre-change state is the measurement in the Description, reconfirmed here: `grep -c "findings-capture\|retro:" plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/references/subagent-prompts.md` returned `0` before the change and `1` after.
design:
Three changes to `references/subagent-prompts.md` step 5 (currently lines 78-85).

**1. Start the file mechanically, never by retyping.**

```
bd show {ID} --json | jq -r '.[0].description' > "{RUN_DIR}/{ID}.retro.md"
```

Verified working: `bd show agent-plugins-9kb.6 --json | jq -r '.[0].description'`
→ 2,254 bytes with the findings block intact. One agent already invented this
(`agent-plugins-9kb.8.show.txt` exists in the run dir) and then retyped the
description anyway because the prompt asked for it. Costs zero generated tokens
and is strictly more faithful.

**2. Use a distinct heading.** Append `## Retro — implementation`, not
`## Retro`, so it cannot collide with or displace a groomed bead's own
`## Retro` section.

**3. Replace the category list with a trigger list, and put the `retro:`
comment obligation INTO the template.** Write for a reader who already has the
diff, the commit, `bd show {ID}` and the gate output. Explicitly exclude the
approach narrative, diffstat, files-changed list, gate table and AC restatement
— 15,211 bytes of gate/diffstat material was never quoted anywhere, and
`git show --stat <sha>` already holds it.

Four items, in order:

1. **Findings** — one bullet per point of friction, EACH ALSO recorded as its
   own `bd comment` on {ID} prefixed `retro:`. Trigger list: you needed
   information the bead and its references did not carry; you had to settle
   something the bead or spec should have pinned; the bead contradicted repo
   reality; you could not satisfy an AC as declared; a sequencing surprise.
   1-3 sentences each, friction only, no root-causing. A clean run records none.
2. **What you tried that did not work** — the reading you took first and
   abandoned. The diff shows only the reading that survived. `9kb.7`'s
   abandoned `Registry` reading is the entire basis of RFC-0015's P4.
3. **What you decided silently** — only choices a diff-reader would not
   recognise AS choices. Narrower than today's "implicit decisions". Consumer
   is the Phase 4 audit table (`SKILL.md:635`).
4. **For a defect bead: the observed pre-fix failure**, quoted from actual
   output. If you could not reproduce it, say so and say what you substituted
   (`agent-plugins-j7f.retro.md:163-172` is the model).

Expected effect: ~34k generated tokens → ~4k, keeping every category that
produced a finding plus the two that are genuinely unrecoverable later.

Full analysis is in the retro-skill lane report; the RFC to file against the
skill can cite this bead.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The retro file is seeded mechanically from 'bd show {ID} --json | jq -r .[0].description' rather than retyped, and the template says so
- [ ] The appended heading is '## Retro — implementation', distinct from any '## Retro' section a groomed bead already carries
- [ ] The template asks for a trigger list, not a category list, with the four items in order: findings, what was tried and abandoned, what was decided silently, and the observed pre-fix failure for defect beads
- [ ] Each finding is required to be recorded as its own retro:-prefixed bd comment on the bead
- [ ] The approach narrative, diffstat, files-changed list, gate table and AC restatement are explicitly excluded
- [ ] The template states that a clean run records no findings
- [ ] references/subagent-prompts.md now mentions the retro: channel — 'grep -c "findings-capture\|retro:"' returns non-zero
- [ ] Measured retro output on the next run is materially smaller than the ~34k-token baseline, and the retro records the observed figure
