title: Resolve references into the index graph with both directions derived
description:
# agent-plugins-9kb.4 — Resolve references into the index graph with both directions derived

## Description

**Blueprint:** specs/features/reference-integrity/reference-integrity-blueprint.md — delta **RES**, section "References in [[module-document-core]] (added — resolved graph) — RES".
**FRD:** specs/features/reference-integrity/reference-integrity-frd.md.
**Delivery:** staged (stage 1 of 2); this feature's closure set is `bd list --label feature-spec-reference-integrity`.

Turn extracted references into a resolved graph and put it in the index.
Resolution is a lookup against slugs the corpus already holds, so the cost of
this work is the walk it rides on rather than a second pass; the graph it
produces is what makes a single-document check able to see the documents
pointing **at** it, and what the `refs` query reads.

This is the last item of stage 1. When it lands, `spec index` emits reference
edges over this repository's own corpus — no new check runs, no finding is
raised, and no exit status changes. That boundary is deliberate: it puts the
extraction and resolution rules, the ones that produce false positives, in
front of a reviewer before any of them can fail a build.

**Verification timing.** This item proves AC-SPECREF-001.3 (unit), -001.6
(integration), -002.2 (unit), -002.7 (unit) and -002.8 (unit), and owes those
citations. It also participates in AC-SPECREF-002.1 (proved by CHK) and
AC-SPECREF-003.1, -003.2 and -003.4 (proved by CMD), all outside this item's
dependency closure. Code work may proceed as soon as this item is ready;
verification of those four waits for CHK and CMD, and the final
Definition-of-Done item is the backstop.

AC-SPECREF-001.6 is verified at **integration** level against the existing
`index` subcommand, which already exists — it does not wait on CMD.

## Retro

Before closing this item, record retro findings on this issue —
one `bd comment` per finding, prefixed `retro:` — following the
findings capture protocol in `rfcs/findings-capture.md`. Friction
only: what happened plus the item or spec text that caused it (or
the gap where guidance was missing). No analysis, no RFCs — the
plan's final DoD item runs the aggregated retro.


## Design

Anchors: `cli/core/references`; `cli/core/corpus/corpus.go` (`Build`, the
`builder`, and the `Corpus` lookups); the emitted index `corpus.Write` produces
and `corpus.Open` serves — its `input_hash` already folds the active profile's
registration, so a profile that registers a new reference property invalidates
the warm index by construction.

- Resolve a reference's slug half against the slugs corpus members declare,
  compared **lowercased**, matching the case-insensitive slug uniqueness
  AC-SPEC-003.4 establishes (AC-SPECREF-002.8).
- WHEN a reference's slug matches a file the index recorded as an **exclusion**,
  or an entry recording a **parse failure**, record that outcome rather than
  "matches nothing", carrying the reason and the file's path
  (AC-SPECREF-002.7). The reader's next step differs, which is why the outcome
  differs.
- Resolve **only within the workspace** the run is against. A slug declared
  only in another repository's index is unresolved, per the FRD's stated
  boundary. The merged-graph case is a known follow-on, not a defect.
- Derive **inbound** references from the same collection the outbound ones are
  read from ([[adr-018]], AC-SPECREF-001.3), and do **not** store the reverse of
  an edge a second time.
- WHEN a reference resolves to no corpus member, record it in the index with its
  unresolved state, so `index` exits zero over a corpus whose links are broken
  (AC-SPECREF-001.6). Indexing never fails; reporting is the checker's job.
- Corpus extracts and resolves **during the walk that already reads each
  candidate's bytes**, so that no document is read twice.
- WHERE a corpus is served **warm**, Corpus reads the graph from the persisted
  index rather than parsing any document — which is what keeps the `refs` query
  and the inbound half of a single-document check inside the AC-SPEC-009.1 and
  AC-SPEC-009.2 budgets (AC-SPECREF-003.4).
- Corpus exposes lookups for **both directions** alongside the existing `Entry`
  and `Slug`, built once when the index is opened.
- Row order follows [[adr-018]]: sorted by path, then by position within the
  document. That satisfies AC-SPECREF-001.5's ordering and AC-SPEC-009.7's
  byte-identical output in one rule.


## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A reference's slug half resolves against corpus slugs compared lowercased (**proves AC-SPECREF-002.8**, unit).
- [ ] A reference carrying an anchor resolves on its slug portion alone, and no finding is raised about the anchor (**proves AC-SPECREF-002.2**, unit).
- [ ] A slug matching an excluded file or a parse-failure entry records that reason and the file's path, distinctly from "matches nothing" (**proves AC-SPECREF-002.7**, unit).
- [ ] Inbound references are derived for every document from the same collection, with no edge stored twice (**proves AC-SPECREF-001.3**, unit).
- [ ] A corpus containing unresolved references produces a complete index and `index` exits zero (**proves AC-SPECREF-001.6**, integration).
- [ ] A slug declared only outside the workspace resolves as unresolved.
- [ ] Extraction and resolution ride the existing corpus walk; no document is read twice.
- [ ] A warm corpus serves the graph from the persisted index without parsing any document.
- [ ] `Corpus` exposes inbound and outbound lookups built once at open, alongside `Entry` and `Slug`.
- [ ] The `references` rows are ordered by path then position, and the emitted index is byte-identical across repeated runs.
- [ ] All citations use the `AC:` marker adjacent to the test declaration per [[testing-standards]].
- [ ] [[module-document-core]] is folded: the References component records the resolution and graph half with its pinned semantics. Set `version` to 0.3 if not already set.

## Notes

tier: advanced — Reaches into the built Corpus build and warm-open paths: resolution, derived inbound edges with no edge stored twice, deterministic row ordering, and read-from-persisted-index on the warm path. Five ACs, and a determinism or warm-cache mistake is a silent wrong answer rather than a failure.

## Retro

### Approach

Resolution went into `cli/core/references/resolve.go` as `Resolve(refs, index)`,
a pure function of the reference rows and one `specmodel.SpecIndex`. The
References component owns the *rule* (the module blueprint says it "resolves
them against the corpus"); Corpus owns the *wiring*. The package still does not
import `core/specindex`, so the `agent-plugins-gz3` boundary test holds
unchanged — it forbids that package, and `specmodel.SpecIndex` is the shared
generated model, not that package.

Wiring in `cli/core/corpus`:

- `builder.classify` now threads the walk's `src` into `classifyDocument`, which
  calls `references.Extract` for every full member. Extraction therefore rides
  the read the walk already performed; nothing opens a file twice.
- `builder.finish` sorts the collected rows by path then `Position.Offset`,
  appends them to `index.References`, and calls `references.Resolve` once. It
  runs after the walk because resolution is a question about the *whole* corpus:
  the first file read may name the last.
- `Corpus` gained `outbound` and `inbound` — `map[string][]int` into the one
  `index.References` collection — built by `indexReferences()`, called from both
  `finish` (cold) and `fromIndex` (warm). No reverse edge is stored.
- `Corpus.OutboundReferences(path)` / `InboundReferences(path)` are the two
  public lookups, keyed by path and accepting the same path forms `Entry`,
  `Document` and `FindingsFor` accept.
- `inputHasher.sum` now folds each type's `ReferenceProperties`.

### Implicit decisions

1. **How a slug matches a non-member (AC-SPECREF-002.7): the file name without
   its extension, lowercased.** Neither the blueprint nor the FRD says how the
   match is made, and it has to be decided to satisfy the criterion at all. The
   index records nothing else about a non-member: an `IndexExclusion` carries
   path/reason/type and an entry with a `parse_error` carries no frontmatter —
   a parse failure by definition has no readable slug. The file *name* is the
   only handle both cases still have, and it is on the index, so the match is
   reproducible by anything reading the artifact rather than resting on
   knowledge only the build held. Recorded in `stem`'s doc comment and in the
   module blueprint: the consequence is one-directional (a non-member whose
   intended slug differs from its file name reports as an ordinary unresolved
   reference — the answer it got before the rule existed), and it lands the
   motivating case, the FRD's `work-order-template`.
2. **A member always wins over a file named like one**, and ties among
   non-members go to the first in path order, decided by comparison rather than
   by arrival order, so `Resolve` is order-independent with respect to how the
   index holds its collections. Tested directly
   (`TestResolutionDoesNotDependOnIndexOrder`).
3. **Only `ReferenceProperties` is folded into the input hash, not the whole
   registration**, even though the blueprint's RES anchors assert the hash
   "already folds the active profile's registration" — it did not; it folded
   only `SlugPattern` and `Numbered`. Reference properties decide the index's
   *content*, so omitting them would serve a stale index after a profile change.
   Typed references, pairings and the lifecycle reach nothing the index records
   and are read by checks against the live profile every invocation, so folding
   them would rebuild the corpus to produce identical bytes. Reasoned in the
   code comment and in the module blueprint. No `input-hash-version` bump: the
   new named field changes the digest for every corpus by itself, so every
   pre-existing index is invalidated automatically.
4. **Lookups keyed by path, not by slug.** `refs <slug>` (CMD) converts a slug
   to a path with the existing `Slug` lookup; keying by path keeps the two
   directions uniform and serves AC-SPECREF-002.9's single-document case
   directly.
5. **Names**: `OutboundReferences` / `InboundReferences` over `Outbound` /
   `Inbound` — the corpus has several lookups and a bare direction word says
   nothing about what is being looked up. Internal helpers: `targets`,
   `lookupKey`, `stem`, `orderedReferences`, `indexReferences`,
   `referencesAt`, `extractReferences`.
6. **File organisation**: resolution in its own `resolve.go` beside
   `references.go`; corpus-level graph tests in a new
   `cli/core/corpus/references_test.go` rather than appended to the 753-line
   `corpus_test.go`; one internal test file `corpus_internal_test.go` for the
   walk property.

### Verification

- AC-SPECREF-002.8 — `TestASlugResolvesComparedLowercased` (unit).
- AC-SPECREF-002.2 — `TestAnAnchoredReferenceResolvesOnItsSlugAlone` (unit),
  including the negative control that the unsplit text matches nothing.
- AC-SPECREF-002.7 — `TestASlugMatchingANonMemberRecordsThatReasonAndPath`
  (unit) and `TestAReferenceToANonMemberRecordsTheReasonAndPath` (corpus).
- AC-SPECREF-001.3 — `TestInboundReferencesAreDerivedFromTheSameCollection`
  (unit), which also asserts the "no edge stored twice" half by counting rows
  and comparing the outbound and inbound views of one edge.
- AC-SPECREF-001.6 — new snapshot case `index-unresolved-reference`
  (integration): `index` over a corpus with one broken link exits 0 and emits a
  complete index carrying the unresolved row. `cites` in `case.toml` is the
  citation form the testing standard requires of a data-driven case; the AC was
  also added to `TestSnapshotCases`'s own `AC:` line.
- AC-SPECREF-001.5 — `TestTheIndexCarriesEveryReferenceOrderedByPathThenPosition`,
  which also asserts two builds render byte-identically.
- Out-of-workspace boundary —
  `TestASlugDeclaredOnlyOutsideTheWorkspaceIsUnresolved`.
- No document read twice — `TestTheWalkOffersEachCandidateExactlyOnce`
  (internal, holds the read side directly) plus
  `TestAColdBuildWithAFullGraphMeetsTheSameBudget` (1000 documents, 3000
  references, same 1s budget as AC-SPEC-009.3's reference-free corpus).
- Warm path — `TestAWarmCorpusServesTheGraphFromThePersistedIndex` plants a
  reference row in the persisted index that no document on disk carries and
  asserts a warm open serves it; `TestTheGraphIsIdenticalWarmAndCold` holds
  warm/cold parity for both directions.

### Gate results

| Gate | Exit |
|---|---|
| `cd cli && gofmt -l .` | 0, printed nothing |
| `cd cli && go vet ./...` | 0 |
| `cd cli && go build ./...` | 0 |
| `cd cli && go test ./core/... ./profile/...` | 0 |
| `cd cli && go test -count=1 ./...` | 0 (13 packages) |
| `scripts/generate-schemas.sh` | not run — no `schemas/*.strata` changed |

### Regeneration diffstat

`scripts/regenerate-cli-snapshots.sh`: three existing cases changed
`input_hash` only (`index-default`, `index-out-custom`, `index-out-stdout`) —
the expected consequence of folding the reference registration into the hash;
their `references` collections stay `[]` because the shipped profile registers
no reference property until PREG. The new case
`index-unresolved-reference` gained its two expected artifacts. No other
snapshot moved.

### Surprises

- The blueprint's RES anchors state the input hash "already folds the active
  profile's registration". It did not. Making that true was a required part of
  this delta rather than a given; without it a profile that registered a new
  reference property would have been served the index built before it.
- `module-document-core.md` still carried "goldmark is not a dependency yet and
  arrives with the Markdown Structure component" in Key Decisions — stale since
  REX. Corrected in the same edit, per the repository's rule that specs read as
  statements of current behaviour.
- "No document is read twice" has no direct observable from outside the package;
  it is held by an internal test on the one walk plus a budget measurement.
  Recorded rather than papered over.

title: Extract body and frontmatter references with their spans
description:
# agent-plugins-9kb.3 — Extract body and frontmatter references with their spans

## Bead description (as given)

**Blueprint:** specs/features/reference-integrity/reference-integrity-blueprint.md
— delta **REX**, section "References in [[module-document-core]] (added —
extraction) — REX".
**FRD:** specs/features/reference-integrity/reference-integrity-frd.md.
**Delivery:** staged (stage 1 of 2); this feature's closure set is
`bd list --label feature-spec-reference-integrity`.

Build the extraction half of [[module-document-core]]'s declared References
component: find every reference a document makes, in the body and in the
frontmatter properties the active profile registers, and record each with the
position a reader must open to fix it.

The two rules that matter most here are both about what is **not** a reference —
a backticked illustration, and a frontmatter value describing the notation —
because a checker that reports either is a checker that gets ignored. Both were
observed in this repository's own corpus.

**Verification timing — frontmatter extraction against the real corpus.** This
item's frontmatter half cannot be exercised against this repository's own corpus
until PREG registers this framework's reference-bearing properties. Verify it
here with a test profile that registers properties of its own; code work does
not wait on PREG. The profile self-application gate and the final
Definition-of-Done item are the backstop.

**Verification timing — participating criteria.** This item proves
AC-SPECREF-001.1, -001.2, -001.4, -001.5 and -001.7 (all unit) and owes those
citations. It also participates in AC-SPECREF-002.2 (proved by RES) and
AC-SPECREF-002.3 (proved by CHK), both outside this item's dependency closure;
verification of those two waits for RES and CHK.

**Boundary — agent-plugins-gz3** (out of scope, and a hard constraint here):
index entries carry only the DocumentFrontmatter envelope, so per-type
properties are lost. **Nothing in this item may reach a reference-bearing value
through IndexEntry.frontmatter**, because that envelope carries neither the
per-type properties nor the spans AC-SPECREF-001.7 requires. Read from the
generic parsed frontmatter instead. This item neither depends on gz3 nor
resolves it.

### DESIGN (as given)

Anchors: new package cli/core/references (the package [[module-document-core]]'s
References component names); cli/core/frontmatter for the per-item span
widening; cli/core/span; goldmark added to cli/go.mod.

- Parse every [[…]] occurrence from a document's **body** — the content after
  the frontmatter block — and record each with its Span (AC-SPECREF-001.1).
- Do **not** record an occurrence inside a fenced code block or an inline code
  span (AC-SPECREF-001.2). Locate code regions with goldmark, the markdown
  parser [[adr-015]] already chose for this module, rather than a hand-rolled
  backtick scan.
- Treat everything before the first # as the reference's slug half and
  everything after it as the anchor, which is recorded and **not interpreted**
  (AC-SPECREF-002.2). No other separator is interpreted.
- Read reference-bearing frontmatter properties from the **generic parsed
  frontmatter** and never from the typed DocumentFrontmatter envelope
  (AC-SPECREF-001.7).
- WHERE a reference-bearing property holds a sequence, record one reference per
  item, each at that item's own span.
- Do **not** record a [[…]] occurring in a frontmatter value as a reference
  (AC-SPECREF-001.4).
- Read the contents of an **HTML comment block as body text**.
- Record each occurrence separately and preserve source order
  (AC-SPECREF-001.5).
- Express every position as a Span from the Spans component.

Package layout and function signatures are yours to choose.

### Acceptance criteria (as given)

- Every [[…]] in a document body is recorded with its Span (**proves
  AC-SPECREF-001.1**, unit).
- A reference inside a fenced code block or an inline code span is not recorded,
  with code regions located by goldmark rather than a backtick scan (**proves
  AC-SPECREF-001.2**, unit).
- A [[…]] in a frontmatter value is not recorded as a reference (**proves
  AC-SPECREF-001.4**, unit).
- Repeated references to the same target are recorded as separate occurrences in
  source order, each with its own span (**proves AC-SPECREF-001.5**, unit).
- Values of profile-registered reference-bearing frontmatter properties are
  recorded as outbound references, distinguishable from body references and
  naming the property they came from (**proves AC-SPECREF-001.7**, unit).
- A sequence-valued reference-bearing property yields one reference per item,
  each at that item's own span.
- A reference carrying # is split on the first #; the anchor is recorded and not
  interpreted; a [[slug|text]] form carries slug|text as its slug half.
- Text inside an HTML comment block is read as body text and contributes
  references.
- No reference-bearing value is reached through IndexEntry.frontmatter
  (agent-plugins-gz3 boundary).
- Every position is a Span from the Spans component.
- All citations use the AC: marker adjacent to the test declaration per
  [[testing-standards]].
- [[module-document-core]] is folded: the References component records its
  extraction half and the package that realizes it; the Frontmatter component
  records per-item spans for sequence values; the Change Guidance rule on the
  Spans scanner records the goldmark narrowing. Set version to 0.3 if not
  already set.

## Retro

### Approach

Three code changes plus one fold:

1. **`cli/core/frontmatter/frontmatter.go`** — `Property` gains `Items []Item`;
   `Item` is `{Position, Raw, Value}`. Populated by a new `sequenceItems`
   helper from the YAML sequence node, with `elementText` and `isScalar`
   beside it.
2. **`cli/core/references/references.go`** (new package) — `Options` and
   `Extract(Options) []specmodel.Reference`, with `frontmatterReferences`,
   `bodyReferences`, `bodyStart` and `reference` unexported.
3. **`cli/core/references/code.go`** — the goldmark code-region mask:
   `codeRegions(body) regions`, `regions.covers`, `linesOf`, `spanOf`.
4. Folds into `specs/architecture/module-document-core.md`: References
   half-built with seven pinned semantics, Frontmatter's sixth pinned
   semantic, the Change Guidance narrowing on the Spans-scanner rule, the
   components diagram and the "six of eight are built" prose. Version was
   already 0.3.

`goldmark v1.8.5` added to `cli/go.mod` (direct after `go mod tidy`).

### Implicit decisions, and why

- **`Extract` returns `[]specmodel.Reference` with `Resolution` left unset**,
  rather than an extraction-local type. The bead forbids redeclaring the MODEL
  types, and a `Reference` is complete except for what only the corpus can
  answer. The happy side effect is a fail-closed one: `ReferenceResolution`
  marshals to an error when its variant is nil, so an unresolved-in-the-code
  sense reference cannot reach the index. A test asserts exactly that.
- **`Path` is a parameter, not something the package derives.** The caller
  walking the corpus knows it; this package sees bytes.
- **`Options` takes `ReferenceProperties []string`, not a `corpus.Profile`.**
  `corpus` will import `references` in RES, so the reverse import would be a
  cycle; and what is reference-bearing is a per-type answer the caller has
  already looked up.
- **Frontmatter references are read from `frontmatter.Document`, passed in
  already parsed**, not re-parsed and not read from `IndexEntry.frontmatter`.
  `TestExtractionReadsNoIndexEntry` parses this package's own imports and fails
  if `core/specindex` appears, so the gz3 boundary is a gate rather than a
  review note.
- **Position semantics differ by origin, deliberately, and are documented on
  `Extract`:** a body reference's position covers the text *between* the
  brackets (the brackets are notation, and it makes `src[Position] == Text`);
  a frontmatter reference's position covers the value's own source text
  **including** YAML quoting, because that is the extent a rewrite replaces.
- **`Text` for a frontmatter reference is the parsed scalar, not the raw.**
  The model's comment says "the raw value of a reference-bearing frontmatter
  property", which is ambiguous; taking it literally would make
  `Text == "\"adr-012\""` and the slug half carry quotes, so every quoted
  frontmatter slug would report unresolved.
- **No trimming of a body reference's text.** `cross-document-references.md`:
  "only the slug SHALL appear between the brackets". `[[ adr-012 ]]` therefore
  carries a slug half with spaces and reports as unresolved, which is what the
  standard says it is. Trimming would be inventing a tolerance the standard
  does not grant.
- **A registered property whose value is not text contributes nothing** — a
  number, a mapping, a nested sequence. Whether such a value belongs in a
  reference-bearing property is a schema question, and the schema has the
  vocabulary to answer it.
- **A fence's info string is masked with its content.** ```` ```[[adr-004]] ````
  is code by the same argument as the lines inside the fence. Covered by its own
  test.
- **`regions.covers` tests overlap, not containment.** A reference that starts
  inside a code span and ends outside it is still something the author wrote
  inside backticks; reporting half of it is worse than reporting none.
- **`sequenceItems` locates a scalar element by its own token, not by the extent
  running to the next element.** Measured: for a block sequence the
  extent-to-next-token approach swallows the following element's `- `
  indicator (`"container-spec-cli"\n  - `), and trimming that back off by hand
  is where a span parser starts guessing. Composite elements have no single
  token, so they are the one case that does use the extent, with a trailing
  indicator removed — verified exact for `- key: value`.
- **`Items` is nil for a non-sequence and non-nil-empty for `[]`**, so a caller
  can tell "not a list" from "an empty list". Both cases have a test.
- **File split**: extraction in `references.go`, the code mask in `code.go`. The
  mask is the only part that knows markdown exists, and keeping it in one file
  makes the goldmark surface one file wide.
- **Package-level `var parser = goldmark.New().Parser()`** — CommonMark, no
  extensions, built once. The only question asked of it is where the code is.

### Gate results

All run as independent steps from `/home/user/agent-plugins`.

| Gate | Exit |
|---|---|
| `cd cli && gofmt -l .` | 0, printed nothing |
| `cd cli && go vet ./...` | 0 |
| `cd cli && go build ./...` | 0 |
| `cd cli && go test ./core/... ./profile/...` | 0 |
| `cd cli && go test ./...` (whole module) | 0 |

No `schemas/*.strata` changed, so `generate-schemas.sh` was not run and no
generated artifact moved. No regeneration diffstat for this bead.

### Anything surprising

- Two throwaway probe tests were written and deleted while implementing, to
  find out what goccy/go-yaml reports for a sequence element's token. Worth
  recording: `tok.Position.Offset` is a **one-based rune** offset (the same
  trap `absolute()` already documents for property keys), `Origin` for a block
  element is `" \"container-spec-cli\""` — leading space, no `- ` — and an
  empty flow sequence `[]` yields a `SequenceNode` with zero values rather than
  a non-sequence node.
- goldmark masked all five negative fixtures on the first run: an inline code
  span, a fenced block, an indented block, a double-backtick span, and a fence
  opened with a trailing space. That is the case for the blueprint's insistence
  on a parser — the trailing-space fence and the double-backtick span are both
  cases a naive scanner gets wrong.
- The References component record block still describes the whole designed
  component ("Wikilink discovery, heading-anchor resolution, and the inbound and
  outbound reference graph"); only the **Built** paragraph was changed to
  "Half built — extraction". The block describes what the component is, not what
  exists yet.
design:
Anchors: new package `cli/core/references` (the package
[[module-document-core]]'s References component names); `cli/core/frontmatter`
for the per-item span widening; `cli/core/span`; `goldmark` added to
`cli/go.mod`.

- Parse every `[[…]]` occurrence from a document's **body** — the content after
  the frontmatter block — and record each with its `Span` (AC-SPECREF-001.1).
- Do **not** record an occurrence inside a fenced code block or an inline code
  span (AC-SPECREF-001.2). Locate code regions with `goldmark`, the markdown
  parser [[adr-015]] already chose for this module, rather than a hand-rolled
  backtick scan: where a code span ends depends on matching backtick-run
  lengths, fence lengths and info strings, and a hand-rolled masker getting one
  of those wrong produces exactly the false positive this criterion exists to
  prevent. This brings `goldmark` into the module ahead of the Markdown
  Structure component that [[module-document-core]] currently says it arrives
  with; **nothing here builds that component, and no heading is read.**
- Treat everything before the first `#` as the reference's slug half and
  everything after it as the anchor, which is recorded and **not interpreted**
  (AC-SPECREF-002.2). No other separator is interpreted: `cross-document-
  references.md` forbids the display alias `[[slug|text]]`, so such a reference
  carries `slug|text` as its slug half and reports as unresolved rather than
  resolving quietly to something the standard prohibits.
- Read reference-bearing frontmatter properties from the **generic parsed
  frontmatter** — the property tree the Frontmatter component retains with raw
  text and positions — and never from the typed `DocumentFrontmatter` envelope
  (AC-SPECREF-001.7). See the gz3 boundary in the problem statement.
- WHERE a reference-bearing property holds a sequence, record one reference per
  item, each at that item's own span. This widens the Frontmatter component,
  whose `Property` today carries the span of a whole value: both
  AC-SPECREF-002.3's finding and AC-SPECREN-001.4's rewrite need the item, not
  the list.
- Do **not** record a `[[…]]` occurring in a frontmatter value as a reference
  (AC-SPECREF-001.4).
- Read the contents of an **HTML comment block as body text**.
  AC-SPECREF-001.2 excludes code alone, and `template-authoring-standards.md`
  requires a finished document's comment blocks to be deleted, so masking them
  would hide a reference in a document that should not carry the block at all.
- Record each occurrence separately and preserve source order, so a document
  referencing the same target twice carries two references with two spans
  (AC-SPECREF-001.5).
- Express every position as a `Span` from the Spans component. This is how
  [[module-document-core]]'s "build a new parsing capability on the Spans
  delimiter scanner" rule is satisfied under a delta that adds a parser:
  positions stay computed one way, and what `goldmark` supplies is the region
  mask the scanner cannot correctly derive.

Package layout and function signatures are yours to choose.

title: Widen the Profile extension point for reference and lifecycle registration
description:
# agent-plugins-9kb.2 — Widen the Profile extension point for reference and lifecycle registration

## Bead description (as given)

**Blueprint:** specs/features/reference-integrity/reference-integrity-blueprint.md
— delta **XPT**, section "Profile extension point in [[module-document-core]]
(modified) — XPT".
**FRD:** specs/features/reference-integrity/reference-integrity-frd.md.
**Delivery:** staged (stage 1 of 2); this feature's closure set is
`bd list --label feature-spec-reference-integrity`.

Every fact this feature checks is vocabulary, and Document Core must not hold
any of it. The Profile interface has carried three members since it was defined
— a union schema, a per-type slug and numbered table, and the convention
defaults — and its own documentation names reference properties and lifecycle
rules as the capabilities that would widen it. This is that widening, reviewed
on its own merits as [[module-spec-profile]]'s Change Guidance requires, and
framed so that **any** profile can express these rules rather than so that this
one can.

**Verification timing.** This item proves AC-SPECREF-004.1 (unit) and owes that
citation. It also participates in AC-SPECREF-002.5 (proved by LIFE) and
AC-SPECREF-004.3 (proved by CMD), both of which land on items outside this
item's dependency closure. Code work may proceed as soon as this item is ready;
verification of those two criteria waits for LIFE and CMD, and the final
Definition-of-Done item is the backstop.

**Coordination — agent-plugins-9jo** (out of scope, do not fix here): the
generated models embed this framework's DocumentType vocabulary, coupling the
framework-agnostic half to it. This item widens the extension point without
adding vocabulary to the host and extends the existing boundary test to the new
registered values; it neither worsens nor fixes 9jo.

### DESIGN (as given)

Anchors: cli/core/corpus/profile.go (Profile, DocumentTypeRules); the boundary
tests in cli/core/corpus; the generated specmodel.DocumentTypeRegistration and
specmodel.ProfileRegistration that MODEL extends.

- DocumentTypeRules carries, per document type, the names of its
  reference-bearing frontmatter properties, its typed reference properties as a
  mapping from property name to the type its target must declare, and its
  property pairings (AC-SPECREF-004.1).
- The Profile interface additionally supplies the **lifecycle registration**:
  the statuses at which a document is live, the statuses at which it is retired,
  and the name of the property in which a retired document names its
  replacement.
- Document Core contains **no** literal retired, superseded_by, or any
  registered property name. The existing boundary test — no non-test source in
  cli/core/corpus carries a document-type literal — extends to the values this
  delta registers, so the widening cannot become a place to smuggle vocabulary
  into the host.
- WHEN a profile is activated, the module validates its registration
  (AC-SPECREF-004.3). The defects are exactly three: a pairing or a typed
  reference naming a property the same type does not register as
  reference-bearing; a typed reference naming a type the profile does not
  define; and a lifecycle registration naming a status outside the profile's own
  vocabulary.
- IF the registration carries a defect, the module reports **every** one it
  finds, naming the offending key, rather than falling back to a default for
  that key.
- The validation **returns** its defects to the caller rather than rendering
  them, because a compiled-in registration has no file position of its own. The
  command surface supplies the position — that is CMD's job, not this item's.

Interface shape and function signatures are yours to choose; the members and the
validation semantics above are not.

### Acceptance criteria (as given)

- DocumentTypeRules carries per-type reference-bearing properties, typed
  reference properties (property → required target type), and pairings
  (**proves AC-SPECREF-004.1**, unit — cite per [[testing-standards]]).
- The Profile interface supplies the lifecycle registration: live statuses,
  retired statuses, and the successor property name.
- Activating a profile validates its registration and returns every defect
  found, each naming the offending key, with no fallback to a default for that
  key.
- All three defect classes are detected: an unregistered property named by a
  pairing or typed reference; a typed reference naming an undefined type; a
  lifecycle status outside the profile's vocabulary.
- Validation returns defects to the caller and renders nothing.
- The cli/core/corpus boundary test extends to the newly registered values, and
  no non-test source there carries retired, superseded_by, or any registered
  property name.
- [[module-document-core]] is folded: the Interface section records the widened
  Profile and DocumentTypeRules. Set version to 0.3 if not already set.
- [[module-spec-profile]] is folded: Interface records the widened Profile
  members. Set version to 0.3 if not already set.

## Retro

### Approach

Four changes, in order:

1. `cli/core/corpus/profile.go` — `DocumentTypeRules` gains
   `ReferenceProperties []string`, `TypedReferenceProperties map[string]string`
   and `Pairings []specmodel.PropertyPairing`; `Profile` gains
   `Lifecycle() LifecycleRules`; `LifecycleRules` is a new exported struct.
2. `cli/core/corpus/registration.go` (new) — `RegistrationDefect` and
   `ValidateRegistration(Profile) []RegistrationDefect`, plus two unexported
   helpers and a `sortedKeys` generic.
3. `cli/core/corpus/registration_test.go` (new) — the AC-SPECREF-004.1 citation
   and six tests over the three defect classes, the no-fallback rule, the
   renders-nothing rule, and determinism. `cli/core/corpus/profile_test.go` —
   the boundary test extended and renamed.
4. Folds: `module-document-core.md` Interface (already at version 0.3, left
   there), `module-spec-profile.md` Interface + Profile Registration table,
   version 0.2 → 0.3, `updated_at` → 2026-08-07.

`cli/profile` and the two `stubProfile` test doubles (`cli/core/corpus`,
`cli/cmd`) gained the `Lifecycle()` member. `cli/profile` returns the **zero**
registration — filling it is PREG (agent-plugins-9kb.5), explicitly out of
scope here.

### Implicit decisions, and why

- **The lifecycle registration carries the profile's whole status vocabulary
  (`LifecycleRules.Statuses`), not only the live and retired sets.** This is the
  one place where the shape I chose adds something the blueprint's three-member
  list does not literally name, and it is forced by an AC in the same bead: "a
  lifecycle status outside the profile's vocabulary" must be *detected*, and
  the host cannot detect it without being told what the vocabulary is. The union
  of live and retired is not the vocabulary — `schemas/profile.strata` says so
  explicitly ("a status in neither is one the lifecycle says nothing about,
  which is the right answer for a draft"). The alternative was deriving it from
  the union schema at `#/definitions/Status`, which bakes a schema-layout
  convention into the host and passes **vacuously** for any profile that keeps
  its status enum elsewhere — the exact failure AC-SPECREF-004.3 exists to
  prevent. Recorded in the `LifecycleRules.Statuses` doc comment and in
  module-document-core's Interface section so a later reader does not re-open it.
- **Statuses are `[]string`, not `[]specmodel.Status`.** The generated `Status`
  is this framework's six-value enum; putting it in the host would mean an
  adopting profile could not express a status of its own without failing
  `Status.Valid()`. That would worsen agent-plugins-9jo, which the bead forbids.
  Plain strings match the established pattern: `DocumentTypes()` is already keyed
  by `string`, not by `DocumentType`.
- **Pairings reuse `specmodel.PropertyPairing` rather than a corpus twin.** The
  interface already returns a generated type (`Conventions() specmodel.ConventionsConfig`),
  `PropertyPairing` is two property names and carries no framework vocabulary,
  and a parallel `corpus.PropertyPairing` would force PREG to convert between
  two identical shapes for nothing. Per adr-016 the Strata source is the single
  description of this surface.
- **One method, `Lifecycle()`, rather than three.** Three sibling methods would
  let a profile register retired statuses and no successor property with no
  single place to read "the lifecycle registration" as one value, and
  `ValidateRegistration` wants it as one value.
- **Validation lives in a new file, `registration.go`, not in `profile.go`.**
  `profile.go` is the declaration of the extension point; validation is behavior
  over it. Same package, so nothing about the surface changes.
- **`RegistrationDefect` has no `Error()` and no `String()`.** "Returns its
  defects rather than rendering them" is easier to hold if the type cannot
  render itself. `DocumentType` / `Key` / `Detail` is enough for CMD to compose
  a finding, and `Detail` deliberately does not repeat `Key`.
- **A profile registering lifecycle statuses but an empty vocabulary gets one
  defect per status**, rather than being waved through. An empty vocabulary
  containing nothing is the honest reading, and it keeps the check from passing
  vacuously on the registration most likely to be half-written. A profile
  registering *no* lifecycle at all has no defect — that is the zero value, and
  the checks that read it simply do not run.
- **Live/retired disjointness is NOT checked.** The blueprint says "the defects
  are exactly three"; a fourth class would be inventing scope.
- **The boundary test was renamed** `TestTheExtensionPointNamesNoConcreteDocumentType`
  → `TestTheExtensionPointNamesNoRegisteredVocabulary`, and now forbids three
  kinds of literal: document types, statuses, and reference-bearing property
  names. All three are read from the generated schema, never listed: statuses
  from `definitions.Status.enum`, reference-bearing properties as every property
  whose value is `$ref: Slug`, `items.$ref: Slug`, or a `oneOf` including it.
  That derivation yields exactly PREG's registered set (`consumers`,
  `contained_by`, `contracts_consumed`, `contracts_provided`, `frd`, `provider`,
  `sources`, `superseded_by`, `system`) with no transcription, so it will cover
  a property added to the schema before anything registers it.
- **`slug` is excluded from the derived property set**, with the reason stated
  in a named constant (`identityProperty`): it names the document declaring it
  rather than another document, so it is not reference-bearing, and
  `corpus.go`'s existing `const slugProperty = "slug"` is not a leak. Without
  the exclusion the extended boundary test fails on pre-existing, correct code.
- **The test asserts non-vacuity per kind**, not just overall: it fails if the
  schema yields zero document types, zero statuses, or zero reference properties.
- **`ValidateRegistration` is not called from `corpus` itself.** "WHEN a profile
  is activated" — activation happens in `cli/cmd`, and positioning the defect at
  `[profile].name` is CMD's job (agent-plugins-9kb.8). Exported and tested here.

### Gate results

All run as independent steps from `/home/user/agent-plugins`.

| Gate | Exit |
|---|---|
| `cd cli && gofmt -l .` | 0, printed nothing |
| `cd cli && go vet ./...` | 0 |
| `cd cli && go build ./...` | 0 |
| `cd cli && go test ./core/... ./profile/... ./cmd/...` | 0 |
| `cd cli && go test ./...` (whole module, for confidence) | 0 |

No `schemas/*.strata` changed, so `generate-schemas.sh` was not run and no
generated artifact moved. No regeneration diffstat for this bead.

### Anything surprising

- The generated models from MODEL (agent-plugins-9kb.1) already carry
  `ProfileRegistration.{live_statuses,retired_statuses,successor_property}` and
  `DocumentTypeRegistration.{reference_properties,typed_reference_properties,pairings}`.
  Nothing in this bead needed a schema change — the Go-side extension point was
  the only thing missing, which is exactly how the MODEL/XPT split was drawn.
- The `cli/cmd` package has a **second** `stubProfile` (in `config_test.go`)
  with the same shape as the one in `cli/core/corpus`. Widening the interface
  meant editing both. Neither the bead nor the blueprint mentions the second.
- The `slug` exclusion above is the only place where the extended boundary test
  needed a hand-written literal. It is worth watching: if a future envelope
  property is both slug-typed and legitimately known to the host, the same
  tension recurs.

title: Declare the reference, finding and registration models in Strata
description:
# agent-plugins-9kb.1 — Declare the reference, finding and registration models in Strata

**Blueprint:** specs/features/reference-integrity/reference-integrity-blueprint.md
— delta **MODEL**, section "Reference, finding and registration models in
Strata (added) — MODEL".
**FRD:** specs/features/reference-integrity/reference-integrity-frd.md.
**Delivery:** staged (stage 1 of 2); this feature's closure set is
`bd list --label feature-spec-reference-integrity`.

Three generated models have to grow before any Go code in this feature can be
written, and all three are declared in Strata and regenerated by one script per
[[adr-016]] — so they change at their source, in one block, rather than being
edited into the generated output. The index gains somewhere to put a reference,
the finding model gains variants for the defects this feature reports, and the
profile registration model gains the two lifecycle facts Document Core cannot
know without being told.

**Regeneration is the whole risk in this block.** This item was blocked on
agent-plugins-j7f: `scripts/generate-schemas.sh` had no strata version floor, and
run with an older binary it regenerated the bundled schema with every inherited
envelope property dropped while reporting success. Committing a destroyed schema
would silently disable the frontmatter checks CI depends on. j7f is closed
(69098fe) and the script now carries a post-generation sanity assertion.

**Verification timing.** This item proves no acceptance criterion on its own. It
participates in AC-SPECREF-001.1, -001.3, -001.5, -001.7, -003.3 and -004.1, each
of which is proved by a later item (REX, RES, XPT, CMD).

**Coordination — agent-plugins-a7m** (out of scope, not fixed here):
`generate-schemas.sh` wipes `cli/core/specmodel`, so a test placed beside the
generated models is destroyed on the next run. Tests for the reference model
therefore live in the consuming packages, as they already do.

**Coordination — agent-plugins-h6c** (out of scope, not fixed here): promoting
the index to a contract document with a formal versioning policy still waits on a
second, independently-built consumer. [[adr-018]] settles the reference shape
only, and the additive-under-1.0 rule this item obeys is what makes shipping
before then safe.

**Supersedes agent-plugins-dgn** — "model references as a separate edge
collection, not only object properties". [[adr-018]] takes exactly that decision
and this item implements it. dgn is left open; the epic's Definition-of-Done item
(agent-plugins-9kb.10) owns closing it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `schemas/index.strata` declares a `Reference` carrying path, text, slug,
      anchor, origin, position and resolution, and a top-level `references` list
      on `SpecIndex`.
- [x] `schemas/finding.strata` declares the four new `FindingDetail` variants
      (unresolved reference, retired target, incomplete pairing, reference-type
      mismatch).
- [x] `schemas/profile.strata` declares `live_statuses`, `retired_statuses` and
      `successor_property` on `ProfileRegistration`.
- [x] `schema_version` remains `"1.0"`, and the reason (additive under
      [[container-spec-cli]]'s rule) is recorded in the fold rather than left as
      an omission.
- [x] Generated artifacts are regenerated from the Strata sources and committed,
      and the generation check passes.
- [x] The regenerated schema retains every inherited envelope property —
      verified explicitly.
- [x] [[module-document-core]] is folded: the Corpus index-model vocabulary gains
      `Reference` and the `references` collection; the Findings vocabulary gains
      the new `FindingDetail` variants; Key Decisions gains [[adr-018]]; version
      set to 0.3.
- [x] No test is placed beside the generated models in `cli/core/specmodel`.

## Retro

### Approach taken

1. Read the bead, the blueprint's MODEL delta, the whole FRD, ADR-018, the three
   `.strata` sources and the fold target (`module-document-core.md`).
2. Probed the strata compiler on PATH with a scratch schema
   (`/tmp/.../scratchpad/emptystruct`) to confirm that a **field-less struct** is
   accepted as a union variant and generates clean Go and JSON Schema. It is —
   this is what made a discriminated `ReferenceOrigin` / `ReferenceResolution`
   possible rather than a flat enum plus a bag of optional siblings.
3. Wrote the three source deltas, regenerated, reviewed the whole regeneration
   diff, then made the minimal emitter-side updates the new required property
   forced.
4. Folded `module-document-core.md`.

### Model shape as landed

`schemas/index.strata` (all new declarations placed between `IndexExclusion` and
`SpecIndex`, keeping the file's existing dependency order):

- `ReferenceBodyOrigin` (empty) / `ReferenceFrontmatterOrigin { property }`, and
  `@discriminator("kind") union ReferenceOrigin { body, frontmatter-property }`.
- `ReferenceResolved { target_path }` / `ReferenceUnresolved` (empty) /
  `ReferenceNonMember { path, reason?, parse_error? }`, and
  `@discriminator("state") union ReferenceResolution { resolved, unresolved,
  non-member }`.
- `Reference { path, text, slug, anchor?, origin, position, resolution }`.
- `SpecIndex.references: [Reference]` — **required**, like `entries` and
  `exclusions`.

`schemas/finding.strata`: `FindingUnresolvedReference { slug, origin,
non_member? }`, `FindingRetiredTarget { slug, successor? }`,
`FindingIncompletePairing { property, counterpart, source_path, target_path }`,
`FindingReferenceType { property, slug, expected_type, actual_type }`, plus four
variants appended to the `FindingDetail` union with tags `unresolved-reference`,
`retired-target`, `incomplete-pairing`, `reference-type`.

`schemas/profile.strata`: `live_statuses: [Status]?`, `retired_statuses:
[Status]?`, `successor_property: String?` on `ProfileRegistration`, placed after
`placeholder_patterns` and before `conventions`.

### Implicit decisions and why

1. **`references` is required on `SpecIndex`, not optional.** `entries` and
   `exclusions` are required lists, and the model already carries a test
   (`TestNewEmitsEmptyCollectionsRatherThanNull`) whose whole point is that a
   collection consumers iterate must never be `null`. An optional `references`
   would have cost zero Go changes but reintroduced exactly the absent-vs-empty
   ambiguity that test exists to prevent. Cost: `specindex.New` now seeds
   `References: []specmodel.Reference{}`, `corpus.fromIndex` gained the matching
   nil-guard, one golden string and one shape assertion in `specindex_test.go`
   moved, and the three `index-*` snapshot manifests gained `"references": []`.
   Safe on the warm path: `openWarm` reports no errors and rebuilds on any decode
   failure, so a stale `specs.json` written before this change rebuilds rather
   than erroring.
2. **Origin and resolution are discriminated unions over (sometimes empty)
   structs, not enums with optional siblings.** The blueprint says a reference
   "carries" a property name only in the frontmatter case and an exclusion reason
   only in the non-member case; a union makes the unrepresentable states
   unrepresentable, and it matches the `FindingDetail` pattern already in the
   package. Verified empty structs compile and generate correctly before
   committing to it.
3. **Discriminator names: `"kind"` for `ReferenceOrigin`, `"state"` for
   `ReferenceResolution`.** `kind` matches the existing `FindingDetail`
   convention; `state` reads correctly for a resolution outcome and the two
   unions never share an object, so there is no collision.
4. **`Reference.slug` is `String`, not the constrained `Slug` alias.** A
   reference is hand-written and may name something that is not a well-formed
   slug; constraining it would make the very reference that must be reported
   unrepresentable in the index. Recorded in the property's doc comment.
5. **`FindingIncompletePairing` names both ends explicitly (`source_path` /
   `target_path`) rather than following `FindingDuplicateSlug`'s `other_path`.**
   The finding is emitted against *both* documents (AC-SPECREF-002.5) and the two
   copies must describe the relationship in the same direction; `other_path`
   would invert between them.
6. **`FindingReferenceType` carries `slug` in addition to the three facts the
   blueprint names.** AC-SPECREF-002.10's own example message names the target
   ("target 'adr-009' declares type 'adr'"), and the blueprint's stated intent is
   that each variant is self-contained without reopening a document. Additive, so
   no later item is constrained by it.
7. **New union variants appended at the end of `FindingDetail`** rather than
   interleaved by topic, keeping the change purely additive and the generated
   diff minimal.
8. **No wikilinks in `.strata` doc comments.** Existing doc comments name
   documents in prose ("See the Document Relationship Standard"), and the
   generated markdown ships in the plugin rather than the corpus, so a `[[…]]`
   there would be a reference nothing resolves. Followed the existing convention.
9. **Fold scope held to `module-document-core.md`.** The bead's `c4_docs` also
   names `module-spec-profile.md`, but the AC list names only Document Core, and
   the profile-interface widening (and therefore that document's fold) is
   agent-plugins-9kb.2 (XPT). ADR-018's Context sentence "today it carries
   `entries` and `exclusions`" was left alone: an ADR Context describes the state
   at decision time.

### Gates — each run independently, exit status reported

| Gate | Command | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| format | `cd cli && gofmt -l .` | 0, printed nothing |
| lint | `scripts/check-skills.sh` | 0 (`0 error(s), 1 warning(s)`, the known bead-bonanza length warning) |
| lint | `cd cli && go vet ./...` | 0 |
| build | `cd cli && go build ./...` | 0 |
| regen | `scripts/generate-schemas.sh` | 0 |
| custom | `scripts/generate-schemas.sh --check` | 0 — "generated artifacts are up to date" |
| test a | `scripts/check-skills.sh --strict` | 1 — **known-red baseline, unchanged**: `0 error(s), 1 warning(s)`, no new findings |
| test b | `scripts/sync-shared-references.sh --check` | 0 — all 11 vendored references current |
| test c | `scripts/sync-strata-docs.sh --check` | 0 — all 3 vendored strata docs match |
| test d | `cd cli && go test ./...` | 0 — every package ok, including the `cli/profile` self-application gate over this repository's own corpus |

Explicit AC-6 verification (envelope retention), run against the regenerated
bundle rather than trusting the script's own assertion:

```
Adr              required: description, slug, status, title, type, updated_at
FeatureBlueprint required: delivery, description, frd, slug, status, title, type, updated_at
ModuleBlueprint  required: description, kind, slug, status, title, type, updated_at, visibility
SpecIndex        required: schema_version, workspace, entries, exclusions, references
```

### Regeneration diffstat

```
 cli/core/corpus/cache.go                           |   3 +
 cli/core/schema/spec-model.schema.json             | 455 ++++++++++++-
 cli/core/specindex/specindex.go                    |   3 +-
 cli/core/specindex/specindex_test.go               |   4 +-
 cli/core/specmodel/specmodel.go                    | 730 ++++++++++++++++++++-
 cli/testdata/cases/index-default/expected/manifest.json    |   3 +-
 cli/testdata/cases/index-out-custom/expected/manifest.json |   3 +-
 cli/testdata/cases/index-out-stdout/expected/manifest.json |   3 +-
 plugin/skills/spec/references/generated/finding.md |  77 +++
 plugin/skills/spec/references/generated/index.md   | 132 ++++
 plugin/skills/spec/references/generated/profile.md |   3 +
 schemas/finding.strata                             | 124 ++++
 schemas/index.strata                               | 204 ++++++
 schemas/profile.strata                             |  33 +
 specs/architecture/module-document-core.md         |  85 ++-
```

Every deletion in the regenerated output was inspected and is benign: a trailing
comma appearing on `"unverified"` and `"exclusions"` because their JSON lists
grew, and gofmt re-aligning the six existing `isFindingDetailVariant()` marker
methods now that longer type names joined the block. Nothing else moved.

### Differences from the dispatch instructions

- The instructions describe this as a Strata-sources-only change. Making
  `references` a required property forced six small non-generated edits
  (constructor, warm-path nil guard, two test expectations, three snapshot
  manifests). Judged in-scope: without them the tree does not compile clean and
  `go test ./...` cannot pass. No test was added anywhere, and nothing was placed
  in `cli/core/specmodel`.

### Surprises

- The three `index-*` snapshot manifests' `input_hash` values changed even though
  no fixture document did. `Fingerprint` folds the active profile's schema into
  the hash, and the profile's schema is the regenerated bundle — so a model change
  correctly invalidates every warm index. Expected behaviour, but not obvious
  from the failure output, which reads as a corrupted fixture.
- `strata` accepts a field-less struct and emits `{"additionalProperties": false,
  "properties": {}}` plus a bare Go `struct{}` that satisfies the union
  interface. Nothing in the vendored language reference states this either way;
  it was established by probe.
design:
Strata sources under `schemas/`; regenerate with `scripts/generate-schemas.sh`,
which rebuilds `cli/core/specmodel/`, `cli/core/schema/` and the plugin
markdown.

**`index.strata`** gains a `Reference` struct and a top-level `references` list
on `SpecIndex`, per [[adr-018]]. A `Reference` carries:

- the `path` of the document the reference occurs in;
- the reference `text` as written, and the `slug` half of it;
- the `anchor` half, uninterpreted and absent where the reference names none
  (AC-SPECREF-002.2);
- the `origin`, distinguishing a reference parsed from the body from one held
  by a named frontmatter property and carrying that property name
  (AC-SPECREF-001.7);
- the `position`, as the existing `Span`;
- the `resolution` — resolved, naming the target's path; unresolved; or
  matched-a-non-member, carrying the exclusion reason or the parse failure
  (AC-SPECREF-002.7).

`schema_version` stays `"1.0"`. This is an addition alongside the existing
shape, which [[container-spec-cli]]'s additive rule permits at the same
version; the model and the emitted index change together in one change, which
is how [[module-document-core]]'s lockstep rule on the index model is satisfied
here. The satisfying act is the recorded no-bump, not an omission — say so in
the fold.

`references` is a list whose order the emitter fixes: [[adr-018]] pins sorting
rows by path and then by position within the document, which satisfies
AC-SPECREF-001.5's document-order requirement and AC-SPEC-009.7's
byte-identical output in one rule.

**`finding.strata`** gains `FindingDetail` variants, each carrying enough to
make its finding self-contained without reopening a document:

- an unresolved reference, carrying the slug, the origin, and — where the slug
  matched a file the index recorded as excluded or unparsable — that reason and
  the file's path (AC-SPECREF-002.1, -002.3, -002.7);
- a retired target, carrying the target's slug and its successor value where it
  declares one (AC-SPECREF-002.6);
- an incomplete pairing, carrying both property names and both documents
  (AC-SPECREF-002.5);
- a reference-type mismatch, carrying the property, the expected `type` and the
  `type` the target declares (AC-SPECREF-002.10).

**`profile.strata`** gains, on `ProfileRegistration`: `live_statuses` and
`retired_statuses`, each a list of `Status`, and `successor_property`, the name
of the property a retired document names its replacement in. These are
profile-level rather than per-type because `status` and `superseded_by` are
envelope properties. `DocumentTypeRegistration` already carries
`reference_properties`, `typed_reference_properties` and `pairings`; this
feature is their first consumer and adds nothing to them (AC-SPECREF-004.1).

Field names and Strata structuring are yours to choose; the carried facts above
are not.

- [ ] `schemas/finding.strata` declares the four new `FindingDetail` variants (unresolved reference, retired target, incomplete pairing, reference-type mismatch).
- [ ] `schemas/profile.strata` declares `live_statuses`, `retired_statuses` and `successor_property` on `ProfileRegistration`.
- [ ] `schema_version` remains `"1.0"`, and the reason (additive under [[container-spec-cli]]'s rule) is recorded in the fold rather than left as an omission.
- [ ] Generated artifacts are regenerated from the Strata sources and committed, and the generation check passes.
- [ ] The regenerated schema retains every inherited envelope property — verify explicitly, since this is the failure `agent-plugins-j7f` describes.
- [ ] [[module-document-core]] is folded: the Corpus index-model vocabulary gains `Reference` and the `references` collection; the Findings vocabulary gains the new `FindingDetail` variants; Key Decisions gains [[adr-018]]. Set `version` to 0.3 if not already set.
- [ ] No test is placed beside the generated models in `cli/core/specmodel` (`agent-plugins-a7m`).

The Reference and FindingDetail shapes are pinned by ADR-018 and the blueprint, so the invention is low — but blast radius overrides, and a wrong shape is expensive once seven items depend on it.

title: Spec Corpus Reference Integrity
description:
Build the References component of Document Core: parse every cross-document
reference from a spec corpus, record the resolved graph in the shared index,
and report the references that resolve to nothing.

**Feature blueprint:** specs/features/reference-integrity/reference-integrity-blueprint.md
**FRD:** specs/features/reference-integrity/reference-integrity-frd.md

**Delivery unit:** staged — two reviewable increments:

- **Stage 1 — the graph in the index:** MODEL, XPT, REX, RES, PREG.
  `spec index` emits reference edges over this repository's own corpus; no new
  check runs, no finding is raised, and no exit status changes. The stage
  boundary is deliberate: it puts the extraction and resolution rules — the
  ones that produce false positives — in front of a reviewer before any of
  them can fail a build.
- **Stage 2 — checks and query:** CHK, LIFE, CMD. The checks report, `refs`
  answers, and exit status becomes sensitive to references for the first time.

Stage membership is carried as a `stage-N` label on each child. The dependency
edges encode the ordering the blueprint's Sequencing Constraints state; they do
not additionally serialise every stage-1 item ahead of every stage-2 item,
since the stages are review increments rather than a hard build order.

This feature's closure set is `bd list --label feature-spec-reference-integrity`.

**Prerequisite:** agent-plugins-j7f (generate-schemas.sh has no strata version
floor) must be resolved before MODEL lands — MODEL regenerates all three Strata
sources, and committing a destroyed schema would silently disable the
frontmatter checks CI depends on. The edge is wired.

**Deliberately out of scope** (each deferred, not overlooked): anchor
resolution beyond splitting on the first `#` (frd-spec-anchor-references),
heading extraction (frd-spec-structure-conformance), suggesting or performing
a repair (frd-spec-slug-rename), references to non-spec files by relative
path, and cross-workspace resolution.

## Success Criteria

The epic is complete when its final child (verify the Definition of Done,
retire the blueprint, run the retro) closes. That item gates on: every delta
folded into its owning blueprint with the version bumps, every one of the 24
acceptance criteria cited at its declared level, the profile self-application
gate green at the severities these checks assign, and the subsumed issues
(agent-plugins-dgn, agent-plugins-3md) closed or re-scoped.

Orchestrator state lived only in context, and a /clear + resume restored the pre-clear half, so the stall went unnoticed for 2h16m. === LIVENESS DETECTION — CORRECTED 21:32Z (supersedes the rule in the earlier note) ===
Do NOT key liveness on bead status. Observed 21:32Z: agent-plugins-9kb.6 sat at status 'open' while a subagent was actively editing 12 files. Dispatch briefs have not been requiring 'bd update <id> --claim', so an in-flight bead can be indistinguishable from an untouched one in the tracker. CORRECT RULE — git is primary, tracker is corroboration:

  newest dirty-file mtime > ~30 min  -> orphaned work from a killed child. Recover it.
  no dirty files                     -> idle. Safe to dispatch the next bead.

title: [bug] PR #14 regressed the warm-index path ~1.8x by emitting UnmarshalJSON on every generated model
description:
Blocking CI on PR #15 (go test, ubuntu-latest), and not caused by that PR.

## Measured

Same machine, same test, back to back:
- 17822a0 (pre-#14): warm query p95 = 24.9 / 23.4 / 23.6 ms
- 08043d6 (post-#14): warm query p95 = 46.3 / 47.4 / 38.8 ms

That is ~1.8x. On the ubuntu CI runner the regression crosses the 50 ms budget of AC-SPEC-009.1: bursts of 82.2 -> 69.6 -> 52.5 ms, converging to a floor of ~52 ms. macOS and Windows are not enforced (referencePlatform), so only the ubuntu leg fails.

## Cause

6940ea8 (#14) regenerated cli/core/specmodel/specmodel.go with 35 hand-rolled UnmarshalJSON methods that did not exist before:

  grep -c 'func (v \*.*) UnmarshalJSON' cli/core/specmodel/specmodel.go
  17822a0: 0
  HEAD:    35

The file grew 1971 -> 3347 lines. Each of these decodes field by field through map[string]json.RawMessage instead of letting encoding/json decode the struct. corpus.Open unmarshals a 1000-entry SpecIndex on every warm query, so the cost lands directly on the path REQ-SPEC-009.1 budgets.

This was not intended. #14's own commit message says the generated artifacts were regenerated with strata pinned to 8997153 because 'HEAD adds unrelated UnmarshalJSON emission that belongs in its own change'. The emission landed anyway.

## Fix

Regenerate cli/core/specmodel with a strata that does not emit UnmarshalJSON, and re-measure. Needs the strata toolchain, which the session-start hook failed to install in the session that found this (clone failed, CLI unavailable), so it could not be done there. Relates to agent-plugins-j7f (no version floor in generate-schemas.sh) -- the same class of defect: the generated output depends on which strata happens to be on PATH, and nothing gates it.

## Note on the budget itself

Even pre-#14 the margin was not large (23-25 ms against 50 ms locally), and agent-plugins-7ek already owns the question of which platform REQ-SPEC-009 is stated against. Fixing this regression should restore headroom; it does not settle 7ek.
acceptance_criteria: cli/core/specmodel carries no generated UnmarshalJSON methods; warm query p95 returns to the pre-#14 range on the same hardware; go test (ubuntu-latest) passes on PR #15
notes:
CORRECTION AND CONFIRMATION (apples-to-apples).

The earlier 19.7 vs 2.8 ms figure compared the generated decoder against a HAND-WRITTEN shallow mirror that left frontmatter and parse_error as json.RawMessage, so it skipped nested decoding and understated the baseline. Redone properly: the SAME 295,086 bytes decoded into specmodel.SpecIndex at each commit, 20 iterations, same machine.

  17822a0 (0 UnmarshalJSON methods):  best 4.02 ms, worst 7.94 ms
  HEAD    (35 UnmarshalJSON methods): best 19.89 ms, worst 25.43 ms

~5x, delta ~16 ms. The warm query p95 moved 24 ms -> 42 ms, a delta of ~18 ms, so the decoder accounts for substantially all of the regression. Attribution confirmed; only the magnitude of the baseline was wrong (4.0 ms, not 2.8 ms).

Worth noting for whoever fixes this: decode is not the dominant cost of a warm query even now. At 17822a0 a warm query was ~24 ms of which only ~4 ms was decode; the rest is Fingerprint, which reads and hashes every candidate file. Removing the generated decoder returns the warm path to roughly its pre-#14 cost -- it does not create large headroom against the 50 ms budget, which is agent-plugins-7ek's question.

title: RFC-0012 P8: replace the C4 composition rosters with child back-pointers
description:
Adopted at triage of rfcs/inbox/spec/rfc-0012-document-relationship-vocabulary.md (P8) on 2026-08-06. Human approved both new back-pointers at triage.

## Problem
The composition rosters — containers on a system, components and modules on a
container, components on a module — are the last hand-maintained mirrors of an
edge the index derives. Three of the four C4 levels had no back-pointer to
derive a roster from, so removing a roster would have deleted the edge rather
than relocated it. Supplying the missing back-pointers removes that obstacle.

## Evidence (verified by triage 2026-08-06, matches the RFC exactly)
containers: 0 documents. system: 0 documents. components: present and EMPTY on
all three blueprint documents. modules: exactly one non-empty value corpus-wide
— container-spec-cli lists module-document-core and module-spec-profile.

## Change
1. schemas/frontmatter.strata:
   - ContainerBlueprint.system: Slug? — unchanged, already the back-pointer.
   - ComponentBlueprint.container: Slug? — NEW. Names the container OR module
     the component is composed into. Singular (adr-007: a component is
     promoted out of exactly one parent's roster). Optional for the same
     reason 'system' is — a parent with no blueprint of its own is a real
     state, and absence records it.
   - ModuleBlueprint.contained_by: [Slug]? — NEW. Names the containers, or
     modules, that compose this module. A list because a shared module is
     composed into more than one host — the fact adr-009 cites when it denies
     modules a context view and tells them to point at their host
     container(s) instead.
   - REMOVE SystemBlueprint.containers, ContainerBlueprint.components,
     ContainerBlueprint.modules, ModuleBlueprint.components.
   Then run scripts/generate-schemas.sh.
2. Corpus migration (the whole of it):
   - specs/architecture/module-document-core.md: delete 'components: []',
     add 'contained_by: ["container-spec-cli"]'
   - specs/architecture/module-spec-profile.md: same
   - specs/architecture/container-spec-cli.md: delete 'components: []' and
     the 'modules:' block
3. Templates — update frontmatter and any instruction-block prose naming a
   removed property, and bump each version:
   - system-blueprint-template.md (drop containers) 1.4 -> 1.5
   - container-blueprint-template.md (drop components, modules) 1.5 -> 1.6
   - module-blueprint-template.md (drop components, add contained_by) 0.7 -> 0.8
   - component-blueprint-template.md (add container) 1.5 -> 1.6
4. plugin/skills/spec/references/frontmatter-standards.md: reconcile the
   relationship-property listing with the vocabulary as it now stands. THIS
   bead owns this file's version bump: 0.1 -> 0.2, covering P3/P4/P5/P7/P8.
5. specs/features/reference-integrity/reference-integrity-frd.md: register
   'container' and 'contained_by' as reference-bearing in AC-SPECREF-004.2.
   Pair neither.

## What this does NOT change
adr-008's block-XOR-link invariant and adr-012's roster-heading convention
govern the parent's BODY, not its frontmatter. The roster SECTION and its
'### <Display Name>' headings are untouched, and a promoted component's
heading anchor keeps resolving.

## Acceptance
- generate-schemas.sh --check clean; sync-shared-references.sh --check clean
- validate-corpus.py passes; no roster property left in the vocabulary
close_reason: Landed in the RFC-0012 triage on 2026-08-06. See the Resolution in rfcs/retired/rfc-0012-document-relationship-vocabulary.md.

title: RFC-0012 P5: remove related from the document envelope
description:
Adopted at triage of rfcs/inbox/spec/rfc-0012-document-relationship-vocabulary.md (P5) on 2026-08-06.

## Problem
'related' is the property that most purely mirrors prose: every value in the
corpus is already cited in the document's body as a [[slug]], and no consumer
keys on it. Under the Document Relationship Standard it satisfies none of the
three justification tests.

## TRIAGE EXTENT FINDING — the real blast radius is 48 files, not 11
Enumerated on 2026-08-06 by matching '^related:' inside YAML frontmatter
across all *.md in the repo:
  - 12 documents under specs/
  - 15 RFCs (9 in rfcs/retired/, all carrying 'related: []' — lossless;
    6 in rfcs/inbox/, three with real values)
  - 13 templates under plugin/skills/*/references/ (all 'related: []')
  - 8 skill reference documents with real values
scripts/validate-corpus.py validates the RFC queue AND the skill reference
files against cli/core/schema/spec-model.schema.json, whose bundle sets
additionalProperties:false. So every one of these 48 files must migrate in
the same change or the corpus gate fails.

## TRIAGE SUFFICIENCY FINDING
The RFC's claim that every 'related' value is already cited in prose holds
for 47 of 48 files. The exception is specs/architecture/module-spec-profile.md,
which lists 'frd-spec-validation-cli' in 'related' and cites it NOWHERE in
its body. Add [[frd-spec-validation-cli]] to that document's ## References
section BEFORE removing the property, or the edge is lost rather than derived.
(module-document-core.md and spec-index-blueprint.md list adr-015/adr-016 in
'related' and cite them in the body but not under ## References — no action
needed; the index parses the whole body.)

## Change
1. schemas/frontmatter.strata: remove DocumentFrontmatter.related. Also fix
   the Adr and Guide struct doc-comments, which both say the type 'carries no
   relationship properties of its own beyond the envelope's related'.
2. Run scripts/generate-schemas.sh.
3. Remove the property from all 48 files. Do not hand-edit anything under
   references/shared/ — run scripts/sync-shared-references.sh after.
4. plugin/skills/spec/references/frontmatter-standards.md: remove 'related'
   from the relationship-property YAML block and the Contents summary line.
   No version bump here — P8 owns this file's bump.
5. Bump the frontmatter 'version' of each of the 8 skill reference documents
   whose own frontmatter loses the property: c4-guide, cross-document-
   references, document-readiness-checklist, ears-guide, template-authoring-
   standards, work-order-definition-of-ready, work-order-field-guide.
   (frontmatter-standards is in that set but its bump belongs to P8.)

## Acceptance
- no '^related:' in frontmatter anywhere in the repo
- generate-schemas.sh --check clean; sync-shared-references.sh --check clean
- validate-corpus.py passes
close_reason: Landed in the RFC-0012 triage on 2026-08-06. See the Resolution in rfcs/retired/rfc-0012-document-relationship-vocabulary.md.

## Problem
FeatureBlueprint.sources is typed [Slug] (required list) but its doc-comment

description:
Adopted at triage of rfcs/inbox/spec/rfc-0012-document-relationship-vocabulary.md (proposal P1) on 2026-08-06.

## Problem
