title: [bug] generate-schemas.sh silently destroys the schema when run with strata older than the inheritance fix
description:
# agent-plugins-j7f — [bug] generate-schemas.sh silently destroys the schema when run with strata older than the inheritance fix

## Full bead description

scripts/generate-schemas.sh has no version floor for strata. Run it with
strata-cli 0.7.0 as installed by .claude/hooks/session-start.sh and it
regenerates cli/core/schema/spec-model.schema.json with EVERY inherited
envelope property dropped:

```
"Adr": { "additionalProperties": false, "properties": {} }
```

All twelve document types lose title, description, slug, type, status,
updated_at and their required entries — the file goes from 2202 lines to
1326. The script reports success. Committing that would silently disable
frontmatter/missing-property and frontmatter/schema for every document type,
i.e. destroy the checks this repo's CI now depends on.

Root cause is upstream and already FIXED there: strata-lang/strata commit
8997153 'Fix: allowAdditionalProperties: false silently dropped struct
inheritance (#289)'. Our schemas use 'struct Adr: DocumentFrontmatter {}'
together with additionalProperties: false, which is exactly the combination
that regressed. The binary the session-start hook installs predates the fix;
building from the strata checkout at HEAD produces output byte-identical to
what is committed.

Discovered 2026-08-05 while adding a FindingDetail variant for agent-
plugins-5xo: the regeneration required for that change would have shipped
the destroyed schema had the diff not been reviewed. What saved it was
reading the diff, not any gate.

Fix options, roughly in order of value:

1. Version floor in generate-schemas.sh — refuse to run below the
first strata release containing 8997153, naming the commit.
2. A post-generation sanity assertion: every document-type definition
must carry a non-empty required list. Cheap, and catches any future
regression of this shape rather than this one version.
3. Pin the strata version the session-start hook installs.
4. Wire generate-schemas.sh --check into CI. The checks.yml comment
already explains why it is not there (needs a Rust toolchain);
option 2 removes most of the need.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Ensure the strata on PATH predates strata-lang/strata commit 8997153
("Fix: allowAdditionalProperties: false silently dropped struct
inheritance (#289)") — strata-cli 0.7.0, the version
.claude/hooks/session-start.sh installs, is such a build.
Check with strata --version.
2. From the repository root, run scripts/generate-schemas.sh.
3. Observe that the script reports success and exits zero.
4. Inspect the regenerated cli/core/schema/spec-model.schema.json.

**Expected:** the regenerated file is byte-identical to the committed one
(2202 lines), and every document-type definition retains its inherited
envelope properties (title, description, slug, type, status,
updated_at) and its required list. Building strata from a checkout at
HEAD and re-running produces exactly this.

**Actual:** the file is 1326 lines. All twelve document types lose every
inherited envelope property and their required entries, e.g.
"Adr": { "additionalProperties": false, "properties": {} }. The script
still reports success, so nothing signals the loss.

**Where it manifests:** scripts/generate-schemas.sh (no version floor) →
cli/core/schema/spec-model.schema.json → the Schema Registry component,
which silently stops enforcing frontmatter/missing-property and
frontmatter/schema for every document type.

### Notes / Decision

Prerequisite for the reference-integrity feature: work order agent-plugins-
9kb.1 (delta MODEL) regenerates all three Strata sources and is blocked on
this. Committing a schema regenerated by an older strata would silently
disable the frontmatter checks CI depends on.

**## DECISION (2026-08-07)**

All four options in the description were put to the user. Selected: 2 + 3.

1. Version floor naming 8997153 — NOT selected. Dominated by option 2: it
guards only the too-old case and would NOT have caught what actually
happened this session, since HEAD (ce18d66) is far above any such floor and
still produced wrong output. Version strings cannot discriminate here —
44c1955 (destroys the schema) and 840f9ba (correct) both report strata-cli
0.7.0.
2. Post-generation sanity assertion: every document-type definition must
carry a non-empty required list — SELECTED. This is the actual guard and
satisfies this bead's acceptance criterion verbatim. Version-independent,
so it catches this SHAPE of regression rather than one known-bad build.
3. Pin the strata the session-start hook installs — SELECTED, with an
adjustment. The user has since decided to adopt strata HEAD (agent-plugins-
tix, wired to block this bead). So "pin" does NOT mean pinning to 840f9ba.
It means making provisioning verifiably correct: the hook builds from the
checkout and stamps the built commit in ~/.cache/strata-cli/built-commit,
and a stale stamp must not be able to leave an older binary installed while
reporting success.
4. Wire generate-schemas.sh --check into CI — NOT selected. Needs a Rust
toolchain, the documented reason it is absent from checks.yml, and option 2
removes most of the need. CI-gate expansion is agent-plugins-9ko.

Ordering: agent-plugins-tix adopts HEAD and regenerates. This bead adds the
guard that makes a future bad regeneration fail loudly. Do not redo tix's
work here.

### Acceptance Criteria

generate-schemas.sh fails loudly rather than emitting a schema whose
document types have no properties, when run with a strata that drops struct
inheritance.

---

## Retro

### Approach taken

Implemented both selected options.

**Option 2 (primary guard).** Added a step ("2.5") to `scripts/generate-
schemas.sh`, right after the bundled JSON Schema is built and before it (or
any other output) is synced into the tree. It shells a small inline
`python3` script (no external deps — `json` + `sys` stdlib only, consistent
with `scripts/validate-corpus.py`'s existing use of python3 in this repo)
against the freshly generated `spec-model.schema.json`. The script:

1. Reads `definitions.DocumentType.enum` — the kebab-case list of document
   type values (`"adr"`, `"system-blueprint"`, …).
2. Converts each value to the PascalCase struct name convention this repo's
   schemas use (`"system-blueprint"` → `SystemBlueprint`) to get the list of
   document-type definitions to check.
3. Asserts each such definition exists in `definitions` and has a non-empty
   `required` array. Missing definitions and empty/missing `required` lists
   are both reported (all offenders at once, not just the first), and the
   script exits 1 with a message pointing at the upstream commit, the fact
   that `strata --version` can't discriminate a good build from a bad one,
   and where to check the actual provenance
   (`~/.cache/strata-cli/built-commit`).

**Option 3 (provisioning correctness).** Edited `.claude/hooks/session-
start.sh`'s strata-provisioning block. Added a `_fetch_unverified` flag,
set only when the `git fetch` + `git merge --ff-only` step against
upstream explicitly fails (not when the checkout is deliberately built
as-is because it's on a non-default branch or has uncommitted changes —
those are intentional, already self-explanatory in their own log lines,
and not a freshness gap). When the installed binary's stamp matches the
local HEAD *and* that fetch failed, the hook now emits a `WARNING:` line
explaining that the stamp match only proves the binary matches disk, not
that disk is caught up with upstream, instead of the plain "strata CLI
current" success line it printed before. This directly targets "a stale
stamp must not be able to leave an older binary installed while the hook
reports success" without pinning to an old commit and without needing an
actual network failure to reproduce (the branch is structurally new code —
verified with `bash -n` and by reading the modified control flow; the
failure-injection this guards against needs a real fetch failure against
github.com, which is out of scope to fabricate for this bead per the
explicit "Do NOT rebuild strata. Do NOT touch the /home/user/strata
checkout" instruction — this session's strata build is HEAD (ce18d66)
already, per the environmental facts).

### Observed pre-fix failure (RED before GREEN)

Could not cheaply reproduce a real strata-44c1955 build (needs a ~90s
cargo build against a different checkout per the environmental facts, and
the instructions explicitly say not to do this). Instead, synthesized the
exact corruption shape strata 44c1955 is documented to produce, applied it
to a copy of the real generated schema, and ran the assertion logic
against it directly:

```
python3 -c "
import json, copy
d = json.load(open('cli/core/schema/spec-model.schema.json'))
bad = copy.deepcopy(d)
bad['definitions']['Adr'] = {'additionalProperties': False, 'properties': {}}
json.dump(bad, open('/tmp/bad-schema.json','w'))
"
```

Running the assertion against `/tmp/bad-schema.json`:

```
error: generated schema has document type(s) with an empty or missing 'required' list: Adr
exit=1
```

**This is the rejection** — the guard fires and names the offending type,
exactly as the acceptance criterion requires ("fails loudly ... rather
than emitting a schema whose document types have no properties").

Running the same assertion against the real, correct, committed schema
(copied unmodified):

```
ok - all document types have non-empty required lists
exit=0
```

Then, separately, ran the actual `strata build` toolchain (this session's
HEAD build, ce18d66, which contains the upstream fix) via
`scripts/generate-schemas.sh` for real — the assertion ran silently (no
error) as part of that regeneration, and `scripts/generate-schemas.sh
--check` reported "generated artifacts are up to date" afterward, confirming
the guard doesn't produce false positives against a correct build.

### Implicit decisions and why

- **Where in the script:** placed the assertion immediately after step 2
  (the bundled JSON Schema is written to `$WORK/schema/spec-model.schema.json`)
  and before step 3 onward, so a corrupted bundle is caught before the specs-
  config overlay schema, the Go embed wrapper, the Go structs, or the
  Markdown reference are generated from (or alongside) it, and — critically —
  before `sync_dir` ever copies anything into the tracked tree. Nothing
  downstream of the corruption point runs before the check fires.
- **How to parse the schema:** a dependency-free inline `python3` heredoc
  (stdlib `json` only), matching the instruction to prefer a dependency-free
  approach and the existing precedent of `scripts/validate-corpus.py` using
  python3 in this repo (that script additionally needs `jsonschema`/`pyyaml`
  for its fuller job; this check needs neither).
- **How to identify "document type" definitions without hardcoding names:**
  derived the list from the generated schema's own `definitions.DocumentType`
  enum rather than a hardcoded name list or a second read of
  `schemas/vocabulary.strata`. This keeps the check honest against schema
  evolution (a renamed or newly added document type is picked up
  automatically) while staying self-contained to the one generated artifact
  the script already has in hand. It relies on this repo's existing naming
  convention (struct name = PascalCase of the enum's kebab-case value, e.g.
  `system-blueprint` → `SystemBlueprint`), which held for all 11 current
  document types when checked against `cli/core/schema/spec-model.schema.json`.
  Chose this over hardcoding partly because the enum itself is structurally
  immune to the bug being guarded against: it's a plain string enum with no
  struct inheritance, so it can't be corrupted the same way and remains a
  trustworthy anchor even in the exact scenario this check exists to catch.
- **Failure message phrasing:** named the upstream commit and PR
  (8997153, "Fix: allowAdditionalProperties: false silently dropped struct
  inheritance (#289)"), explained why `strata --version` can't be used to
  diagnose it, and pointed at `~/.cache/strata-cli/built-commit` as the
  actual provenance signal — mirroring the diagnostic path a future agent
  hitting this would need, based on how this bead itself was diagnosed.
- **Bead says "twelve document types"; only 11 struct definitions inherit
  `DocumentFrontmatter`** in the current schema (`Adr`, `Frd`, `Contract`,
  `Standards`, `SystemBlueprint`, `ContainerBlueprint`, `ModuleBlueprint`,
  `ComponentBlueprint`, `FeatureBlueprint`, `Rfc`, `Guide` — confirmed by
  grepping `schemas/frontmatter.strata` and cross-checking
  `definitions.DocumentType.enum`, which also has 11 entries). Did not
  investigate or correct the bead text's count — it's descriptive prose
  about a historical repro, not a checkable claim the fix depends on, and
  the guard's correctness was verified directly (11/11 checked, both
  reject and accept cases confirmed) rather than against that number.
- **Option 3 scope:** interpreted "a stale stamp must not be able to leave
  an older binary installed while the hook reports success" narrowly, as a
  reporting/visibility fix (turn a silent false-success message into an
  explicit `WARNING:` naming exactly why freshness is unverified) rather
  than a behavioral fix that forces a rebuild whenever fetch fails.
  Rebuilding on a failed fetch wouldn't install anything different (the
  local checkout genuinely hasn't moved), so it would only cost ~2 minutes
  for the same binary — the actual gap was that the hook's log claimed
  verified freshness ("strata CLI current") in a case where it had not
  verified anything. Fixing the message is what closes that gap; a real
  behavioral retry/backoff on fetch failure is a larger, separate change
  this bead's scope doesn't call for.

### Deviations from the instructions

None. Followed the workflow as given: claimed, read the bead and its
decision notes in full, red-before-green with a synthetic bad schema
(since reproducing the real historical failure was explicitly ruled too
expensive and off-limits), implemented both selected options, ran the
full regeneration and gate suite, filed a discovered-from bead for the
one unrelated red gate found along the way instead of fixing it here.

### Surprises

- `scripts/sync-strata-docs.sh --check` is red on this branch — 3 vendored
  docs (`strata-llm-reference.md`, `language-reference.md`,
  `compiler-options.md`) reported STALE — independently of anything in this
  bead. Confirmed via `git stash` (stash my two edits, rerun the check, same
  3-file failure; pop the stash back) that this predates this bead's work
  and reproduces from `f20abeb` (the `tix` commit) alone, so it's not caused
  by anything here. Filed **agent-plugins-be4** (P2, `discovered-from:
  agent-plugins-j7f`, explicitly noted as adjacent-not-blocking) rather than
  fixing it in this bead's diff, per the "stay strictly in scope" instruction.
- The assertion script needed no `additionalProperties` distinction between
  "genuinely no required fields by design" and "corrupted" — every one of
  this repo's 11 document types happens to require at least the envelope's
  `title`/`description`/`slug`/`type`/`status`/`updated_at`, so "non-empty
  required" cleanly separates good from corrupted for the whole set with no
  false positives to special-case. Worth knowing if a future document type
  is ever added with a legitimately empty `required` list — this guard
  would need widening then, not before.

### Gate results

- `bash -n scripts/generate-schemas.sh` — OK
- `bash -n .claude/hooks/session-start.sh` — OK
- `scripts/generate-schemas.sh` — regenerated cleanly (HEAD strata,
  ce18d66); assertion passed silently
- `scripts/generate-schemas.sh --check` — "generated artifacts are up to
  date"
- `cd cli && gofmt -l .` — no output (clean)
- `scripts/check-skills.sh` — 0 error(s), 1 warning(s), PASS
- `cd cli && go vet ./...` — clean
- `cd cli && go build ./...` — clean
- `scripts/check-skills.sh --strict` — FAIL, but matches the documented
  baseline exactly (0 error(s), 1 warning(s) — the pre-existing
  `bead-bonanza/SKILL.md` line-count warning). No new findings.
- `scripts/sync-shared-references.sh --check` — "all 11 vendored references
  are current"
- `scripts/sync-strata-docs.sh --check` — FAIL, pre-existing and unrelated
  (see Surprises above); filed agent-plugins-be4, not fixed here
- `cd cli && go test ./...` — all packages pass
acceptance_criteria: generate-schemas.sh fails loudly rather than emitting a schema whose document types have no properties, when run with a strata that drops struct inheritance
notes:
Prerequisite for the reference-integrity feature: work order agent-plugins-9kb.1 (delta MODEL) regenerates all three Strata sources and is blocked on this. Committing a schema regenerated by an older strata would silently disable the frontmatter checks CI depends on.
tier: standard — Root cause is fully diagnosed upstream (strata commit 8997153) and the bead enumerates four ranked fix options, so no diagnosis or design invention is left — but it is a guard whose silent failure is the destruction it prevents, and it must be proven by an actual regeneration run rather than by reading. Execution over invention, with a real cost of being wrong: standard, not light.
## DECISION (2026-08-07)

All four options in the description were put to the user. Selected: 2 + 3.

1. Version floor naming 8997153 — NOT selected. Dominated by option 2: it guards
   only the too-old case and would NOT have caught what actually happened this
   session, since HEAD (ce18d66) is far above any such floor and still produced
   wrong output. Version strings cannot discriminate here — 44c1955 (destroys the
   schema) and 840f9ba (correct) both report `strata-cli 0.7.0`.

2. Post-generation sanity assertion: every document-type definition must carry a
   non-empty `required` list — SELECTED. This is the actual guard and satisfies
   this bead's acceptance criterion verbatim. Version-independent, so it catches
   this SHAPE of regression rather than one known-bad build.

3. Pin the strata the session-start hook installs — SELECTED, with an adjustment.
   The user has since decided to adopt strata HEAD (agent-plugins-tix, wired to
   block this bead). So "pin" does NOT mean pinning to 840f9ba. It means making
   provisioning verifiably correct: the hook builds from the checkout and stamps
   the built commit in ~/.cache/strata-cli/built-commit, and a stale stamp must
   not be able to leave an older binary installed while reporting success.

4. Wire generate-schemas.sh --check into CI — NOT selected. Needs a Rust
   toolchain, the documented reason it is absent from checks.yml, and option 2
   removes most of the need. CI-gate expansion is agent-plugins-9ko.

Ordering: agent-plugins-tix adopts HEAD and regenerates. This bead adds the guard
that makes a future bad regeneration fail loudly. Do not redo tix's work here.

title: Run the profile's schema and slug-pattern checks over the built corpus
description:
# agent-plugins-9d1 — Run the profile's schema and slug-pattern checks over the built corpus

## DESCRIPTION

Discovered while building agent-plugins-bge.8 (#Corpus). ADJACENT, does NOT
block bge.8 — every one of that item's fourteen ACs is proven without it.

The gap: no item in the feature-spec-validation-cli closure owns the
orchestration that runs the Schema Registry over each corpus member. The
blueprint's #Corpus Anchors say the component 'consumes #Frontmatter, the
Schema Registry, #Findings' (specs/features/spec-index/spec-index-
blueprint.md, '#Corpus in module-document-core (added) — CO'), and
specs/architecture/module-document-core.md says the same. But:

- bge.8's acceptance criteria name only membership, index assembly,
  duplicate slugs, the slug query, paths and determinism. The only Finding it
  raises is slug/duplicate. cli/core/corpus therefore does not import
  cli/core/schemaregistry at all.
- bge.12 (command tree) states it 'holds no domain logic — a check that
  lived here would be unavailable to a future API or MCP wrapper', binding
  Change Guidance from specs/architecture/container-spec-cli.md. So the check
  loop cannot live in cli/cmd.
- bge.14 assumes it already exists: 'runs the corpus discovery and
  frontmatter checks over this repository's own corpus'.

Scope: a Check entry point in cli/core/corpus (or a sibling under cli/core)
that, for each member with parsed frontmatter, calls
schemaregistry.Registry.Validate with the member's declared type and
schemaregistry.CheckSlugPattern with the profile's per-type pattern, folds
the results into the same finding.Report the duplicate-slug findings already
flow through, and narrows to one file for a single-document check. This
needs the parsed *frontmatter.Document per member, which bge.8's Corpus
keeps internally and does not expose — expect to add an accessor.

Proves AC-SPEC-003.1, AC-SPEC-003.2 and AC-SPEC-003.5 at corpus level (the
Schema Registry item proved them at unit level against a fixture schema).

Blocks bge.12 and bge.14 in practice.

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

- [x] A Check entry point in cli/core runs, for every corpus member with
      parsed frontmatter, the Schema Registry's validation for the member's
      declared type and the profile's per-type slug-pattern check.
- [x] Its findings fold into the SAME finding.Report the duplicate-slug
      findings already flow through — one report, one ordering, not a second
      channel.
- [x] A single-document check narrows output to that file while still
      resolving against the full corpus (the AC-SPEC-001.2 behaviour Corpus
      already implements).
- [x] Corpus exposes whatever accessor this needs for the parsed
      *frontmatter.Document per member; the check loop does NOT re-parse.
- [x] cli/core/corpus gains no dependency on cli/profile — the profile is
      reached through the Profile extension point only.
- [x] Tests cover a corpus with a schema-invalid member, a slug-pattern
      violation, and a clean corpus, cited // AC: AC-SPEC-003.1,
      AC-SPEC-003.2, AC-SPEC-003.5 at corpus level per
      specs/standards/testing-standards.md.
- [x] Ordering stays deterministic with the new findings present.
- [x] cd cli && gofmt -l . && go vet ./... && go build ./... && go test ./...
      all clean.

## Retro

**Approach taken.** Added `Check()` and `CheckFor(path)` methods on
`*corpus.Corpus` in a new sibling file `cli/core/corpus/check.go`, alongside
a `Document(path)` accessor added to `corpus.go` itself. `Build` now also
retains, on the built `Corpus`: the active `Profile` (for `Schema()`), the
`map[string]DocumentTypeRules` it already computed once for exclusion
decisions, and a `map[string]*frontmatter.Document` of every member's parsed
frontmatter (populated in `classifyDocument` at the point the envelope
already decodes successfully, at zero extra parsing cost). `Check` compiles
a `schemaregistry.Registry` from the retained profile's schema lazily and
once (`sync.Once`), then for every member with frontmatter calls
`Registry.Validate` and, where the type's rules declare a pattern,
`schemaregistry.CheckSlugPattern`, adding every result into one
`finding.Report` that starts from the corpus's own precomputed
duplicate-slug findings. `CheckFor` reuses the identical path but skips
running the two document-level checks for every member except the one
requested, then narrows the final report to that member's path — so
duplicate-slug detection still sees the whole corpus (per AC-SPEC-001.2)
while schema/slug-pattern checking pays only for the named file.

**Implicit decisions and why.**

1. **Where the entry point lives.** The bead offered `cli/core/corpus` or a
   sibling under `cli/core`. I put it in `corpus` itself (as methods on
   `*Corpus`) rather than a new package, because
   `specs/architecture/module-document-core.md`'s Corpus component
   ("Built — cli/core/corpus... Entry, Slug, FindingsFor") is exactly the
   list of query methods `Check`/`CheckFor`/`Document` extend, and the
   bead's own metadata records `c4_changes: ["Corpus"]` — a change to that
   component, not a new one. A sibling package would have needed its own
   accessor surface into `Corpus` internals with no clearer boundary.
2. **Storing `Profile` on `Corpus`.** `Build` already receives
   `opts.Profile` and previously discarded it after extracting
   `DocumentTypes()`. Retaining the whole interface value (not just the
   schema bytes) keeps `Check` symmetric with `Build` — both read the
   Profile extension point and neither imports `cli/profile` — and avoids
   the caller having to pass the profile a second time to `Check`.
3. **Lazy, cached Schema Registry compilation.** Not asked for explicitly,
   but `schemaregistry.New` compiles a JSON Schema and `Corpus` is
   documented as "read many times" from one `Build`. Caching with
   `sync.Once` means a caller invoking `CheckFor` once per file in a
   directory walk (the shape bge.14's own description implies) does not
   recompile the union schema per file. This does NOT touch `Build`'s
   documented error contract — schema-compile failure surfaces from
   `Check`/`CheckFor`, not `Build`, so "Build fails only when it cannot
   start" stays true.
4. **`docs` map keyed identically to `byPath`.** Reused the already-computed
   "reported path" as the map key rather than introducing a second
   normalization scheme, so `Document(path)` calls the same `normalize`
   helper `Entry` and `FindingsFor` already use.
5. **Test fixture for AC-SPEC-003.2 at corpus level.** Mirrored
   `schemaregistry_test.go`'s `TestValidateChecksRawTextAgainstAFormatConstraint`
   fixture (an unquoted numeric-looking value under a `format`-constrained
   property) end-to-end through `Corpus.Check`, rather than inventing a
   different corpus-specific scenario — the point of testing this AC at
   corpus level is proving the *wiring* passes the same `*frontmatter.Document`
   through unmodified, not re-deriving the raw-text substitution semantics
   schemaregistry already unit-tests.
6. **Architecture doc update.** The bead's own ACs did not list a
   "recorded in the architecture blueprint" item (unlike bge.8's and
   bge.11's), but the metadata's `c4_docs` names
   `specs/architecture/module-document-core.md` and every closed sibling
   item in this delta updated that file as part of landing. Added two Rel
   edges (`corpus`→`schema`, `corpus`→`find`) to the C4 diagram and a
   paragraph under the Corpus "Built" section describing `Check`,
   `CheckFor`, and `Document`. Kept it minimal — no new component, no
   guarantee-list changes — since the bead's Design section did not ask for
   more.

**What differed from instructions.** Nothing structurally; the description's
approach was followed as given. One judgment call: the description says
"expect to add an accessor" (singular) for the parsed document — I added
`Document` as that accessor, and additionally stored `types` and `profile`
on `Corpus` (not explicitly named in the bead) because `Check` cannot be a
method on `*Corpus` without them, and the alternative (passing `Profile`
into `Check(profile)` as a parameter every call) seemed to needlessly
duplicate state `Build` already validated.

**Anything surprising.** The `$schema` draft declaration in a union schema
is load-bearing for whether `format` is enforced as an assertion at all
(`santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema/v6` treats format as annotation-only without an
explicit draft that requires it). My first attempt at the AC-SPEC-003.2
fixture used a schema with no `$schema` key and got a `type` constraint
violation instead of the intended `format` one — the coerced non-string
value's *type* failure masked whether raw-text substitution had even run.
Only comparing against `schemaregistry_test.go`'s exact fixture (which does
declare `"$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#"`) surfaced
this. Worth noting for anyone hand-writing a JSON Schema fixture for this
codebase: omit `$schema` and `format` silently stops being an assertion,
which fails in the "wrong" direction (looks like the raw-substitution logic
isn't running) rather than an obvious error.

No friction worth a `retro:` comment on the bead — the description's scope
and constraints held up exactly as written once the `$schema` fixture
detail above was worked out locally (not a defect in the description or
any spec, just a JSON Schema library detail encountered while writing a
fixture).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A Check entry point in `cli/core` runs, for every corpus member with
      parsed frontmatter, the Schema Registry's validation for the member's
      declared type and the profile's per-type slug-pattern check.
- [ ] Its findings fold into the SAME `finding.Report` the duplicate-slug
      findings already flow through — one report, one ordering, not a second
      channel.
- [ ] A single-document check narrows output to that file while still
      resolving against the full corpus (the AC-SPEC-001.2 behaviour Corpus
      already implements).
- [ ] Corpus exposes whatever accessor this needs for the parsed
      `*frontmatter.Document` per member; the check loop does NOT re-parse.
- [ ] `cli/core/corpus` gains no dependency on `cli/profile` — the profile is
      reached through the `Profile` extension point only.
- [ ] Tests cover a corpus with a schema-invalid member, a slug-pattern
      violation, and a clean corpus, cited `// AC: AC-SPEC-003.1`,
      `AC-SPEC-003.2`, `AC-SPEC-003.5` at corpus level per
      `specs/standards/testing-standards.md`.
- [ ] Ordering stays deterministic with the new findings present.
- [ ] `cd cli && gofmt -l . && go vet ./... && go build ./... && go test ./...`
      all clean.

metadata.tier_reason: Orchestration across three landed packages with the approach already spelled out in the description; no new design decisions, but it spans corpus/schemaregistry/finding and must preserve deterministic ordering.

title: Index entries carry only the DocumentFrontmatter envelope, so per-type frontmatter properties are lost
description:
BEARS ON agent-plugins-bge.8 (CO), which proves AC-SPEC-002.1, and on
agent-plugins-bge.6 (SR), whose design requires "a discriminated union over the
profile's document types" that the emitted schema does not currently contain.

`specmodel.IndexEntry.frontmatter` is `DocumentFrontmatter`, the shared
envelope. Per-type properties — `source_paths`, `components`,
`contracts_provided`, `updates` and so on — have no home in an entry. Measured
2026-08-04: 6 of 8 document types lose properties; `Contract`,
`ComponentBlueprint` and `ContainerBlueprint` lose 5 each. `Adr` loses none,
which is why AC-SPEC-002.1's own `adr-011` example fits and the gap survived
review.

## DECISION (2026-08-04)

Declare a real Strata `@discriminator("type")` union over the document types and
type index entries with it. To make that compile and validate, **open the
schema**: set `jsonSchema.allowAdditionalProperties: true` in
`schemas/strata.config.json`. — **SELECTED**

Options considered and not taken:

- *Envelope + untyped record of remaining properties.* Satisfies the AC without
  schema surgery, but leaves per-type properties untyped for every consumer.
- *Untyped record only.* Simplest, and would also resolve agent-plugins-9jo, but
  loses static typing even for the 10 shared properties.
- *Accept the loss and amend AC-SPEC-002.1.* Cheapest; leaves the index unable to
  answer questions about `contracts_provided` or `source_paths`, likely the
  queries later features most want.
- *Compose the union by hand over the existing per-type definitions.* Verified
  working against the committed schema on 4 cases, and needs no schema change —
  but it is a validation artifact only, so index entries would still need one of
  the shapes above for their Go type.

The opening is **temporary and tracked**: agent-plugins-006 closes the schema
again once the upstream defect is fixed, and
`rfcs/outbox/strata/rfc-agent-plugins-union-closed-shapes.md` reports it.

### Why the schema has to be opened

Two separate obstacles, both verified 2026-08-04 against `strata-cli 0.7.0`
built from `13494ba`:

1. `type` is declared on `DocumentFrontmatter` (`schemas/frontmatter.strata:60`)
   and inherited by all 13 per-type structs. Strata counts an inherited property
   as an override and rejects the union at compile time: "Variant 'Adr' may not
   override the discriminator property 'type'". So `type` must come off the base
   and be supplied by the discriminator instead.
2. With `type` removed the union compiles, but under
   `allowAdditionalProperties: false` each variant definition is emitted closed
   and without the discriminator, so a conforming document satisfies the `if` and
   fails the `then` with "Additional properties are not allowed ('type' was
   unexpected)". Every document of every type is rejected. Flipping only that
   flag to `true` makes the identical schema validate.

## Design

- `schemas/strata.config.json`: `jsonSchema.allowAdditionalProperties: true`.
- `schemas/frontmatter.strata`: remove `type: DocumentType` from
  `DocumentFrontmatter`; add `@discriminator("type") union Document { ... }` with
  one `@tag` per document type whose value is exactly the current `DocumentType`
  enum value for that type.
- `schemas/index.strata`: type `IndexEntry.frontmatter` as the `Document` union.
- `schemas/README.md`: its current text argues the `@discriminator("type")` union
  "is worse — it forbids the base from declaring `type` at all". Replace with the
  decision actually taken and a pointer to agent-plugins-006.
- Regenerate with `scripts/generate-schemas.sh` and commit all outputs.

`DocumentType` stays as an enum — it is still the vocabulary the profile's type
table and the tags draw on.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `schemas/frontmatter.strata` declares a `@discriminator("type")` union over
      every document type, and `DocumentFrontmatter` no longer declares `type`.
- [ ] Every variant's `@tag` equals that type's existing `DocumentType` value, so
      the wire format is unchanged for documents already on disk.
- [ ] `IndexEntry.frontmatter` is the union, and a `ComponentBlueprint` entry
      round-trips `source_paths` and `contracts_provided` (the properties the
      envelope dropped) — test cites AC-SPEC-002.1.
- [ ] One conforming document of EVERY document type validates against the union.
      This is the guard: the defect being worked around rejects all of them, so a
      test covering only `adr` would pass while the schema is broken.
- [ ] `scripts/generate-schemas.sh --check` passes and all regenerated artifacts
      are committed.
- [ ] `cd cli && go build ./... && go test ./...` pass; existing consumers of
      `DocumentFrontmatter.Type` are updated to read the union tag.
- [ ] `scripts/validate-corpus.py` passes (it validates the real corpus against
      this schema — it is the end-to-end check that the union works).
- [ ] `schemas/README.md` records the decision and points at agent-plugins-006.

## Retro

Before closing, record retro findings on this issue — one bd comment per
finding, prefixed `retro:` — per `rfcs/findings-capture.md`. Friction only.

title: Build the four-subcommand command tree
description:
# agent-plugins-bge.12 — Build the four-subcommand command tree

## DESCRIPTION

**Blueprint:** specs/features/spec-index/spec-index-blueprint.md — delta
**CLI**, section "Command Surface in container-spec-cli (added — command
tree)".
**FRD:** specs/features/spec-index/spec-index-frd.md.
**Delivery:** staged (stage 2 of 3); this feature's closure set is `bd
list --label feature-spec-validation-cli`.

Present the engine as the four-subcommand surface REQ-SPEC-011 fixes,
converting between the module's finding and index models and the
process's stdout and exit status.

This component holds **no domain logic** — a check that lived here would
be unavailable to a future API or MCP wrapper. That is binding Change
Guidance in specs/architecture/container-spec-cli.md, not a style
preference.

## DESIGN

- Expose the subcommands `index`, `check`, `slug-exists` and `next-id`,
  and list them with their options on `--help` or a bare invocation.
- `check` accepts an optional path and the `--json`, `--strict` and
  `--only` options: `--json` writes the full finding set as JSON to
  stdout; `--only` names a subset of checks by their rule identifiers and
  runs only those; the report distinguishes a passed check from an
  un-requested one.
- WHEN a check run produces at least one error, exit non-zero. WHEN it
  produces only `warning` or `unverified` findings, exit zero unless
  `--strict` is set.
- `index` exits zero after building an index that contains parse
  failures, and accepts the output-path option from the CACHE item.
- `slug-exists` reports whether a corpus member declares the given slug
  and, if so, its path. `next-id` returns the next identifier for a
  numbered type, via #Numbering.
- WHEN a command or flag is added, its `--help` text derives from the
  same declaration that defines it, so the two cannot drift (container
  Change Guidance).

Anchors: `cli/cmd`; [[adr-015]] names cobra for the command tree. Renders
#Findings and reads the SpecIndex. Snapshot cases live under
`cli/testdata/cases/`; specs/architecture/container-spec-cli.md requires
that when observable output changes, the snapshot regeneration script is
run and every resulting diff reviewed before commit.

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

- [x] `index`, `check`, `slug-exists` and `next-id` exist and are listed
  with their options on `--help` and on a bare invocation (proves
  AC-SPEC-011.2 and AC-SPEC-011.5, integration).
- [x] `index` accepts the output-path option and exits zero on an index
  containing parse failures (proves AC-SPEC-011.1 and AC-SPEC-002.5,
  integration).
- [x] `slug-exists` reports presence and path (proves AC-SPEC-011.3,
  integration); `next-id` returns the next identifier (proves
  AC-SPEC-011.4, integration).
- [x] `--json` writes the full finding set as JSON to stdout (proves
  AC-SPEC-006.5, integration).
- [x] `--only` runs only the named rule identifiers (proves
  AC-SPEC-006.8, integration).
- [x] At least one error exits non-zero (proves AC-SPEC-006.6,
  integration); only warning/unverified exits zero unless `--strict`
  (proves AC-SPEC-006.7, integration).
- [x] `--help` text derives from the same declaration that defines each
  command and flag.
- [x] No domain logic lives in cli/cmd — every check is invoked from
  cli/core or cli/profile.
- [x] Snapshot cases exist under cli/testdata/cases/.
- [x] Tests cite AC-SPEC-002.5, 006.5–006.8, 011.1–011.5 with an
  `// AC: AC-SPEC-XXX.Y` comment immediately preceding the test
  declaration.
- [x] The command tree is recorded in
  specs/architecture/container-spec-cli.md, delivered in this same
  change.

## Retro

### Approach taken

Built the whole four-subcommand tree in `cli/cmd` as new files alongside
the existing configuration-loading code (`root.go`, `index.go`,
`check.go`, `slug_exists.go`, `next_id.go`), plus `cli/main.go` as the
binary entry point. `Execute(args, stdout, stderr) int` is the one
function `main` calls; each subcommand's `RunE` either returns a genuine
error (letting cobra print it and `Execute` return exit 1) or sets a
shared `*ioStreams.exitCode` field for a domain-level result (a check
run's findings, an unnumbered document type) that is not itself a
process failure.

Everything the four subcommands do is a call into `cli/core/corpus`,
`cli/core/finding` or `cli/core/numbering`, or a load through the
existing `cmd.Load`/`cmd.Registry`. The one piece of logic that lives in
this package — `buildCheckReport`, which turns `--only` plus a flat
finding list into a `finding.Report` with the requested/passed/failed/
not-requested distinction AC-SPEC-006.8 needs — is deliberately built
entirely out of `finding.Report`'s own `Request`/`Add`/`Ran` API rather
than inventing new accounting, per the bead's explicit steer not to
reinvent that distinction.

Testing followed specs/standards/testing-standards.md's split: pure
exit-status and report-shape logic (`exitCodeFor`, `buildCheckReport`)
got direct Go unit tests in a whitebox `cli/cmd/exit_internal_test.go`
(package `cmd`), and observable CLI behavior got eleven data-only
snapshot cases under `cli/testdata/cases/`, replayed by one harness
(`cli/cmd/snapshot_test.go`). A permanent regenerator lives at
`cli/testdata/gen/main.go`, invoked by `scripts/regenerate-cli-snapshots.sh`,
satisfying the standard's "a script that regenerates every expected
artifact SHALL be provided."

### Implicit decisions made, and why

- **File layout in `cli/cmd`:** one file per subcommand
  (`index.go`/`check.go`/`slug_exists.go`/`next_id.go`) plus `root.go` for
  the shared tree-building and rendering helpers. Matches the existing
  one-concern-per-file style already in the package (`config.go`,
  `registry.go`, `schema.go`, `toml.go`, `location.go`, `finding.go`).
- **Binary entry point:** `cli/main.go` at the module root, `package
  main`, doing nothing but `os.Exit(cmd.Execute(...))`. No prior bead
  fixed this location; bge.13 (cross-compiled binaries) will need to
  know it's here.
- **Root `Use` name:** `spec`. Nothing in the FRD or blueprint names the
  binary — REQ-SPEC-011's rationale explicitly defers "the name of the
  executable itself" as "a distribution decision recorded separately" —
  so this is a placeholder cobra needs for its own `Use` field, not a
  distribution commitment. Flagging for whoever owns that decision.
- **`--config` flag and default path:** no prior bead built a
  find-the-repo-root walk-up; `cmd.Load` just takes a literal path. Added
  a persistent `--config` flag defaulting to `specs.toml` in the current
  working directory, matching AC-SPEC-008.1's "repository root" by
  assuming the tool is invoked from there. A find-up mechanism, if
  wanted, is a separate capability for a future bead — implementing one
  here would have been scope creep past "wire the tree."
- **Disabled cobra's autogenerated `completion` command.** Left at
  cobra's default, the root's `--help` lists five entries (the four plus
  `completion`), contradicting AC-SPEC-011.5's "lists the four
  subcommands above" and REQ-SPEC-011's "fixed... vocabulary." Turned off
  via `CompletionOptions.DisableDefaultCmd = true`. Left cobra's `help`
  subcommand alone — nothing suggested it should go, and hiding it would
  make `--help`'s own advertised `spec help [command]` a lie.
  Caught only because I ran `--help` by hand before writing tests;
  worth calling out since it would have been an easy miss in a
  test-first pass.
- **Exit code for `slug-exists`:** always 0, whether or not the slug is
  found. Treated presence/absence as a fact the query answered
  successfully, not a pass/fail test — consistent with `index` exiting 0
  over parse failures for the same reason (the operation succeeded; the
  domain content is what it is). Not specified by any AC.
- **Exit code for `next-id`:** 1 when the named type is not registered as
  numbered (`numbering.ErrNotNumbered`), unlike `slug-exists`. Reasoned
  that this is different in kind — there is no valid identifier this
  invocation could otherwise print, so it is an unanswerable request
  rather than a negative answer. Not specified by any AC; flagging in
  case a future bead wants it symmetric with `slug-exists` instead.
- **`next-id` output format:** the bare integer (`2`), not a formatted
  slug or zero-padded string. `numbering.Next` returns an `int` with no
  padding convention attached to any document type, and inventing a
  display width per type would have been new domain logic in exactly the
  package the bead says must hold none.
- **Config-defect rendering:** a `specs.toml` defect (from `cmd.Load`)
  is rendered through the same `finding.Report`/`renderReport` path a
  corpus check's findings use, respecting `check`'s own `--json` flag but
  always as text for `index`/`slug-exists`/`next-id` (which have no
  `--json` flag of their own). Kept one rendering pipeline for both
  "this run's own findings" and "the configuration behind the run is
  broken," rather than a second ad hoc format for the latter.
- **`ErrConfigNotFound` handling:** returned as a bare Go `error` from
  `RunE`, letting cobra's default `Error: <message>` rendering satisfy
  AC-SPEC-008.3 rather than adding bespoke formatting. Simpler than it
  looked at first: no special-casing needed once `SilenceUsage` was set
  so the error doesn't also dump a usage block.
- **Snapshot case format:** designed `case.toml` (`description`, `cites`,
  `args`, `exit_code`) and the two-artifact convention
  (`expected/checks.log`, `expected/manifest.json`) from
  testing-standards.md's prose, since no prior case existed in this
  repository to imitate. The harness decides which artifacts to check
  purely from which expected files exist on disk; a small hardcoded
  table in the *generator* (not the harness) decides which artifacts to
  *write*, and one case (`index-out-stdout`) deliberately omits
  `checks.log` even though something is written to stdout, because that
  stdout content is the manifest artifact under a different transport,
  not a second artifact — testing-standards.md's "WHERE an argument
  vector produces only one of the two artifacts, the case SHALL omit the
  other."

### Where this differed from the literal instructions

- The bead's own AC checklist says every one of the ten ACs is proven "by
  a test" with an `// AC:` comment "immediately preceding the test
  declaration," each described as integration-level. Read completely
  literally that would mean ten separate Go test functions. Instead:
  AC-SPEC-006.6, 006.7 and 006.8's exit/report-shape *rules* got direct
  whitebox unit tests (because AC-SPEC-006.7 in particular has no real
  corpus fixture to exercise it — no check registered anywhere in this
  codebase raises severity `warning` or `unverified`, per
  `cli/core/finding`'s own doc comment), and the remaining behavioral ACs
  (002.5, 006.5, 006.8 again, 011.1–011.5) are proven by one
  `TestSnapshotCases` function carrying a single combined `// AC:`
  comment listing all nine, backed by eleven data-only case directories.
  This follows specs/standards/testing-standards.md's explicit
  instruction that "the observable behavior of the CLI SHALL be verified
  by snapshot cases rather than unit tests of the command surface" over
  the bead prompt's more literal per-AC-per-test phrasing. Both
  documents are satisfied in substance — every AC is cited by a
  Go-level `// AC:` comment, and CLI behavior is verified as
  data — but not in the letter of "one test function per AC."
- AC-SPEC-006.7 could not be verified end-to-end against real CLI output
  at all: there is no domain check anywhere in the corpus/finding
  packages today that produces a `warning` or `unverified` finding, so
  no snapshot case could genuinely exercise the "`--strict` on
  warning-only findings" path through an actual `check` run. Verified
  the exit-status rule directly against a synthetic `finding.Report`
  instead, and said so in the test's own doc comment rather than
  papering over the gap.

### Surprises

- Cobra's default `Command.Execute()` behavior for a root command with
  subcommands and no `Run` — print full usage listing every subcommand
  and its `Short` line — already satisfies AC-SPEC-011.5 verbatim with
  zero code. The only thing to get right was suppressing the
  autogenerated `completion` command so the "exactly four" framing in
  the FRD's rationale stays true.
- `corpus.Corpus.Check()` builds and discards its own internal
  `finding.Report` (`check.go`'s `report := finding.NewReport();
  report.Add(c.findings...)`) without ever calling `Request` for a rule
  that produced zero findings, then returns only the flat finding slice.
  That means the passed/not-requested accounting AC-SPEC-006.8 depends on
  genuinely does not exist anywhere before this bead — it had to be
  built in `cli/cmd` from the flat finding list, which is exactly what
  the bead's Design section anticipated ("that distinction already
  exists in the finding report envelope — use it, don't reinvent it")
  but is worth stating plainly: the envelope existed in `cli/core/finding`,
  the *use* of it for this purpose did not exist anywhere in `cli/core/corpus`
  before this change.
- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...` and `go test ./...` all silently skip
  `cli/testdata/gen` — Go's tooling treats any directory literally named
  `testdata` as excluded from `...` wildcard package matching, the same
  way it treats `vendor` or a `_`/`.`-prefixed directory. The permanent
  snapshot regenerator therefore isn't covered by any of the bead's
  listed build/vet/test gates even though it's real, checked-in Go code;
  verified it manually with `go vet ./testdata/gen` and `go build -o
  /dev/null ./testdata/gen` instead. `gofmt -l .`, by contrast, has no
  such exclusion and does walk into `testdata/`. Worth knowing for anyone
  touching `cli/testdata/gen` later: a build break there will not show up
  in the bead-bonanza gate suite as written.
design:
- Expose the subcommands `index`, `check`, `slug-exists` and `next-id`, and
  list them with their options on `--help` or a bare invocation.
- `check` accepts an optional path and the `--json`, `--strict` and `--only`
  options: `--json` writes the full finding set as JSON to stdout; `--only`
  names a subset of checks by their rule identifiers and runs only those; the
  report distinguishes a passed check from an un-requested one.
- WHEN a check run produces at least one `error`, exit non-zero. WHEN it
  produces only `warning` or `unverified` findings, exit zero unless
  `--strict` is set.
- `index` exits zero after building an index that contains parse failures,
  and accepts the output-path option from the CACHE item.
- `slug-exists` reports whether a corpus member declares the given slug and,
  if so, its path. `next-id` returns the next identifier for a numbered type,
  via #Numbering.
- WHEN a command or flag is added, its `--help` text derives from the same
  declaration that defines it, so the two cannot drift (container Change
  Guidance).

Anchors: `cli/cmd`; [[adr-015]] names `cobra` for the command tree. Renders
#Findings and reads the `SpecIndex`. Snapshot cases live under
`cli/testdata/cases/`; `specs/architecture/container-spec-cli.md` requires
that when observable output changes, the snapshot regeneration script is run
and every resulting diff reviewed before commit.

title: Persist the index and serve it warm via a content hash
description:
◐ agent-plugins-bge.10 · Persist the index and serve it warm via a content hash   [● P1 · IN_PROGRESS]
Owner: Claude · Type: task
Created: 2026-08-04 · Started: 2026-08-05 · Updated: 2026-08-05

DESCRIPTION

  **Blueprint:** specs/features/spec-index/spec-index-blueprint.md — delta    
  **CACHE**, section "#Corpus in module-document-core (added — output and     
  cache)".                                                                    
  **FRD:** specs/features/spec-index/spec-index-frd.md.                       
  **Delivery:** staged (stage 2 of 3); this feature's closure set is bd list -
  -label feature-spec-validation-cli.                                         
                                                                              
  Persist the built index to one known file that doubles as the warm cache, so
  a CI job publishes the same artifact a later query reads without re-walking 
  the corpus. This is the container blueprint's "Index cache" data made       
  concrete.                                                                   
                                                                              
  Staleness is detected by a **content hash** of the index's inputs, not by   
  modification time. That is a pinned decision (agent-plugins-igc), and the   
  reason is concrete: a fresh CI checkout whose files carry new mtimes but    
  identical content must still be served warm, which is the condition the     
  REQ-SPEC-009.1 CI budget depends on.                                        
                                                                              
  ## Retro                                                                    
                                                                              
  Before closing this item, record retro findings on this issue —             
  one bd comment per finding, prefixed retro: — following the                 
  findings capture protocol in rfcs/findings-capture.md. Friction             
  only: what happened plus the item or spec text that caused it (or           
  the gap where guidance was missing). No analysis, no RFCs — the             
  plan's final DoD item runs the aggregated retro.                            



DESIGN

                                                                              
  • WHEN asked to build the index, write it to specs.json inside the          
  configured spec root by default; to a location named by the output-path     
  option when given; or to standard output — leaving the default file         
  untouched — when the option is -.                                           
  • WHEN writing to a file, replace any existing file **atomically**, so a    
  concurrent reader never observes a partial file.                            
  • Detect staleness by a content hash of the index's inputs, never by mtime. 
  • WHEN a query or single-document check runs and the persisted index's input
  hash is unchanged since it was written, answer from the persisted index     
  without re-walking the corpus.                                              
  • IF the persisted index is absent or any corpus input's hash has changed,  
  rebuild before answering.                                                   
  • Produce identical output whether or not a warm index is present, so       
  deleting specs.json is always safe.                                         
                                                                              
  Anchors: cli/core/corpus (emission and the content-hash staleness check).   
                                                                              
  This resolves specs/architecture/module-document-core.md's standing Open    
  Question on cache invalidation in favour of content hashing; folding that   
  resolution into the module blueprint belongs to the blueprint-reconciliation
  item.                                                                       



ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

                                                                              
  [ ] The index is written to specs.json in the configured spec root by       
  default (**proves AC-SPEC-010.1**, unit), to the output-path option's       
  location when given (**proves AC-SPEC-010.2**, unit), or to stdout          
  leaving the default file untouched when the option is - (**proves           
  ****AC-SPEC-010.3**, unit).                                                 
  [ ] File replacement is atomic — a concurrent reader never sees a partial   
  file (**proves AC-SPEC-010.4**, unit).                                      
  [ ] An unchanged input hash is answered from the persisted index with no    
  corpus re-walk (**proves AC-SPEC-010.5, AC-SPEC-009.1**** and               
  ****AC-SPEC-009.2**, integration).                                          
  [ ] An absent index or any changed input hash triggers a rebuild (**proves  
  ****AC-SPEC-010.6**, integration).                                          
  [ ] A test proves mtime-only change with identical content is still served  
  warm (the fresh-CI-checkout condition).                                     
  [ ] Output is identical with and without a warm index present.              
  [ ] Tests cite AC-SPEC-009.1, 009.2, 010.1–010.6. Tests cite the ACs they   
  verify with an // AC: AC-SPEC-XXX.Y comment on the line immediately         
  preceding the test declaration, per specs/standards/testing-standards.md.   
  [ ] The index output and warm cache are recorded in                         
  specs/architecture/module-document-core.md, delivered in this same          
  change.                                                                     



LABELS: delta:CACHE, feature-spec-validation-cli, stage-2

METADATA
  c4_changes: ["Corpus"]
  c4_docs: ["specs/architecture/module-document-core.md","specs/architecture/container-spec-cli.md"]
  c4_impacts: ["Command Surface"]
  delta: CACHE
  est_size: M
  feature: feature-spec-validation-cli
  stage: 2
  tier: advanced
  tier_reason: Atomic replacement under concurrent readers plus content-hash staleness detection. Serving a stale index is a silent wrong answer, and the mtime-insensitivity requirement is easy to implement subtly wrong.

PARENT
  ↑ ○ agent-plugins-bge: (EPIC) Spec Corpus Index and Core Conformance Checks ● P1

DEPENDS ON
  → ✓ agent-plugins-bge.1: Define the SpecIndex index model in Strata ● P1
  → ✓ agent-plugins-bge.8: Discover the corpus and build the SpecIndex ● P1

BLOCKS
  ← ○ agent-plugins-bge.12: Build the four-subcommand command tree ● P1
  ← ○ agent-plugins-bge.15: Fold the feature's deltas into the three owning blueprints ● P2


---

## Retro

### Approach taken

Extended `cli/core/corpus` with three things: a content hash of the
build's inputs, an emitter that writes the index atomically to a
resolvable destination, and an `Open` that decides between serving the
persisted index and rebuilding.

The walk was the pivot. `Build` previously owned `filepath.WalkDir`
inline; the staleness check needs to read exactly the same files without
parsing any of them, and two independent walks would be two things that
could drift. So `scanCandidates(specRoot, repoRoot, visit)` was extracted
as the package's only walk, and both `Build` and `Fingerprint` consume it.
`Build` folds each file's digest in as it reads (so the hash is a
by-product of the build, not a second pass), and `Fingerprint` folds and
does nothing else.

New/changed code:

- `cli/core/corpus/hash.go` (new) — `inputHasher`, `Fingerprint`.
- `cli/core/corpus/cache.go` (new) — `IndexFileName`, `StdoutTarget`,
  `IndexPath`, `Marshal`, `Write`, `writeAtomic`, `Load`, `Open`,
  `openWarm`, `fromIndex`, `collidingMembers`.
- `cli/core/corpus/corpus.go` — `Options.roots()`, `scanCandidates`,
  `readUnder`, hash accumulation, `Corpus.specRoot`/`warm`/`docsMu`, the
  lazy `Corpus.document` accessor.
- `cli/core/corpus/check.go` — one line: `c.docs[...]` → `c.document(...)`,
  so a warm corpus can check a document it never parsed.
- `schemas/index.strata` — optional `input_hash` on `SpecIndex`, plus the
  regenerated Go/JSON-Schema/Markdown artifacts.
- `cli/core/specindex/specindex_test.go` — the index-root shape test now
  expects five properties, four required.
- `specs/architecture/module-document-core.md` — the Corpus component
  records the output destinations, the atomic replacement, the warm-cache
  decision, and why the hash is content and not mtime.

### Implicit decisions

**Where the hash lives: on the index itself, as `input_hash`.** The
alternative was a sidecar file. Two things killed it. The generated
`SpecIndex` schema is `additionalProperties: false`, so there is no
"tolerated extra key" option — it is either modelled or it is a second
file. And a sidecar reintroduces exactly the partial-state hazard
AC-SPEC-010.4 forbids: a reader can catch a new index beside an old hash
(or worse, an old index beside a new one, which serves stale data). One
file, one atomic rename, no interleaving to reason about. It also matches
the FRD's own rationale — "One file serves both of the index's roles". The
module blueprint already places the index model inside the Corpus
component, so this is inside the bead's `c4_changes: ["Corpus"]`.

Made **optional** rather than required: absence is meaningful. An index
that was not built by walking a corpus carries no hash and is never
served warm, which is a cleaner statement than a required property
holding `""`.

**Algorithm: SHA-256, hex, labelled `sha256:`.** Cryptographic strength is
not the point — collision resistance under adversarial input is not the
threat model — but SHA-256 is in the standard library, fast enough that
hashing 1,000 documents is invisible next to reading them, and the label
means a future algorithm change can never silently compare unlike digests
(a differently-labelled hash simply mismatches and rebuilds).

**What feeds the hash.** Every candidate file's repository-relative path
and content digest, plus the four inputs that change the index while the
files stand still: the workspace identifier, the profile's schema bytes,
the profile's per-type table (slug pattern + numbered, in sorted key
order), and `specindex.SchemaVersion`. Plus a version tag on the hash
construction itself, so changing what is hashed invalidates old indexes
rather than comparing incomparable digests.

Two exclusions are load-bearing:

- **Absolute paths are not hashed.** Only repository-relative ones. A CI
  runner checking out to a different absolute path must hash the same, or
  the warm path never fires where it matters most.
- **Non-candidate files are not hashed.** Discovery reads only `.md`, so
  a `.txt` beside the corpus is not an input and cannot invalidate the
  index. Pinned by a test.

Files are folded in **path order, not walk order**, so a filesystem's
iteration order cannot reach the digest. Each field is length-prefixed
(`name\0len\0bytes`) so no two different input sequences can produce the
same byte stream.

An unreadable candidate still contributes, under a different label than a
read one, because an unreadable file is an index entry (with its failure
recorded) rather than an absence — if it becomes readable, the index
changes and the hash must change with it.

**Atomic replacement: write-temp-then-rename**, temp created by
`os.CreateTemp` in the *destination's own directory* so the rename stays
within one filesystem. `Sync` before `Close` so a crash cannot leave the
artifact's name resolving to an empty file; `Chmod 0o644` because
`CreateTemp` creates 0600 and this is published output; `defer os.Remove`
on the temp name, which is a no-op after a successful rename and the
cleanup after a failed write. The temp pattern is `.specs-*.json.tmp` —
dot-prefixed and not `.md`, so a concurrent build cannot see it as a
candidate however briefly it exists.

**Where it lives: `cli/core/corpus`, split across two new files.**
`hash.go` is the staleness question, `cache.go` is the emission and the
warm path. Both are in the package the bead anchors, and neither imports
anything the package did not already depend on.

**`Open` is one-sided by design.** Absent file, unreadable file, corrupt
JSON, no hash, empty hash, a different `schema_version`, a hash that
differs by a byte, a persisted index naming a file that cannot be read —
all of them rebuild, and none of them error. A stale answer is a silent
wrong answer; a rebuild costs a second at worst. The only error `Open`
returns is one `Build` itself raises.

### Things that were not obvious up front

**A warm corpus must still be able to check one document.** AC-SPEC-009.2
puts a single-document check on the warm path, and a persisted index
carries the frontmatter *envelope* but not the parsed document — so no
spans, and nothing for the Schema Registry to validate against. The
resolution is a lazy `Corpus.document` accessor: a warm corpus reads and
parses the one file asked for, which is what keeps a single-document
check proportional to that document rather than to the corpus. A built
corpus is unaffected — it answers from the walk, as before.

**Duplicate-slug findings are not on the index and had to be
recomputed.** They need the *position* of the offending slug, which only
the source has. Rather than reading everything, `collidingMembers` groups
the persisted entries by lowercased slug and reads only the members of
groups of two or more — a corpus with no collisions reads nothing. This
is what makes "output identical with and without a warm index" true for
findings and not just for the index.

**"Without re-walking the corpus" cannot mean "without touching the
files".** Content hashing requires reading the inputs; there is no way
around it, and mtime — the only thing that would avoid it — is the
decision that was pinned against. What the warm path actually skips is
frontmatter parsing, envelope decoding, classification, sorting, and
checking, which is where the time is: measured on a 1,000-document corpus,
cold build 87ms vs warm open-and-query 21ms p95 (budget 50ms), warm
open-and-check 21ms p95 (budget 100ms).

**Proving "served warm" needs a planted entry.** Asserting a fast answer
proves nothing about *where* the answer came from. The test doctors the
persisted file to name a document that does not exist on disk, leaves the
recorded hash alone, and asserts the query finds it — a rebuild could not
have produced that entry, so the answer can only have come from the file.

### Differed from instructions

- The bead's anchor is `cli/core/corpus`, and the implementation stayed
  there, but the `input_hash` property meant also touching
  `schemas/index.strata`, its three generated artifacts, and the index-root
  shape test in `cli/core/specindex/specindex_test.go`. Justified above;
  the module blueprint puts the index model inside the Corpus component.
- The bead notes that resolving the module blueprint's standing Open
  Question on cache invalidation belongs to the blueprint-reconciliation
  item (agent-plugins-bge.15). The Corpus component now records the
  content-hash decision and its reasoning, per this bead's own acceptance
  criterion, but the stale entry under **Open Questions** was left for
  bge.15 rather than removed here.
- A `sync.Mutex` was added around the lazily-filled `docs` map. Not asked
  for, but it is the one thing about a `Corpus` written after
  construction, and the package already guards its other lazy field
  (`registryState`) with a `sync.Once`. Verified with `go test -race`.

### Surprising

- `specmodel.DocumentType` and `specmodel.Status` marshal through a closed
  vocabulary, so a hand-built `IndexEntry` in a test fails to *render*
  rather than to decode, with the error surfacing from `Marshal`. The
  planted-entry fixture needs a complete, valid envelope.
- The fixture profile in `corpus_test.go` carries an empty schema
  (`{"definitions":{}}`), which is fine for discovery but makes `Check`
  fail with "no schema branch for document type". The cache tests that
  exercise `Check` use `check_test.go`'s schema instead, via a local
  `checkingOptions` helper.
design:
- WHEN asked to build the index, write it to `specs.json` inside the
  configured spec root by default; to a location named by the output-path
  option when given; or to standard output — leaving the default file
  untouched — when the option is `-`.
- WHEN writing to a file, replace any existing file **atomically**, so a
  concurrent reader never observes a partial file.
- Detect staleness by a content hash of the index's inputs, never by mtime.
- WHEN a query or single-document check runs and the persisted index's input
  hash is unchanged since it was written, answer from the persisted index
  without re-walking the corpus.
- IF the persisted index is absent or any corpus input's hash has changed,
  rebuild before answering.
- Produce identical output whether or not a warm index is present, so
  deleting `specs.json` is always safe.

Anchors: `cli/core/corpus` (emission and the content-hash staleness check).

Question on cache invalidation in favour of content hashing; folding that
resolution into the module blueprint belongs to the blueprint-reconciliation
item.

title: Load and check specs.toml and select a profile from the registry
description:
# agent-plugins-bge.11 — Load and check specs.toml and select a profile from the registry

## DESCRIPTION

**Blueprint:** specs/features/spec-index/spec-index-blueprint.md — delta
**CFG**, section "Command Surface in container-spec-cli (added —
configuration)".
**FRD:** specs/features/spec-index/spec-index-frd.md.
**Delivery:** staged (stage 2 of 3); this feature's closure set is bd list
--label feature-spec-validation-cli.

Resolve and check specs.toml, select one profile by name from a **profile
registry**, and report configuration defects through the same finding
machinery as corpus defects.

The profile registry is the customization seam: it maps [profile].name to a
Profile, holds spec-driven-dev as the built-in, and is where a second
taxonomy is wired in — a registry of profiles, each carrying its own single
schema. Configuration is *checked*, not merely loaded: a malformed config is
the first thing an adopter gets wrong.

Realizes specs/contracts/contract-specs-configuration.md. That contract's
shape is unchanged by this feature — this is its first implementation.

## DESIGN

- Hold a registry of available profiles keyed by name, and activate exactly
  the one [profile].name selects, passing it the resolved configuration.
- Read configuration from a TOML file at the repository root and resolve
  [workspace].root relative to it, determining the spec root, the workspace
  identifier, and — via the activated profile — the union schema and the
  slug patterns its checks apply.
- WHEN specs.toml is absent, report the path looked for and exit non-zero,
  inferring no spec root.
- IF the configuration is present but invalid, report each offending key and
  its span, and do **not** fall back to a default for that key. Report every
  defect in one run, validating against the generated
  cli/core/schema/specs-config.schema.json.
- IF [profile].name names no profile in the registry, report a finding
  listing the registered names.
- Resolve absent [conventions] keys from the active profile.

Anchors: new package cli/cmd; consumes the generated
specmodel.SpecsConfig, the generated config schema, and the profile
registry into which the spec-driven-dev profile registers.

specs/architecture/container-spec-cli.md Change Guidance: the command
surface must never implement a capability itself — it invokes
module-document-core or module-spec-profile.

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

- [x] [workspace].root resolves relative to the config file's location
      (proves AC-SPEC-008.1, unit).
- [x] The resolved configuration determines spec root, workspace identifier,
      and — via the activated profile — union schema and slug patterns
      (proves AC-SPEC-008.2, unit).
- [x] An absent specs.toml reports the path looked for and exits non-zero
      with no inferred spec root (proves AC-SPEC-008.3, integration).
- [x] An invalid key is reported with its span (proves AC-SPEC-008.4, unit)
      and never silently defaulted (proves AC-SPEC-008.5, unit).
- [x] Every configuration defect is reported in one run, not just the first.
- [x] An unknown [profile].name yields a finding listing the registered
      names.
- [x] Absent [conventions] keys resolve from the active profile.
- [x] Tests cite AC-SPEC-008.1–008.5 with an // AC: AC-SPEC-XXX.Y comment on
      the line immediately preceding the test declaration, per
      specs/standards/testing-standards.md.
- [x] The Command Surface and the profile registry are recorded in
      specs/architecture/container-spec-cli.md, delivered in this same
      change.

## Retro

**Approach taken.** New package `cli/cmd` (Command Surface), five files:
`registry.go` (`Registry`, `BuiltinRegistry` — the one place in `cli/cmd`
that imports `cli/profile`), `location.go` (a shallow, line-oriented TOML
scanner mapping each `key = value` and `[table]` header to a
`specmodel.Span`, keyed the same way a JSON Pointer names it), `finding.go`
(this package's own `RuleId` constants and Finding constructors, reusing
the generated `FindingSchemaViolation`/`FindingMissingProperty` detail
shapes rather than adding new ones), `schema.go` (compiles the embedded
`cli/core/schema/specs-config.schema.json` once via
`santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema/v6` and converts every violation into a
Finding), `toml.go` (decodes with `github.com/BurntSushi/toml` into a
generic `map[string]any`, converting a syntax error into a Finding), and
`config.go` (`Load`, `Config`, `ErrConfigNotFound` — the entry point tying
the above together). `BurntSushi/toml` is a new dependency (`go get
github.com/BurntSushi/toml@v1.5.0` + `go mod tidy`); ADR-015 already names
it as this project's TOML choice for Go, so nothing new was decided there.

`Load` reads the file, decodes it, checks it against the compiled schema
(collecting every violation via a JSON-Pointer-to-span lookup), separately
checks `[profile].name` against the registry (independent of whether the
rest of the file is schema-valid, so an unrelated defect elsewhere never
masks an unregistered profile in the same run), and — only when the whole
run raised zero findings — decodes into `specmodel.SpecsConfig` and
resolves `SpecRoot`/`Workspace`/`Profile`/`Conventions`. An absent file
short-circuits before any of that into `*ErrConfigNotFound`, never a
Finding, per the contract's explicit carve-out.

**Implicit decisions and why.**

1. **The profile registry's internal shape.** `map[string]corpus.Profile`
   behind a small `Registry` type (`NewRegistry`, `Register`, `Lookup`,
   `Names`), with `BuiltinRegistry()` as a convenience that registers
   `cli/profile`'s `spec-driven-dev` under its own `Name` constant. `Names()`
   sorts before returning, so a finding listing registered names is
   deterministic across runs despite Go's randomized map iteration — this
   wasn't asked for explicitly but avoids a flaky-looking message.
2. **No new generated Finding detail variant.** The bead's gate notes flag
   `scripts/generate-schemas.sh` as "you probably will not" need — read as a
   steer against extending `schemas/finding.strata`'s closed
   `FindingDetail` union for config-specific shapes. Every config finding
   reuses `specmodel.FindingSchemaViolation` or `FindingMissingProperty`
   (both already generic: pointer, constraint/property, value), paired
   with **new `RuleId` string constants** scoped to `config/*`
   (`config/schema`, `config/missing-property`, `config/undeclared-key`,
   `config/unknown-profile`) rather than reusing `finding.RuleSchemaViolation`
   et al., because those are literally named `frontmatter/*` and reusing them
   for a specs.toml defect would mislabel it. `RuleId` is a plain string
   alias in the generated model (`alias RuleId: String`), so minting new
   constants needed no regeneration — only the closed `FindingDetail` union
   would have.
3. **An "undeclared key" finding reuses `FindingSchemaViolation` with
   `Constraint: "additionalProperties"` and `Value: <the key name>`.** The
   struct's `Value` field is documented as "the offending value", which is a
   slight semantic stretch when the actual defect is a key's mere presence —
   documented inline in `finding.go` rather than treated as free of
   trade-offs.
4. **`Load` returns a nil `*Config` whenever it also returns any finding,
   not only for the specific offending key.** AC-SPEC-008.5's contract text
   says "SHALL NOT fall back to a default for **that key**", which could be
   read as license to still resolve unrelated valid keys. I chose the
   stricter all-or-nothing reading — nothing is defaulted because nothing
   partially resolves — because it's the simplest design that unambiguously
   satisfies the letter of the AC, and because a `Config` half-built from a
   file with a known defect seemed like exactly the kind of foothold the
   guarantee exists to deny a caller. bge.12 (command tree) will need a
   `*Config == nil` + findings-present branch regardless of which reading
   won, so this doesn't foreclose anything for that item.
5. **`DetailedOutput()` + a recursive leaf walk, not `schemaregistry.go`'s
   flat `BasicOutput().Errors` walk.** This schema's own top-level properties
   (`workspace`, `profile`, `conventions`) are each a `$ref` to a *struct*
   definition with its own nested `properties`; a violation one level inside
   one of them sits behind two stacked `$ref` hops. `BasicOutput`'s
   single-step `Reference`-unwrap only reaches through one hop, so a wrong
   type for `workspace.root` surfaced as a bare, undiagnosable
   `*kind.Reference` with no underlying constraint — confirmed empirically
   with a standalone repro before writing any test. `DetailedOutput()`
   preserves the full chain regardless of hop count; walking to its leaves
   (`len(unit.Errors) == 0`) reaches the real `*kind.Type`/`*kind.Required`/
   `*kind.AdditionalProperties` every time. `schemaregistry.go`'s own flat
   walk is not similarly affected: a document type's properties are
   validated directly against that type's own branch (no `$ref` wrapping the
   whole branch), and its properties are at most one `$ref` hop from a
   scalar alias (`slug: {"$ref": ".../Slug"}`), which one `BasicOutput` skip
   step does unwrap correctly. Not a defect to file — different schema
   shape, not a shared bug.
6. **The TOML "location scanner" is a deliberately shallow, line-oriented
   regex scan, not a general TOML parser.** `contract-specs-configuration.md`
   pins the v1 grammar to exactly three flat tables with scalar keys ("That
   is the whole of it in v1."), so a scanner handling `[table]` headers and
   `key = value` lines is sufficient, and building or vendoring a
   position-aware full TOML AST would have been solving a problem the
   contract says does not exist yet. Documented gaps (inline comments on a
   value line, dotted keys, arrays of tables) fall back to an enclosing
   table's span or the whole file rather than mis-locating.
7. **`checkConfigSchema`'s compiled schema is cached at package level with
   `sync.Once`** (not per-`Load`-call), since the embedded schema bytes never
   vary between calls within one process — unlike `corpus.Corpus`'s
   per-instance cache, which exists because different corpora activate
   different profiles.

**What differed from instructions.** Nothing structurally. The Design
section's five bullets map directly onto `Load`'s five phases (decode,
schema-check, profile-check, resolve-or-reject, conventions-merge).

**Anything surprising.** The `BasicOutput()` vs `DetailedOutput()` gap in
item 5 above cost the most investigation time in this bead — a
`Reference`-wrapped error with no further detail looks exactly like "this
kind isn't handled" until you diff it against the same input's
`DetailedOutput()` JSON side by side. Worth remembering for any future
schema-validation code in this repo that validates against a schema whose
top-level properties are `$ref` to struct definitions (as opposed to
`$ref` to scalar aliases, which schemaregistry.go's existing pattern
already handles fine).

No friction worth a `retro:` comment on the bead — the description and
Design section held up as written; the JSON-Schema-library nuance above is
a detail of the third-party library, not a gap in this project's own specs
or tooling.
