title: ADR: index cache invalidation
description:
Requested directly by the user, 2026-07-31: 'ADR the cache invalidation'.

FRD-spec-validation-cli defines a 'warm index' (a cached index whose inputs are unchanged since it was built) and hangs three latency ACs on it — AC-SPEC-009.1, AC-SPEC-009.2 and AC-SPEC-009.4 all assume warmth. Nothing decides how warmth is determined or invalidated.

Open questions the ADR must answer: what keys the cache (content hash, mtime, size, git object id); whether configuration changes invalidate the whole cache or a subset; whether the profile version participates in the key (it must, or a rule change silently reuses stale findings); where the cache lives and whether it is gitignored; what happens on a partial invalidation.
acceptance_criteria: An approved ADR fixing the cache key, the invalidation triggers, the on-disk location, and the correctness argument that a stale finding cannot survive a rule change
close_reason: Decided: content hash (input_hash), not mtime. Recorded on the issue and in the retired blueprint's Tracker Reconciliation; ADR deliberately not authored per the blueprint's stated default.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: Superseded by feature-spec-validation-cli: cache staleness is detected by **content hash** of the index's inputs, not mtime — pinned in the CACHE delta of the approved feature blueprint. Close by recording that decision, or write it up as an ADR documenting the rejected mtime alternative (maintainer's choice). Close or re-scope when agent-plugins-bge.16 lands.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
Resolved by feature-spec-validation-cli and closed at its retirement (agent-plugins-bge.16), taking the closing default the blueprint offers rather than authoring the ADR.

DECISION: index cache staleness is detected by a **content hash of the corpus inputs**, not by modification time. The built index carries the digest as input_hash (a sha256: value, visible in 'spec index --out -'); a query or single-document check answers from the persisted specs.json when that digest is unchanged and rebuilds otherwise. Implemented in cli/core/corpus (cache path), verified by cli/core/corpus/cache_test.go citing AC-SPEC-009.1, AC-SPEC-009.2, AC-SPEC-010.5 and AC-SPEC-010.6.

WHY NOT AN ADR: the blueprint offered either closing with the choice recorded or writing it up to document the rejected mtime alternative. Closing is the better fit — mtime was the only alternative in contention and it is not a live trade-off but a defect: a fresh CI checkout carries new mtimes over identical content, so an mtime cache would cold-build on every CI run and defeat the REQ-SPEC-009.1 budget this decision exists to protect. An ADR recording one rejected option with no standing tension would be ceremony. If a second invalidation strategy is ever proposed (e.g. a partial or per-file cache), that is the moment to author one.

title: ADR: adopt strata as the single source of truth for schemas and generated types
description:
Requested in PR #4 review of container-spec-cli (2026-07-31): 'Use strata: git@github.com:strata-lang/strata.git'.

Strata models a structure once and generates JSON Schema, Markdown documentation, and Go structs from that one definition. The reviewer wants it used to model: the specs.toml configuration, the frontmatter structure, the JSON artifacts the tool emits, and the structure of errors/findings emitted as JSON.

## Session setup requirement

This session could NOT reach the strata repo. add_repo failed ('cross-tier adds are not supported in v1'), git clone failed on proxy auth, GitHub MCP is scoped to brettcallaghan/agent-plugins, and WebFetch of raw content 404d. list_repos confirmed the repo IS available to the account (private, can_push).

**Create the next session with BOTH brettcallaghan/agent-plugins AND strata-lang/strata as initial sources.** Without that the ADR cannot be written against the real tool.

## Reading list (from the strata repo root)
- docs/public/strata.llm.md
- docs/content/docs/lang.mdx

## Known constraints
- Do not use the binary from the last release; build the CLI from source (Rust). This is a temporary Rust build-time dependency in a Go project, which the ADR must address.
- Known issue: strata-generated Go structs carry no YAML or TOML tags. The agreed workaround is to convert YAML/TOML to JSON and deserialize from JSON. module-document-core's Frontmatter component already documents this two-step model.
- Strata is a build-time tool whose generated artifacts get committed; advised against embedding strata binaries in this repo (423 KiB packed, distributed by clone via .claude-plugin/marketplace.json).
- Does NOT replace santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema — strata generates the schema, that library validates against it.
acceptance_criteria: An approved ADR recording the strata adoption decision, what it generates, where generated artifacts live and how they are regenerated, how the Rust build-time dependency is managed in CI, and the YAML/TOML tag workaround

title: spec: add a type-independent document self-check step (RFC P1)
description:
## Retro

Implemented in the bead-bonanza orchestrator's own loop (no `Agent` tool
exists in this session, so no subagent could be dispatched).

**Changed**

- `plugin/skills/spec/references/document-readiness-checklist.md` — new
  (102 lines, carries `## Contents`). Eight type-independent checks.
  Checks 1, 2, 3 and 6 cite `[[template-authoring-standards]]`
  (check 3 routing on to `[[frontmatter-standards]]` for the status
  vocabulary); check 8 cites `[[cross-document-references]]`. Checks 4
  (EARS coverage), 5 (compound modal verbs) and 7 (instruction blocks
  deleted) are stated in the file's own voice.
- `plugin/skills/spec/SKILL.md` — new Authoring Workflow step 7
  ("Self-check the finished document"), inserted after step 6
  ("Preflight feature blueprints") and before the retro offer, which
  renumbered from 7 to 8. Frontmatter `version` 1.3 -> 1.4.
- `plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` — version 0.7.0 -> 0.8.0.

**Implicit decisions made**

- Step number: the new step is 7, retro offer renumbered to 8. No other
  file references the spec skill's step numbers (grepped), so nothing
  downstream needed updating.
- New file's frontmatter: `status: active`, `version: "0.1"`, slug
  `document-readiness-checklist` — matched to its sibling
  `blueprint-readiness-checklist.md`, whose slug likewise ends in
  "checklist" rather than a standards role noun.
- Considered and reverted: a References-table row pointing at the new
  checklist. Every row in that table exceeds 80 columns (table cells are
  exempt from the width rule), but this bead's acceptance criteria state
  an unconditional "every line added or changed is at most 80
  characters". The AC won; the row was removed. The step body cites
  `references/document-readiness-checklist.md` as a backticked path, so
  check-skills.sh still validates the one-hop reference.

**Constraint honored**

`plugin/skills/spec/references/blueprint-readiness-checklist.md` is
byte-identical to its pre-change state (`git diff` empty).

**Gates**

- `scripts/sync-shared-references.sh --check` — PASS (11 vendored
  references current; the new file is not a vendored reference).
- `scripts/dogfood-install.sh` — re-materialized `.claude/skills/`.
- `scripts/check-skills.sh` — PASS, exit 0. One pre-existing warning
  (bead-bonanza SKILL.md body is 770 lines), unrelated to this bead.
- 80-column check on every added/changed line — clean.

**Not done (forced by the orchestrator's no-commit rule)**

No commit, no push. `scripts/bb-close-bead.sh` was deliberately not used
because it commits; the close, export and stage steps were performed
manually in the skill's prescribed order.
design:
Two edits, both under `plugin/skills/spec/`.

(a) Insert a new numbered step into the Authoring Workflow — the ordered
list beginning at `plugin/skills/spec/SKILL.md:188` — placed after the
existing step 6 ("Preflight feature blueprints", line 210) and before
step 7's retro offer, renumbering the following steps:

    N. **Self-check the finished document.** Before setting any document
       to `ready-for-review`, run
       `references/document-readiness-checklist.md` against it. Fix what
       it reports and re-run; do not set `ready-for-review` while any
       check fails. (Feature blueprints additionally run the blueprint
       readiness checklist in step 6 — that one is about groomability,
       this one about conformance.)

(b) Create `plugin/skills/spec/references/document-readiness-checklist.md`
holding these eight type-independent checks:

    1. Frontmatter parses as YAML and declares title, description, slug,
       type, status, updated_at.
    2. The slug matches the registry's rule for this type.
    3. status is a value from the controlled vocabulary.
    4. Every normative statement uses an EARS pattern.
    5. No requirement joins two modal verbs with "and".
    6. No prose line exceeds 80 characters (tables, URLs, fences exempt).
    7. Every template instruction comment block has been deleted.
    8. Every [[slug]] reference resolves to an existing document.

CITE, DO NOT RESTATE — this is the triage refinement; do not copy the
RFC's literal checklist text. Checks 1, 2, 3, 6 and 8 restate rules the
framework already owns, and the framework forbids duplication
(`plugin/skills/spec/SKILL.md:205-206`: "Cross-reference other documents
instead of duplicating their content — duplication drifts"). Their
existing homes, verified during triage:

  - `plugin/skills/spec/references/template-authoring-standards.md`
    v0.12 — "### Line Length" (line 42) owns check 6; "## Metadata
    (Frontmatter)" (line 54) owns check 1; "## Slug Conventions"
    (line 62 onward) owns check 2; "### Reference Validation"
    (line 433) owns check 8.
  - `plugin/skills/spec/references/cross-document-references.md` — owns
    how a `[[slug]]` reference resolves (check 8).

So the new checklist SHALL cite those documents by `[[slug]]` for checks
1/2/3/6/8, and state in its own voice only what is genuinely new:
check 4 (EARS coverage), check 5 (compound modal verbs), check 7
(instruction blocks deleted).

The pattern to follow is stated by the sibling checklist at
`plugin/skills/spec/references/blueprint-readiness-checklist.md:27`:
"The checks are defined only here — the skills reference this document
rather than restating it, so authoring and grooming can never disagree
about what 'groomable' means."

New-file frontmatter must satisfy template-authoring-standards: title,
description, slug, type: standards, status, updated_at, version.

Gate to respect: `scripts/check-skills.sh:132-136` fails any file under
`plugin/skills/*/references/` that exceeds 100 lines without a line
matching `^#+ Contents` or `^Sections \(complete`. Keep the new file
under 100 lines, or give it a `## Contents` section.

Version bumps:
  - `plugin/skills/spec/SKILL.md` frontmatter `version: "1.3"` -> "1.4"
    (MINOR).
  - `plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` "0.7.0" -> "0.8.0" (MINOR).
    Shared with agent-plugins-8bx and agent-plugins-x8t — set the value
    idempotently; do not bump a second time if it already reads 0.8.0.

CONSTRAINT: do not weaken or widen
`plugin/skills/spec/references/blueprint-readiness-checklist.md`. It
gates groomability, which is a separate concern, and the source RFC
lists leaving it alone as an explicit Non-Goal.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A new numbered step exists in the Authoring Workflow of
      plugin/skills/spec/SKILL.md, positioned after "Preflight feature
      blueprints" and before the retro-offer step, and its wording
      applies to every document type rather than to feature blueprints
      only.
- [ ] plugin/skills/spec/references/document-readiness-checklist.md
      exists and covers all eight checks listed in Design.
- [ ] For checks 1, 2, 3, 6 and 8 the new file cites
      [[template-authoring-standards]] / [[cross-document-references]]
      instead of restating their rules; checks 4, 5 and 7 are stated in
      the new file's own voice.
- [ ] The new file is under 100 lines, or carries a "## Contents"
      section.
- [ ] The new file's frontmatter declares title, description, slug,
      type: standards, status, updated_at and version.
- [ ] Every line added or changed in every touched file is at most 80
      characters.
- [ ] plugin/skills/spec/SKILL.md frontmatter version reads "1.4".
- [ ] plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json version reads "0.8.0".
- [ ] plugin/skills/spec/references/blueprint-readiness-checklist.md is
      byte-identical to its pre-change state.
- [ ] scripts/check-skills.sh exits 0.

metadata.tier_reason: authors a NEW normative framework document plus a workflow step that gates every document type; must judge which of 8 checks to cite vs. state in its own voice across two other standards docs, and a restating checklist would create exactly the duplication-drift the framework forbids. Well-specified but invention-heavy with framework-wide blast radius.

title: Close out the RFC triage: write the three Resolutions, disclose self-authorship, retire and log, bump the plugin
description:
Three RFCs were triaged on 2026-08-10 and their approved proposals filed as the
beads in this epic. `triage-rfc`'s steps 5–7 are therefore **mid-flight, not
done**: the implementation was sequenced into beads (step 5's "Sequence before
you edit" branch, which applies here because more than five proposals were
approved and most of them change one file), but the Resolutions, the retro log
and the version bumps are all still outstanding.

The RFCs, all in `rfcs/inbox/bead-bonanza/`:

- `rfc-self-close-ceremony-and-finding-harvest.md` — P1 adopted, P2 adopted,
  **P3 rejected as written** (refuted by `agent-plugins-t09`'s measurement;
  replaced by a bead carrying the constraints measurement supports), P4 adopted.
- `rfc-self-run-dir-discoverability-and-orchestrator-recovery.md` — P1–P5 all
  adopted; P5 merged with the sibling RFC's P2.
- `rfc-self-silent-ceremony-loss-and-the-stale-twin.md` — P1–P6 all adopted;
  P3 adopted but **re-planned**, because as written it was a single restructure
  of a file whose contents were about to change.

Leaving them in the inbox with no Resolution is the failure mode `triage-rfc`
names directly: "Silent rejection (no Resolution entry) — the next retro
re-derives and re-proposes the same idea." Three self-authored RFCs re-derived
from the same runs would be indistinguishable from independent corroboration,
which is precisely the signal the accumulation model reads.

This bead is the closure. It runs last.
design:
Per `triage-rfc` steps 5–7, once the epic's beads have landed.

**1. Write each RFC's Resolution.** Per proposal, never per RFC: outcome
(adopted / adopted-with-refinement + the refinement / rejected + rationale), the
bead that carried it, date, files changed, version bumps. Specifically:

- Record **P3 of the close-ceremony RFC as rejected**, naming
  `agent-plugins-t09`'s measurement as the refutation and the replacement bead.
  A rejection is a first-class outcome and is recorded so the idea is not
  relitigated without new evidence.
- Record **P3 of the stale-twin RFC as adopted-with-refinement**, the refinement
  being that it was decomposed into the extraction beads plus a measurement
  gate, because the content-reducing work had to precede it.
- Record the **merge** of the run-dir RFC's P5 with the stale-twin RFC's P2 in
  both Resolutions, so neither reads as unaddressed.

**2. Disclose self-authorship.** All three carry `origin: self`. Each Resolution
SHALL state that the RFC was authored and triaged within this repository, and
name any proposal that ratifies a decision its own author made. Note that each
RFC's `model` field is withheld under the session policy tracked by
`rfcs/inbox/retro-skill/rfc-self-retro-skill-withheld-model.md`, so
same-agent authorship cannot be confirmed or excluded — say that rather than
implying independence. An approval recorded without the disclosure reads later
as independent corroboration when there was none.

**3. Record the triage-originated changes.** Several beads in this epic came
from the review session rather than from any RFC — the pre-flight script, the
DoR amendment and the Phase 2 deletion, C4-based bucketing, the sprint retro,
and the lost-deferral correction. Table each as a `T` row in the Resolution of
the RFC whose evidence prompted it (or of the RFC triaged alongside it where
none did), marked triage-originated, per step 4's convention. Do not number them
into any RFC's `P` sequence.

**4. Number and retire.** Rename each to
`rfcs/rfc-<nnnn>-<short-description>.md` using the next free numbers (0013
onward — 0010 and 0011 are referenced but absent from `rfcs/retired/`; confirm

title: RFC-0004's deferral bead agent-plugins-1a9 was never persisted: correct the record and audit for other lost deferrals
description:
`rfcs/retired/rfc-0004-bead-bonanza-dispatch-and-script-contracts.md`'s
Resolution records a deferral:

> | P5 — record the gate profile's baseline verdict | **deferred** ->
> `agent-plugins-1a9`, `theme:gate-baseline`. Entangled with an unsettled
> question: the standard states the body budget in CHARACTERS while
> `check-skills.sh` measures LINES. Bead is `deferred` /
> `blocked-needs-info` pending that decision. | `agent-plugins-1a9` |

**That bead does not exist.** Measured 2026-08-10:

```
$ bd show agent-plugins-1a9
Error fetching agent-plugins-1a9: no issue found matching "agent-plugins-1a9"
$ grep -c '1a9' .beads/issues.jsonl
0
$ git log --all --oneline -S "agent-plugins-1a9" -- .beads/issues.jsonl
(no output)
$ bd label list-all | grep gate-baseline
(no output)
```

It never reached `.beads/issues.jsonl` on any branch, and the theme label was
never created. The deferral was lost with the container it was created in —
exactly the failure mode `CLAUDE.md` warns about ("A bead that is not in
`.beads/issues.jsonl` when the container dies is gone").

Two consequences, and the second is the one that matters.

**The record is false.** A retired RFC's Resolution names a bead a reader can
follow, and following it fails. Anyone auditing what happened to P5 concludes
the work is tracked when it is not.

**The accumulation model leaked.** `triage-rfc`'s deferral mechanism exists so
that recurrence across projects surfaces priority: a deferred bead is the
accumulation signal, and step 2's dedupe reads deferred beads to detect it. A
deferral that evaporates cannot accumulate. This one recurred twice —
`rfc-self-silent-ceremony-loss-and-the-stale-twin.md` P3 re-proposes gate
baselining, and a hardening bead re-proposed the units fix — and neither
recurrence was detected as one, because there was nothing to dedupe against.

The blocking question is now answerable: the binding constraint is the
5,000-token skill re-injection cap, so the threshold is a size, and the units
question resolves to bytes. Both halves of the original deferral are now live
beads. What is left is the record and the leak.


## Steps to Reproduce

1. Read the Resolution table in
   `rfcs/retired/rfc-0004-bead-bonanza-dispatch-and-script-contracts.md` and
   note the bead cited for P5: `agent-plugins-1a9`.
2. Follow it:

```
$ bd show agent-plugins-1a9
Error fetching agent-plugins-1a9: no issue found matching "agent-plugins-1a9"
$ grep -c '1a9' .beads/issues.jsonl
0
$ git log --all --oneline -S "agent-plugins-1a9" -- .beads/issues.jsonl
(no output)
$ bd label list-all | grep gate-baseline
(no output)
```

**Expected:** a deferred bead a reader can follow, and a theme label carrying
the accumulation count.
**Actual:** neither exists, in any branch's database or history.
design:
**1. Correct RFC-0004's Resolution.** Do not rewrite the deferral row's history
— add a dated note beneath the table:

> **2026-08-10:** bead `agent-plugins-1a9` was never persisted to
> `.beads/issues.jsonl` and does not exist in any branch's database; the
> deferral was lost with its container. The blocking question (body budget in
> characters vs `check-skills.sh` measuring lines) is resolved: the binding
> constraint is the 5,000-token re-injection cap, so the threshold is a size in
> bytes. Both halves of P5 are now tracked by <the check-skills bead> and <the
> pre-flight bead, which captures the gate baseline>.

Editing a retired RFC's Resolution to record a later correction is within
`triage-rfc`'s conventions — triage writes the Resolution; it is the Evidence
and Proposals sections that are the reporter's testimony and must not be
touched.

**2. Create the `theme:gate-baseline` label** on the two beads that inherit the
deferral, so the accumulation signal exists going forward. This is the point of
theme labels — a bead without one is invisible to the model.

**3. Audit for other lost deferrals.** This one was found by accident while
deduping, not by looking. Enumerate every bead id cited in a Resolution across
`rfcs/retired/*.md` and check each resolves:

```bash
grep -ohE 'agent-plugins-[a-z0-9]+' rfcs/retired/*.md | sort -u \
  | while read id; do bd show "$id" >/dev/null 2>&1 || echo "MISSING: $id"; done
```

Report every miss. Recreate a lost bead only where its proposal is still live;
where the work has since landed by another route, note that in the Resolution
instead. Do not mass-recreate — an unread bead resurrected as an open work item
is worse than an honest note that it was lost.

**4. Note the systemic cause once, where it will be read.** `CLAUDE.md` already
documents that only `.beads/issues.jsonl` carries beads between containers, and
that `bd export` must be run and committed before a session ends. This incident
is evidence that the documented practice was not followed at least once. Add the
observation to the existing section — a dated line, not a rewrite — rather than
creating a new warning: the guidance was correct and present; what it lacked was
a verification step.

Deliberately out of scope: adding an automated check that every Resolution's
cited beads resolve. It is a reasonable idea and it is a different bead; propose
it if the audit in step 3 finds more than one miss.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] RFC-0004's Resolution carries a dated note recording that agent-plugins-1a9 was never persisted, that the units question is resolved to bytes, and which beads now carry both halves
- [ ] The RFC's Evidence and Proposals sections are unchanged
- [ ] theme:gate-baseline exists on the beads inheriting the deferral
- [ ] Every bead id cited in a Resolution across rfcs/retired/ was checked for existence and every miss is reported
- [ ] Any recreated bead corresponds to a proposal that is still live; work that landed by another route is noted in its Resolution instead
- [ ] CLAUDE.md's beads-persistence section carries a dated line recording this incident, without rewriting the existing guidance

title: bb-close-bead.sh writes no trailers, and the amend that adds them strands the sha the ledger recorded
description:
`bb-close-bead.sh` commits with the bare subject `{ID} P{PRIORITY} {TITLE}` and
no body. A repository whose convention requires commit trailers — this one
requires `Co-Authored-By` and `Claude-Session` — must therefore
`git commit --amend` after the script's step 6, which **rewrites the commit**.
The subagent template's step 7 then records the pre-amend sha.

Observed on `9kb.10` in run `1786121603-ri`:

```
$ tail -1 agent-plugins-9kb.10.progress.jsonl
{"phase":"committed","sha":"14f0be3"}
$ git log --oneline --grep=9kb.10        # landing commit on the branch
875593a ...
$ git merge-base --is-ancestor 14f0be3 HEAD; echo $?
1                                        # dangling pre-amend object
```

Every bead in that run that pushed trailers has the same drift. The recorded sha
names an object that is not on the branch, which breaks the two things that
depend on it: the acceptance check being added in a sibling bead, and the
recovery procedure's `committed -> verify the sha` step.

Repro: run `bb-close-bead.sh`, `git commit --amend` to add any trailer, compare
the ledger's `sha` to `git rev-parse HEAD`.

Two independent fixes, both needed. The trailer support removes the amend; the
sha-source change makes the ledger correct even when something else rewrites the
commit.


## Steps to Reproduce

1. On a branch, run the close ceremony for any bead:
   `bb-close-bead.sh <id> <priority> "<title>" <retro-file> <paths>`
2. Note the short sha it prints.
3. Add any commit trailer the way a project convention requires:
   `git commit --amend` (append `Co-Authored-By:` or similar).
4. Follow the subagent template's step 7, which records the sha the script
   printed: `bb-progress.sh "$RUN_DIR" <id> committed sha=<printed sha>`
5. Compare: `git merge-base --is-ancestor <printed sha> HEAD; echo $?`

**Expected:** the recorded sha is the landing commit.
**Actual:** exit 1 — the recorded sha is a dangling pre-amend object.
Observed on `9kb.10`: ledger `14f0be3`, landing commit `875593a`.
design:
**1. `bb-close-bead.sh --trailers-file <path>`.** Contents are appended to the
commit message body, separated by a blank line. Optional: WHERE a project has no
trailer convention the flag is omitted and behaviour is unchanged. Update the
script's own header usage line and the interface published in SKILL.md — the
skill states the script is authoritative on disagreement, so both must move
together.

Phase 0 resolves the trailers file once per run, alongside the gate profile,
from the project's stated commit convention, and passes it into every dispatch
prompt. Where the convention lives in `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md` prose rather than a
file, Phase 0 writes it to `$RUN_DIR/trailers.txt` and passes that. Note that
this repository's trailers include a session URL that varies per session, so the
file is per-run, not committed.

**2. Read the sha from the branch, not from the script's stdout.** Change step 7
of every affected template in `references/subagent-prompts.md`:

> 7. `bb-progress.sh "$RUN_DIR" {ID} committed sha=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)`
>    — read it from the branch, not from the script's printout, so any rewrite
>    between the two steps cannot desync it.

This is the fix that holds even when the amend comes from somewhere the skill
does not control — a hook, a signing step, a project convention added later. Do
it regardless of whether the trailers flag is used.

**3. Reorder so no amend is needed.** With trailers passed in, step 6 closes and
commits with trailers already in place and step 7's sha is final. Confirm the
per-bead, fast-lane and shared-surface templates all reflect the new ordering —
the fast-lane and shared-surface templates reference the per-bead workflow rather
than restating it, so check that the reference still resolves correctly.

**Do not** change `bb-progress.sh` or `bb-verify-skip.sh`. Do not change the
close ceremony's four ordering constraints — this adds a message body, not a
reordering.

Verify by running the repro: close a probe bead with `--trailers-file`, confirm
the trailers are on the commit, confirm no amend was needed, and confirm
`git merge-base --is-ancestor <ledger sha> HEAD` exits 0. Record the observed
output in the retro.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] bb-close-bead.sh accepts an optional --trailers-file whose contents are appended to the commit body after a blank line
- [ ] Omitting the flag leaves behaviour byte-identical to today
- [ ] The script header's usage line and the interface published in SKILL.md both show the new flag
- [ ] Phase 0 resolves the trailers file once per run and passes it into every dispatch prompt
- [ ] Every subagent template reads the committed sha from 'git rev-parse --short HEAD', not from the script's printout
- [ ] The per-bead, fast-lane and shared-surface templates all reflect the no-amend ordering
- [ ] bb-progress.sh and bb-verify-skip.sh are unchanged, and the close ceremony's four ordering constraints are unchanged
- [ ] The repro was run: trailers present, no amend needed, and 'git merge-base --is-ancestor <ledger sha> HEAD' exits 0, with the output recorded in the retro

metadata.tier_reason: Shell flag, template reordering across three prompts, and a repro to run. Touching the close ceremony means the ordering constraints must be preserved exactly.

Measured: git log -1 --format='%(trailers:key=Claude-Session,valueonly)' 223da6c returns EMPTY, so git does not parse them as trailers at all, while the same command on the five sibling commits returns the value. title: Define the resume path for an interrupted bead: a WIP commit is the one sanctioned exception to one-commit-per-bead
description:
`SKILL.md:718-722` states the invariant absolutely:

> **One commit per bead, always.** Every closed bead = exactly one commit on the
> branch.

There is no interruption case, so an interrupted bead has no legal move. Bead
`9kb.5` in run `1786121603-ri` landed in two commits — `e3f2777` "WIP
agent-plugins-9kb.5 (PREG): profile registration, snapshots pending" at 20:52,
then `bb7ecc3` at 21:06. The agent improvised a commit the invariant forbids
rather than following a stated resume path, because there is none. The
alternative available to it was losing the work.

The invariant is right and should stay. What it needs is the one sanctioned
exception, plus the rule that restores the invariant at close time — so that
"one commit per bead" remains true of every *closed* bead, which is what the
invariant is actually protecting (bisectability, and a clean revert per bead).
design:
Append to the one-commit-per-bead principle (which moves to
`references/operating-principles.md` — put it there and leave the rule's
one-line summary above the cap):

> **WHEN a bead is interrupted mid-implementation** and its work must be
> persisted before the agent stops, commit it with a subject prefixed
> `WIP <bead-id>` and leave the bead `in_progress`. A WIP commit is the one
> sanctioned exception, and it is **not** a close: no `bd update --status
> closed`, no retro, no `committed` progress event. Emit
> `bb-progress.sh "$RUN_DIR" <id> blocked reason="interrupted; WIP <sha>"` so
> the ledger records where it stopped.
>
> The agent that resumes the bead finishes the work, then squashes its own
> commit together with every `WIP <bead-id>` commit on the branch into the
> single landing commit before running the close ceremony. Record the
> interruption and the squash in the bead's retro.

Two things the resuming agent needs and the rule must supply:

1. **How to find them.** `git log --oneline --grep="^WIP <bead-id>"` on the
   branch. State it, because the resuming agent may be a different agent with no
   knowledge that a WIP exists — which is the whole situation being handled.
2. **The safety boundary.** Squashing rewrites history, so it is permitted only
   while the WIP commits are unpushed. WHERE a WIP commit has already been
   pushed, do not rewrite it: land the completion as a normal second commit,
   note the two-commit landing in the retro, and report it in Phase 4. The
   existing prohibition on force-pushing a published branch
   (`references/subagent-prompts.md`, Constraints) is not weakened by this bead.

Also add the recovery counterpart in `references/recovery.md`: a bead whose
ledger tail is `blocked` with an `interrupted` reason is resumable, not failed —
distinct from the existing "last phase was `implementing` or earlier -> stash and
surface" path, which assumes nothing was committed.

Cross-check `bb-close-bead.sh` for anything that would reject a tree containing
prior WIP commits for the same bead. It refuses to run without a retro file and
with nothing staged; neither should fire here, but confirm rather than assume.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The one-commit-per-bead rule carries an interruption case permitting a 'WIP <bead-id>' commit with the bead left in_progress
- [ ] The exception explicitly excludes closing, writing a retro, and emitting a committed event, and requires a blocked event naming the WIP sha
- [ ] The resume rule requires squashing all WIP commits for the bead into the single landing commit before the close ceremony
- [ ] The rule states how a fresh agent finds prior WIP commits
- [ ] The rule forbids rewriting a pushed WIP commit and defines the two-commit fallback, without weakening the force-push prohibition
- [ ] references/recovery.md distinguishes an interrupted-with-WIP bead from the stash-and-surface path
- [ ] bb-close-bead.sh was checked against a tree containing a prior WIP commit for the same bead and the result recorded

metadata.tier_reason: One sanctioned exception plus its restore rule; the pushed-WIP boundary is the only judgment and it is stated.

title: Back the in-session Monitor with a durable out-of-session trigger, and cancel it in Phase 4
description:
The skill mandates a wake mechanism that cannot survive the failure it exists to
report.

`SKILL.md:612-615` and `references/recovery.md:62` require the orchestrator to
arm a `Monitor` on a subagent's progress JSONL for anything running past five
minutes. Run `1786121603-ri` complied: Monitor `btnrafelq` was armed and
relaying correctly — `gates-passed` at 18:27:46, `committed` at 18:29:20. At
18:33:08.850 a user interrupt landed. At 18:33:08.862 and .863 two notifications
were **enqueued**:

> `status: killed — Agent "Batch: RES + PREG (9kb.4, 9kb.5)" was stopped by user`
> `status: killed — Monitor "batch RES+PREG phase events" stopped`

Neither was ever dequeued — every prior notification in that transcript shows an
enqueue followed ~50ms later by a dequeue. The same interrupt stopped the
orchestrator, so the mechanism that would have reported the death died with it.
Result: 2h16m of silence while the UI showed the task running.

The underlying mechanics, which are easy to get wrong from the inside:

| Mechanism | Starts a turn | Carries state into it | Survives interrupt/clear |
|---|---|---|---|
| Task notification (child finishes or dies) | yes | no | **no** |
| `Monitor` on a file | yes | yes — the matched event | **no** — dies with the turn |
| Scheduled trigger (`send_later`, cron) | yes | yes — arbitrary text | **yes** — server-side |
| SessionStart / UserPromptSubmit hook | **no** | yes | n/a — enriches an existing turn |

A durable sprint needs one mechanism that wakes fast and one that survives. This
run had only the first kind, twice.

Verified in the same session: a `send_later` trigger armed at 21:13Z fired
correctly at 21:31Z and drove a full recovery check. Its binding is to the cloud
`persistent_session_id`, not to a local transcript, which is why it survives
clears and interrupts.
design:
Amend the Monitor rule (`SKILL.md:612-615`, and the matching text at
`references/recovery.md:62`) to require both mechanisms and to say why:

> **Monitor any subagent past 5 minutes, and back it with a durable trigger.**
> The `Monitor` is the fast path: it is in-session, and it dies with the turn
> that armed it, so it cannot report its own death. Before the first dispatch of
> a run, also arm a recurring out-of-session check-in — a cron/recurring trigger
> where the harness offers one, otherwise a re-armed `send_later` — at 15–30
> minute intervals, whose message states the RUN_DIR path and points at the
> orchestrator-recovery procedure. Cancel it in Phase 4 when the run drains. A
> run whose only wake mechanism is in-session cannot survive an interrupt that
> lands on the orchestrator.

Details that matter:

- **Prefer a recurring trigger over a one-shot** for a run of unknown length: it
  re-arms itself instead of depending on the agent to remember, and the agent
  forgetting is the failure mode being defended against.
- **The trigger's message must be self-contained.** It wakes a turn that may hold
  no run context. It carries the RUN_DIR path, the epic id, and one line
  instructing the woken agent to run the orchestrator-recovery procedure rather
  than to "check on the run".
- **Cancelling is part of Phase 4**, not optional tidy-up: a trigger left armed
  after the run drains wakes an agent into a finished sprint, which trains the
  reader to ignore it.
- **Do not have the check-in key liveness on `bd list --status in_progress`.**
  The improvised heartbeat in the observed run did exactly that and would have
  concluded "nothing in flight" while an agent edited twelve files. Point it at
  the recovery procedure's git-mtime rule instead.

Where the harness offers neither trigger mechanism, say so once at run start —
the run proceeds, but the user should know the only wake path is in-session.

Depends on the RUN_DIR pointer and the recovery procedure existing, since the
trigger's message points at both.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] SKILL.md and references/recovery.md both require a Monitor AND a durable trigger, and state that a Monitor cannot report its own death
- [ ] A recurring trigger is preferred over a one-shot, with the reason given
- [ ] The trigger message is required to be self-contained: RUN_DIR, epic id, and an instruction to run the orchestrator-recovery procedure
- [ ] Cancelling the trigger is a required Phase 4 step
- [ ] The guidance forbids keying the check-in's liveness test on bd claim status and points at the git-mtime rule
- [ ] The no-trigger-available case is handled with a one-line notice at run start

metadata.tier_reason: Guidance edit with the wording drafted; the mechanics table in the description settles the reasoning.

title: Make the mixed-tier batching rule decidable, and record deliberate over-routes in the Phase 4 report
description:
`SKILL.md:475-478` resolves a bucket whose beads carry different capability
tiers:

> prefer bucketing beads that share a tier. When a bucket mixes tiers, run the
> whole batch subagent at the **highest** tier among its members — never run a
> bead below its tier. If honoring that would drag several cheap beads up, split
> the bucket.

"Several" is the entire rule, and it is undefined. Worse, the rule omits the
quantity that actually decides the trade: what a full gate run costs. Batching
exists to avoid repeated full `<test>` runs — that is the stated reason in the
same phase ("Each 'plain sequential' bead burns a full `<test>` run (often 10+
min). Batching N beads in one subagent saves N-1 of those.") — so where the gate
suite finishes in seconds, batching buys nothing and the correct tier should
simply win.

Observed in the 23-bead run: the decision came up twice with opposite outcomes
and no principle to appeal to. `bge.9` (`light`) was batched with a `standard`
bead and ran a tier above its assignment; `bge.8` (`advanced`) and `bge.11`
(`standard`) were split rather than batched. Both calls were defensible, neither
was derivable from the skill. The deciding factor turned out to be gate-suite
cost — seconds in that repo — which the rule never mentions.

There is a reporting gap alongside it. Phase 4's escalation table captures
*under*-routing only: a bead escalated because its tier was too low shows up, a
bead deliberately run a tier high does not. `SKILL.md:670-679` already says
over-routing "succeeds silently and is paid for on every run" — and then
provides no place to record the instances the orchestrator knowingly created.
design:
Replace the final sentence of `SKILL.md:478` with a decidable rule:

> Split the bucket WHEN the number of beads dragged above their tier exceeds
> one, OR when any bead would be dragged more than one tier. Weigh that against
> what batching saves: batching exists to avoid repeated full `<test>` runs, so
> WHERE the gate suite completes in seconds the saving is negligible and the
> correct tier wins; WHERE it takes minutes, one bead one tier high is the
> cheaper error.

The gate-suite duration is knowable at this point — `pre-flight-check.sh`
captures the gate baseline, and its timing is the input this rule needs. Have
the rule name that source rather than asking the orchestrator to estimate.

**Add the over-routing record.** In the Phase 4 report specification (which
moves to `references/final-report.md` — sequence accordingly), add deliberate
over-routes alongside the escalation table:

> | Bead | Assigned | Ran at | Why raised |
> |------|----------|--------|------------|
> | demo-9h0 | light | standard | batched with a standard bead; gate suite ~11 min |
>
> State `none` explicitly when there were none. Together with the escalation
> table this is the run's complete routing evidence: escalations expose
> under-routing, this exposes over-routing, and `groom-beads`' retro loop needs
> both to recalibrate the rubric.

Keep the existing asymmetry note — a zero-escalation run is not a clean bill of
health — and cross-reference the new table from it, since the new table is now
the direct answer to the question that note raises.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The split rule is stated numerically: more than one bead dragged above tier, or any bead dragged more than one tier
- [ ] The rule weighs the split against gate-suite duration and names the pre-flight gate baseline as the source of that duration
- [ ] The Phase 4 report specification carries an over-routing table with bead, assigned tier, tier it ran at, and why
- [ ] 'none' is required explicitly when there were no over-routes
- [ ] The existing zero-escalation asymmetry note cross-references the new table
- [ ] The tier vocabulary and the escalation ladder are unchanged

title: Replace worktree-parallel's skip conditions with the measured git-side constraints (RFC P3 rejected as written)
description:
`SKILL.md:438-441` gives worktree-parallel exactly two skip conditions:

> Skip this mode if there are <3 isolated beads (parallelism savings don't pay)
> or if the beads aren't actually isolated (you'll just hit merge conflicts).

Neither covers the constraints that actually bite, so the mode has been skipped
for wrong reasons and would fail for unstated ones.

**The received proposal on this is wrong and is rejected.**
`rfcs/inbox/bead-bonanza/rfc-self-close-ceremony-and-finding-harvest.md` P3
proposes excluding worktree-parallel in the beads backend entirely, reasoning
that `.beads/embeddeddolt/` is gitignored so "a worktree cannot see the tracker
database at all". Bead `agent-plugins-t09` measured it and the inference does
not hold: `bd` 1.1.2 resolves the shared database through git's common
directory. From a worktree with `BEADS_DIR` unset, `bd where` prints the main
checkout's path, `bd worktree info` reports the main repo, `bd list` returns the
identical issue set, and no `embeddeddolt/` or redirect file is created in the
worktree. Concurrency was tested separately in an isolated repo: 8 concurrent
`bd create` -> 8 successes; 4 concurrent `bd label add` on one issue -> all four
present; 4 concurrent writes across main + 3 worktrees -> all landed, export
byte-valid. The premise (gitignored) is true; the conclusion drawn from it was
never run.

Triage decision, 2026-08-10: **P3 rejected as written**, replaced by the
constraints that measurement supports. This bead is that replacement. It is
sequenced after the two beads that establish the facts — the ledger correction
and the `worktree.baseRef` investigation — because writing skip conditions
before those land would repeat exactly the error being corrected.
design:
Replace `SKILL.md:438-441`'s skip conditions with the measured set. Final
wording depends on the `worktree.baseRef` bead's outcome, which is why this bead
waits on it; draft below.

**Keep:** <3 isolated beads; beads not actually isolated (now decided by C4
blast radius as well as file overlap — see the bucketing bead).

> - **A worktree's own `.beads/issues.jsonl` goes stale while `git status` reads

> - **`export.git-add: true` stages into the main index from writes issued

>   that each commit `.beads/issues.jsonl` produce an N-way textual conflict in

>   WHEN worktrees branch from the default branch rather than session HEAD, any

>   foundation, and the mode SHALL be skipped for any wave whose beads build on

title: Contract and .strata sources duplicate rationale prose near-verbatim; establish which is authoritative
description:
Raised by the repository owner in review of PR #16 against
`specs/contracts/contract-specs-configuration.md:8`: "How much of this contract
is already defined by `.strata` source files? Are we duplicating documentation
from those files rather than referencing it?"

**Measured: yes, in the rationale prose, near-verbatim.**

`schemas/config.strata` is 91 lines and **88% docstring by character count**
(2,490 of 2,844 chars). It is a prose document that happens to declare types.
The contract is 339 lines. The two carry the same argument in the same words.

`schemas/config.strata`:

> In particular there is no way to define a document type, register a block
> tag, or supply a schema from here. Those belong to the profile, and holding
> them back is what keeps the promise cheap: a key that was never public
> cannot be broken by changing it. Promotion runs one way and is additive, so
> a repository that never wrote a key it could not write is unaffected by a
> later version that lets it.

`specs/contracts/contract-specs-configuration.md:85-90`:

> There is deliberately no way to override a document type, add one, register
> a fenced block tag, or supply a schema. Those are the internal surface, and
> holding them back is what keeps v1's compatibility promise cheap: a key that
> was never public cannot be broken by changing it, and the framework's
> vocabulary is still moving. Promotion is one-way and additive — a repository
> that never wrote a key it could not write is unaffected by a later version
> that lets it.

Two copies of one argument, drifting independently. The risk is not the
duplication itself but that a future change updates one and not the other, and
neither reader can tell which is authoritative.

**Not all of the contract duplicates.** Sections that have no counterpart in
the `.strata` sources and are the contract's real content: Guarantees /
Resolution (`:206`), Checking the configuration (`:223`), Operational
Expectations (`:258`), Versioning and Change Policy (`:276`), Key Decisions
(`:299`), Open Questions (`:304`). The overlap is concentrated in Overview
(`:19`) and the two Specification subsections (`:62`, `:91`).
design:
This is a question about where prose lives across the whole spec corpus, not
just this one contract — treat the decision as setting a convention.

**Establish the rule first.** Which artifact is authoritative for what:

- The `.strata` source is authoritative for **shape** — what properties exist,
  their types and constraints. That is mechanically enforced and generated.
- The contract should be authoritative for **promise** — compatibility, the
  resolution order, what checking does, what a consumer may rely on across
  versions. None of that is expressible in a schema.
- **Rationale prose is the contested middle.** "Why the public surface is
  small" currently lives in both.

**Then check what the toolchain can actually do** before choosing:

1. Does the docs pipeline render `.strata` docstrings into a referencable
   page? If a contract can link to a generated page for the shape, the
   duplication is removable. If not, some restatement is unavoidable and the
   rule becomes "state the promise, summarise the shape in one line, link to
   the source".
2. Does `spec check` have any way to detect prose drift between a `.strata`
   docstring and a document that restates it? Probably not — note it if so,
   since that would make the convention enforceable rather than advisory.

**Then apply it to this contract**: keep Guarantees, Operational Expectations,
Versioning, Key Decisions and Open Questions; reduce Overview and the two
Specification subsections to the promise plus a pointer, with the worked
`specs.toml` example retained only if the generated docs do not carry an
equivalent.

**Do not simply delete the prose from one side.** The contract's version is
slightly richer ("and the framework's vocabulary is still moving"). Whichever
side loses the passage, the surviving copy should be the union of the two.

Check the other contracts and the `schemas/*.strata` sources for the same
pattern before closing — `finding.strata`, `frontmatter.strata`,
`index.strata`, `profile.strata` and `vocabulary.strata` are all candidates.

title: Ledger entries must cite the command that proved them, including claims of sufficiency
description:
Both repos keep an "environmental-failure ledger" in their agent instructions
(`/home/user/strata/AGENTS.md`, and per-run copies in `dispatch.md`) so agents
stop re-diagnosing the same failures. The mechanism is sound and worth keeping.
The problem is that entries are admitted on reasoning rather than on a run.

**Five ledger-shaped claims failed in one session (2026-08-07/08).** Four were
recorded as durable instructions; all five were plausible and none had been
executed:

| Claim | Reality | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| "worktree-parallel is unusable for any bead that runs `bd`" (`strata/AGENTS.md:493`) | False. `bd` resolves the shared DB via git's common directory; `bd where` from a worktree prints the main checkout's path. Concurrent writes lock-serialize cleanly. | Every bead of a 12-bead run dispatched sequentially |
| "release assets 404 through the proxy" (`strata/AGENTS.md:199-206`) | Half false. The browser URL 404s; `api.github.com/.../releases/assets/<id>` returns 200 with 3,141,712 bytes | A route dismissed without test |
| "`command -v bd strata`" verifies provisioning (`docs/session-bootstrap.md`) | Insufficient. Both binaries were present and `strata` was the build that silently destroys the schema | ~18 min plus three `cargo build --release` cycles |
| "`9kb.9.progress.jsonl` has never existed" (retro, since corrected) | False. Complete seven-event trail; the retro had read a stale snapshot | A published RFC with a refuted premise |
| "strata-lang/strata is public, so auth was never the bottleneck" (bead `bkf`, since corrected) | False. `private: True`. The reachability test ran with session credentials present | A viable PAT approach dismissed |

The common shape: **a true premise, a plausible inference, and no command.**
`.beads/embeddeddolt/` really is gitignored; the binaries really were on PATH;
the browser URL really does 404. Every inference drawn from those was wrong.

Note the third and fifth rows are not claims of impossibility — they are
claims of sufficiency and of access, which ran fine and proved nothing. A rule
that only gates "X is impossible" would miss them.
design:
Add a single admission rule to the ledger convention in both repos'
agent-instruction files, and to the `bead-bonanza` dispatch-plan template that
copies ledger entries into prompts.

**Proposed wording:**

> **Ledger entries are admitted on evidence, not on reasoning.** Every entry
> asserting what is impossible, unnecessary, unreachable, or already-verified
> SHALL cite the command that was run and the output observed. Run it first;
> record it after. A true premise plus a plausible inference is not evidence —
> five entries admitted that way in one session were wrong, and four of them
> had been copied into durable instructions where they kept costing capability.
>
> Applies equally to a claim of sufficiency ("this check verifies the install")
> as to a claim of impossibility — a check that runs clean and proves nothing
> is the harder case, because nothing about it looks like a failure.
>
> Where an entry cannot be tested cheaply, record it as **unverified** in the
> entry itself and say what would settle it. An entry marked unverified is
> useful; one that reads as settled and is not, is worse than absent.

**Also add the corollary about scope**, which is what made the two
credential-confounded claims wrong:

> State the conditions the command ran under when they could change the result
> — attached repositories, credentials present in the environment, warm versus
> cold caches, the toolchain version. A reachability or permission test run
> inside a session that already holds a grant measures the grant, not the
> capability.

**Where it goes:**
- `/home/user/strata/AGENTS.md` — at the head of the environmental-failure
  ledger section
- `/home/user/agent-plugins/CLAUDE.md` — wherever the equivalent guidance sits
- `plugin/skills/bead-bonanza` — the dispatch-plan ledger section, so per-run
  ledgers inherit the rule

**Then audit the existing entries** in both files against it. Any entry with no
cited command is either re-verified now or marked unverified. Expect several:
the two corrected this session were found by accident, not by audit.

Keep the existing trap-warning convention intact — this adds an admission bar,
it does not license deleting entries that carry forward-looking engineering
memory.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The admission rule is present at the head of the environmental-failure ledger section in strata's AGENTS.md and in this repo's equivalent guidance
- [ ] The rule covers claims of sufficiency and access, not only claims of impossibility
- [ ] The rule requires stating the conditions a command ran under when they could change the result (attached repos, credentials, cache warmth, toolchain version)
- [ ] The rule defines 'unverified' as a first-class entry state, with what would settle it
- [ ] The bead-bonanza dispatch-plan ledger section carries the same rule so per-run ledgers inherit it
- [ ] Every existing ledger entry in both files was audited; each is either re-verified with its command cited or marked unverified
- [ ] No entry was deleted to satisfy the rule — the trap-warning convention is intact

metadata.tier_reason: Admission rule with drafted wording, then an audit of existing entries across two repos — the audit is the volume.

title: Move provisioning into the per-environment setup script, pinned by commit, with a verification that detects a wrong binary
description:
This session's SessionStart hook never ran, and the fallback that made it look
like it had was actively dangerous.

**Verified the hook did not fire.** `/root/.claude/session-env/<this-session>/`
is EMPTY, where a prior single-root session's directory contains
`sessionstart-hook-0.sh` with the hook's two exports verbatim. `env | grep
BD_` returns nothing (`session-start.sh:100-102,120-122` exports
`BD_DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1`). Zero `[session-start]` log lines anywhere in the
transcript. Zero `bd prime` invocations.

**Root cause: two attached repos.** Claude Code registers hooks only from the
project root. Attaching `agent-plugins` and `strata` as siblings makes
`/home/user` the root, and `/home/user/.claude` does not exist — so
`agent-plugins/.claude/settings.json` is never read. Attaching ONE repo makes
that repo the root and the hook fires: verified against session `d49cdb0c`
(Aug 1, agent-plugins sole root), whose `session-env` directory contains the
hook's exports.

**Why nothing looked broken.** `bd` and `strata` were on PATH anyway, because
the container image was snapshotted on Aug 1 from that single-root session.
`/usr/local/bin/bd` mtime Jul 26; `~/.cache/strata-cli/build.log` ends Aug 1
with nothing appended since.

**And the snapshot carried `strata @ 44c1955`** — the build that per
`.bonanza/1786121603-ri/decisions.md` silently DESTROYS the schema (every
document type emits `"properties": {}`, 2202 lines -> 1326) while reporting
success. The session's first check at 16:53:34 read exactly that commit, then
spent ~18 minutes and three `cargo build --release` cycles isolating it.

**So the documented verification recipe is unsound.**
`docs/session-bootstrap.md` says the symptom is "no `bd` on PATH and no
`strata` binary" and verifies with `command -v bd strata`. This session had
both binaries present and one silently wrong. A presence check returns success
on a broken install — and note this is a claim of SUFFICIENCY that ran fine
and proved nothing, which is a harder case to catch than a claim of
impossibility.

## Correction — the PAT route is viable, and an earlier draft of this bead said otherwise

An earlier version of this description asserted that "strata-lang/strata is
public and already clones and fetches unauthenticated through the proxy, so
auth was never the bottleneck". **That is false.**

```
$ curl -sS https://api.github.com/repos/strata-lang/strata
  private: True
  visibility: private
$ env | grep -i token
  GH_TOKEN=<set>
  GITHUB_TOKEN=<set>
```

The reachability test that produced the claim ran inside a session where the
repo had already been attached by the user, with GitHub credentials in the
environment and the agent proxy brokering the request. It measured the
session's existing grant, not public access. Auth IS the bottleneck for an
unattached session, and a PAT is the mechanism that removes it.

Release GRANULARITY remains a separate, real objection to downloading a
prebuilt binary: the only published release is v0.7.0, fourteen commits behind
the only correct build (`840f9ba`), and `allowAdditionalProperties` — which
`schemas/strata.config.json:7` sets — does not exist at that tag. Releases are
tagged by version and `strata --version` reports `0.7.0` for all four relevant
builds, so no release artifact can express "I need v0.7.0-14". **Clone and
build at a pinned commit; do not download a release.**
design:
The durable fix is the per-environment setup script described in
`docs/session-bootstrap.md` — it runs before Claude Code launches and does not
depend on the project root. Combined with the correction above, the target
setup is:

**Attach ONE repo (`agent-plugins`) so the project root carries `.claude/` and
hooks fire. Obtain strata via a PAT-authenticated clone in the setup script.**

That gets the hook back AND drops the second root — the two problems have the
same cause and the same fix.

## Setup script requirements

1. **Clone strata with a PAT** stored as an environment secret. The repo is
   private; an unattached session has no credential for it. Use
   `git clone --filter=blob:none` — the blobless clone preserves per-file
   history, which `sync-strata-docs.sh` needs (it stamps each vendored file
   with `git -C "$STRATA_SRC" log -1 --format='%H' -- <path>`).
2. **Clone to `~/.cache/strata-src`, not `/opt/strata-src`.**
   `scripts/sync-strata-docs.sh:62` searches `$STRATA_SRC_DIR`,
   `$REPO_ROOT/../strata`, `$HOME/strata`, `$HOME/.cache/strata-src` —
   `/opt/strata-src` is on none of them. With no match, `--check` prints
   `RESULT: SKIP (nothing to compare against).` and **exits 0**: a gate
   reporting green while comparing against nothing. The current draft in
   `docs/session-bootstrap.md` clones to `/opt/strata-src`.
3. **`git checkout <pin>` before `cargo build`.** The draft builds at whatever
   HEAD is; HEAD is currently `ce18d66`, which hard-errors with
   `/go/optionalStyle: unknown property`. Today's correct pin is `840f9ba`.
   Store it in a repo-owned file (e.g. `strata-pin`) that BOTH the setup script
   and `.claude/hooks/session-start.sh` read, so the two provisioning paths
   cannot drift.
4. **Write the pin to `~/.cache/strata-cli/built-commit`** so the hook's warm
   path agrees instead of rebuilding.
5. **Replace the verification recipe** in `docs/session-bootstrap.md`. Instead
   of `command -v bd strata`, compare `cat ~/.cache/strata-cli/built-commit`
   against the pin. Note that a container image can carry provisioning from a
   prior single-root session, so presence proves nothing about correctness.
6. **Keep the shape assertion.** `scripts/generate-schemas.sh`'s `required`-list
   check is version-independent and catches the silent-destruction class a pin
   cannot (a pin only helps until it is bumped). Both halves are needed — this
   is `decisions.md`'s "2 + 3".

## Verify before recording

Per the ledger convention bead: run each command in a session with only
`agent-plugins` attached and confirm (a) the hook fires — check
`/root/.claude/session-env/<session>/` is non-empty — and (b)
`sync-strata-docs.sh --check` reports a real comparison rather than `SKIP`.
Record the observed output in the retro. Do not write the recipe into
`docs/session-bootstrap.md` before it has been run.

## Adjacent correction to fold in

`/home/user/strata/AGENTS.md:199-206` claims release assets are unreachable
through the proxy. Half wrong: the browser URL
(`github.com/.../releases/download/...`) returns 404, but the API endpoint
(`api.github.com/repos/.../releases/assets/<id>` with
`Accept: application/octet-stream`) returns 200 with 3,141,712 bytes of valid
gzip — verified twice. Correct the entry, while noting the release route stays
rejected for the granularity reason above. NOTE: that test also ran with
session credentials present, so re-verify it against a PAT-only session before
recording the correction.

## Separate hazard, same setup surface

`strata/.claude/skills/` carries sf-plugin skills vendored at **0.14.0** while
`agent-plugins/plugin` is **0.15.0**, and `spec/SKILL.md` differs (315 vs 333
lines). agent-plugins won the tie-break this session (verified from skill-load
base directories) but that ordering is not a guarantee. Moving to a single
attached repo makes this moot for co-attached sessions; if the vendored copies
stay, re-run `scripts/vendor-sf-skills.sh` in strata.

environment-provisioning work; it carried the label because it was found during
a bead-bonanza run, not because it changes the skill. It is not part of the

title: bd remember is write-only: bd export drops memories, and CLAUDE.md blames the import side
description:
`bd remember` is a write-only hole in this project: nothing written to it has
ever survived a container.

Measured today:

```
$ grep -c '"_type":"memory"' .beads/issues.jsonl
0                                  # of 95 records, all "_type":"issue"
$ bd export --help
  Memories (from 'bd remember') are excluded by default ...
  Use --include-memories or --all to include
$ bd import --help
  Memory records (lines with "_type":"memory") are automatically detected
  and imported ... 'bd export | bd import' a full round-trip
```

This is not inert plumbing. `plugin/skills/groom-beads/SKILL.md:334` instructs
agents to capture grooming-miss patterns as `bd remember "<insight>"`, and
`:103` tells a later agent to "skim existing `bd remember` insights". **A
shipped skill writes into a store guaranteed to be wiped, and another step
reads from the empty result.** The SessionStart hook's `bd prime --hook-json`
would inject those memories if any existed.

`CLAUDE.md:143-145` also misattributes the loss:

> - `bd remember` memories are **excluded** from `bd export` by default, and
>   the session-start hook imports without `--all`. Durable context belongs in
>   an issue description, not a memory.

The first clause is right; the second is wrong — `bd import` auto-detects
memory lines and has no `--all` flag at all. The loss is 100% on the export
side. Anyone debugging this from the current text goes to the wrong end.

Context: this was the only genuine persistence gap found when evaluating
third-party memory tooling. Every hosted option is proxy-403'd here
(`api.mem0.ai`, `api.getzep.com` both fail exactly as `bd dolt push` does) and
every local option must commit its store to git, reinventing
`.beads/issues.jsonl` with a weaker schema. Fixing this flag is the cheaper
and better win.
design:
Three edits, all small.

1. **Change the mandated export** wherever it appears — `CLAUDE.md`'s "Before
   ending a session" block, and any companion guidance in
   `.claude/hooks/session-start.sh`:

   ```bash
   bd export --include-memories > .beads/issues.jsonl
   ```

   Note `bd config` exposes only `export.auto|path|interval|git-add` — there is
   no key that makes AUTO-export include memories. So the explicit end-of-session
   export is the only path, which the docs already mandate for the deletion
   reason. This adds a second reason to the same rule.

2. **Correct `CLAUDE.md:143-145`.** Replace the import clause with the measured
   behaviour: memories are excluded by `bd export` unless `--include-memories`
   or `--all` is passed; `bd import` auto-detects and imports them with no flag.
   Once the export carries them, drop or soften "durable context belongs in an
   issue description, not a memory" — that advice exists only to work around
   this bug.

3. **Verify the round trip end to end** before closing: `bd remember` a probe,
   run the corrected export, confirm the record appears in
   `.beads/issues.jsonl`, then confirm `bd import` of that file restores it.
   State the observed result in the retro.

Check whether the same stale advice appears in `/home/user/strata/CLAUDE.md`
or `AGENTS.md` and fix it there too if so.

title: Relational reference checks read documents off disk on the warm single-document path
description:
`cli/core/corpus/check.go:131-136` says the relational reference checks are
"a lookup over data already in memory, not a second corpus walk". On a warm
corpus that is not true, and the single-document path pays for it.

`retiredTargetFindings` and `pairingIncompleteFindings` call `c.document()`
(`check.go:218`, `check.go:264`). `Corpus.document` (`corpus.go:789-806`)
returns from the `c.docs` cache when present, but on a warm corpus — where
`c.docs` is not populated by a walk, because there was no walk — it falls
through to `readDocument`, which opens and parses the file off disk.

Two consequences:

1. The comment misdescribes the code, which is the kind of drift AGENTS.md
   says to fix in the same change that notices it.
2. The relational checks run corpus-wide even when `--only` narrows the report
   to one document: they are computed at `check.go:136-138`, before the
   narrowing loop at `check.go:143-150`. So a single-document check does one
   disk read and parse per retired-target and per pairing reference in the
   whole corpus, and AC-SPEC-009.2's single-document budget scales with the
   corpus's relational-reference count rather than staying constant.

Not yet measured on this corpus — the budget test's current margin is the
first thing to establish.
design:
Establish the size of the problem before changing structure:

1. Measure. Count the retired-target and pairing references in this corpus and
   time `spec check <one file>` warm against `spec check` warm. If the
   single-document path is already close to AC-SPEC-009.2's budget, this is
   urgent; if the corpus has a handful of such references, it is a comment fix
   plus a guard test.
2. Decide where the work belongs. The counterpart-declared fact the pairing
   check reads (`targetDoc.Property(pairing.Counterpart)`) and the status the
   retired-target check reads are both properties the index could carry, which
   would make the check a genuine in-memory lookup and make the comment true.
   That is the structural fix; it costs an index schema change and a rebuild.
3. Cheaper alternative: skip the relational checks for references whose
   findings the `--only` narrowing would discard anyway. This keeps the index
   as-is and makes the single-document cost proportional to one document's
   references. Note it changes nothing for the corpus-wide path.

Fix the misleading comment in whichever change lands, not as separate cleanup.
