---

## Retro

### Approach

Read the three blueprints in full first, then read the code before
touching a word of any of them: `cli/core/corpus/{corpus,check,cache,
hash,profile}.go`, `cli/core/{span,frontmatter,schemaregistry,finding,
numbering,specindex,schema}`, `cli/profile/profile.go` and its two test
files, and the `cli/cmd` command tree. Two things that turned out to
matter were only visible from the code and not from any blueprint or
bead: `cli/core` contains **no** `markdown` or `references` package (so
two of the eight components in module-document-core's own diagram are
unbuilt), and `cli/core/schema/spec-model.schema.json` is **generated**
from `schemas/*.strata` rather than authored inside the profile module.

Every claim I wrote is anchored to something I read. Where I asserted a
number I measured it: the "70ms cold, 26ms warm" figure in
container-spec-cli's Data section is a timed run of `/tmp/spec check`
over this repository's 26 documents, not an estimate.

I also cross-checked the blueprint frontmatter against the compiled
schema (`python3` over `cli/core/schema/spec-model.schema.json`) before
editing frontmatter, which is what caught the `version` problem below.

Baseline and final state of the targeted gate are identical: `/tmp/spec
check` reports **no findings** over 26 indexed documents, all four
checks passed, before and after.

### Implicit decisions I made

1. **Amend rather than rewrite.** Every blueprint already carried
   **Built** paragraphs folded in by the individual code deltas. I kept
   the existing design prose as the statement of intent and attached
   reconciliation to it, rather than rewriting sections wholesale. The
   one exception is module-spec-profile's Document Types component,
   which the bead explicitly required removed.

2. **Version numbers: `0.1` → `0.2` on the two module blueprints.** The
   feature added no new capability to these documents' subjects; it made
   them describe a shipped implementation. A minor bump reads that
   correctly, and both were still at their authoring version.

3. **container-spec-cli got no `version` bump, because it cannot have
   one.** See the first finding below — the container-blueprint schema
   declares no `version` property and sets `additionalProperties:
   false`, so adding one would have made the corpus check fail. I moved
   `updated_at` to `2026-08-05T00:00:00Z` instead, on all three
   documents.

4. **Unbuilt components are marked, not deleted.** Markdown Structure
   and References (document-core) and Element Records and Lifecycle
   Rules (spec-profile) each keep their design section and gain an
   explicit "**Not yet built**" paragraph naming the absent package,
   plus `(planned)` in their diagram technology label. Deleting them
   would have discarded design work the bead did not ask me to discard;
   leaving them unmarked would have been exactly the contradiction the
   bead exists to remove. Removal was reserved for Document Types, which
   the bead named.

5. **Open Questions resolved in place, with `- [x]` and a **Resolved**
   lead**, rather than being deleted or moved to a decisions section.
   The reasoning that made the question worth asking is the most useful
   part of the resolution, so the question text stays above the answer.

6. **Where a decision belongs to another document, I linked rather than
   duplicated it.** The index-contract deferral is written out in full
   in container-spec-cli's Open Questions (which owns it) and referenced
   from module-document-core's Corpus section, so the two cannot drift
   into disagreeing.

### Where the built system differed from the planned design

| Planned | Built | Recorded as |
|---|---|---|
| Markdown Structure and References as Go packages under `cli/core` | Neither exists; no markdown parser in `go.mod` at all | "**Not yet built**" paragraph in each component section; `(planned)` in the C4 diagram; a paragraph under the diagram naming which six of the eight are built; a qualifier on the relationship prose that names them |
| Profile registers a schema per document type via a Document Types "type registry" component | One embedded union schema plus a two-column slug/numbered table, all in one file (`cli/profile/profile.go`) | Component removed from module-spec-profile's diagram and body; replaced by a paragraph explaining what remains of it and why; Profile Registration's **Built** section gained the three-member table |
| Element Records / Lifecycle Rules implement `adr-008`'s record-XOR-link rule and supersession integrity | Neither registered; the status *vocabulary* is enforced (it is a schema constraint) but `superseded_by` resolution is not, because it needs the unbuilt References component | "**Not yet built**" paragraphs distinguishing the registered half from the unregistered half; Key Decisions entry for `adr-008` changed from "implements" to "will implement when it is built" |
| "The module SHALL NOT write to the filesystem outside a cache location the caller supplies" | There is no cache location — the emitted index *is* the cache; the only write is `corpus.Write` to `IndexPath` | Guarantee rewritten to "SHALL write exactly one artifact — the emitted index"; a paragraph after the Interface table records that the guarantee is narrower in fact than in statement |
| Cache invalidation open between mtime and content hash | Content hash, whole-index, over the same walk `Build` uses, excluding absolute paths, folding in workspace/schema/type-table/schema-version | Open Question marked resolved in module-document-core with the full argument; the mechanism written into container-spec-cli's Data section; the "rebuild the affected entries" guarantee corrected to plain "rebuild", since invalidation is whole-index |
| Index cache described as a thing separate from the emitted index | One artifact serves both roles; `index` writes it, `check`/`slug-exists`/`next-id` read it warm from the default path | **Built** paragraph in container-spec-cli's Data section, including what `--out` does (writes a consumer artifact, not a cache) |
| Byte offsets taken from the YAML parser | Re-derived by counting codepoints, because `goccy/go-yaml` reports codepoint-counted positions | Fifth pinned semantic in the Frontmatter component, including that no ASCII fixture can expose it and that the self-application gate is what found it |
| Reads via ordinary file I/O | Every read goes through an `os.Root` handle and normalizes CRLF to LF at that one choke point | New first pinned semantic in the Corpus component, with the deliberate consequence (byte offsets index normalized text; line/column unaffected) spelled out |
| `goldmark` among the module's implementation choices | Not a dependency | Key Decisions entry for `adr-015` qualified: first three in use, `goldmark` arrives with Markdown Structure |
| `samber/oops` "deferred to implementation" | Implementation shipped without it; structure lives in the generated `FindingDetail` union, internal errors use `fmt.Errorf` | Open Question annotated with what shipped, restating the question as "whether to adopt" rather than "whether to start with" |
| Self-application gate runs over `docs/` | Runs over `specs/`, resolved from the test file's own location, and fails outright if `specs.toml`/`specs/` are absent | module-spec-profile's Verification gates corrected, including why the vacuous-pass guard exists |
| Fixture-corpus snapshot tests under `cli/core/testdata/` | Snapshot cases live at `cli/testdata/cases/`; no `cli/core/testdata` exists. No property tests over the delimiter scanner either — `cli/core/span` has table-driven edge-case tests | module-document-core's Verification gates rewritten to name the paths and suites that exist |
| Profile registers patterns transcribed from the prefix registry | Patterns grounded in this repository's actual corpus; three deliberate divergences (feature blueprints, guides, RFC numbering) | Recorded in module-spec-profile's Interface section and in the Cross-Cutting Standards note about what "derive from the reference documents" now means |

The check loop the bead flagged (`agent-plugins-9d1`, discovered during
implementation and owned by no original delta) was **already** described
in module-document-core — `Corpus.Check`/`CheckFor` in the Corpus
**Built** section, and the `Rel(corpus, schema, ...)` edge in the
diagram. bge.9d1 folded it correctly; nothing was needed here beyond
verifying it against `cli/core/corpus/check.go`.

### Surprises

- **Two of eight components in module-document-core's own diagram were
  never built, and nothing in the bead said so.** The Design section
  enumerated the six built ones by name, which reads as a checklist of
  confirmations rather than as an implicit statement that the other two
  are unbuilt. It was the AC — "no blueprint statement contradicts the
  shipped code" — that pulled them into scope, not the enumeration.

- **A statement can be stale in the direction of over-promising even
  when every delta did its job.** `goldmark`, `samber/oops`, the
  `docs/` corpus root, `cli/core/testdata/` — four separate stale
  statements, none of which belonged to any code delta's surface, all
  of which contradicted the tree. This is exactly the residue the bead
  was created to sweep, and it was larger than the Design section's

- **The schema fought the acceptance criterion.** "version bumped on
  each" is unsatisfiable for a container blueprint under this
  framework's own frontmatter schema. The corpus check would have
  caught it, which is a good sign for the check, but the AC was written

- **Running the tool to measure it dirtied the tree.** `spec index`
  writes `specs/specs.json`, which is not gitignored, so timing the

title: Ship cross-compiled static binaries and CI
description:
# agent-plugins-bge.13 — Ship cross-compiled static binaries and CI

## DESCRIPTION

**Blueprint:** `specs/features/spec-index/spec-index-blueprint.md` — delta **BUILD**, section "Static binary and distribution in container-spec-cli (added)".
**FRD:** `specs/features/spec-index/spec-index-frd.md`.
**Delivery:** staged (stage 3 of 3); this feature's closure set is `bd list --label feature-spec-validation-cli`.

Ship the CLI as a per-platform statically linked binary that installs without
a runtime or network fetch, satisfying the portability and supply-chain
requirements an adopting security review turns on.

**CI exists but does not cover Go.** `.github/workflows/checks.yml` runs on
push and pull_request, but only the docs-corpus gates (`check-skills.sh`,
`sync-shared-references.sh --check`, `validate-corpus.py`). There is no Go
build/test job and no release matrix. This item adds those; it does not
create CI from nothing. (Corrected 2026-08-04: the work order's original
premise that the repository had no CI at all was already stale when written.)

**Open obligation — the `(manual)` markers.** The blueprint's AC Coverage
table declares AC-SPEC-009.4, 009.5 and 009.6 verified at *manual* level, but
`specs/features/spec-index/spec-index-frd.md` does **not** append the
`(manual)` marker to those three criteria. Per the AC traceability standards,
a criterion is exempt from the citation obligation only once the FRD records
that designation — so as written these three are simultaneously
un-citable-by-test and non-exempt. Resolve it in this item by one of:
(a) appending `(manual)` to those criteria in the FRD, which is the mechanical
consequence of the level the blueprint already approved; or (b) recording an
automated verification for them. Do not close this item leaving the
contradiction in place. Flagged at grooming time — see also the final DoD
item, which audits citations.

`agent-plugins-55q` ("ADR: release and distribution of CLI binaries") is open
in the tracker and directly relevant to this item, though the blueprint's
Tracker Reconciliation does not list it. Check it before choosing a
distribution mechanism.

## Retro

Before closing this item, record retro findings on this issue —
one `bd comment` per finding, prefixed `retro:` — following the
findings capture protocol in `rfcs/findings-capture.md`. Friction
only: what happened plus the item or spec text that caused it (or
the gap where guidance was missing). No analysis, no RFCs — the
plan's final DoD item runs the aggregated retro.


## DECISION (2026-08-04)

On the `(manual)` marker contradiction described above. Options considered:

- **Append `(manual)` to AC-SPEC-009.4/.5/.6 in the FRD — SELECTED.**
  Records in the FRD the verification level the blueprint already approved.
  A clerical fix, not a scope change: the three criteria become legitimately
  exempt from the citation obligation per
  `specs/standards/testing-standards.md` lines 266-268. This is RFC 0010 P3.
- Find automated verification for all three and move those rows off `manual`
  in the blueprint's AC Coverage table. Rejected for this run as materially
  more work than the bead was sized for.
- Leave unresolved and let the final DoD item flag it. Rejected: ships a
  known hole in AC traceability.

Implement the selected option as part of this bead: edit
`specs/features/spec-index/spec-index-frd.md` so each of AC-SPEC-009.4,
AC-SPEC-009.5 and AC-SPEC-009.6 carries the `(manual)` marker in the format
`frd-template.md` defines. Do not change what the criteria require.

## DESIGN

- The CLI runs on a machine with no language runtime, interpreter or package
  manager installed beyond the binary itself.
- Installation retrieves no executable content from the network, and the CLI
  is installable from at least one package registry that supports
  on-premises mirroring.
- The build produces the platform matrix by cross-compilation from a single
  source, and identical corpus content yields byte-identical output across
  Linux, macOS and Windows — in concert with the determinism the Corpus item
  implements.

Anchors: Go build/release configuration and CI under `.github/workflows`
(to be created).

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

- [ ] The binary runs in an image containing only a shell and the binary
      (**proves AC-SPEC-009.4**, manual).
- [ ] Installation retrieves no executable content from the network
      (**proves AC-SPEC-009.5**, manual).
- [ ] The CLI is installable from at least one registry supporting
      on-premises mirroring (**proves AC-SPEC-009.6**, manual).
- [ ] Identical corpus content yields byte-identical output on Linux, macOS
      and Windows, including a CRLF checkout on Windows (**proves
      AC-SPEC-009.7**, e2e).
- [ ] The platform matrix is produced by cross-compilation from a single
      source.
- [ ] CI exists under `.github/workflows` and runs the test suite.
- [ ] The `(manual)` marker contradiction described in Problem is resolved
      one way or the other, and the resolution is stated on this issue.
- [ ] Static binary and distribution are recorded in
      `specs/architecture/container-spec-cli.md`, delivered in this same
      change.

---

## Retro

### Approach taken

Five things shipped, in the order they became necessary rather than the
order the bead lists them.

**1. The `(manual)` markers (the baked-in DECISION).** Appended `(manual)`
to the criterion text of AC-SPEC-009.4, AC-SPEC-009.5 and AC-SPEC-009.6 in
`specs/features/spec-index/spec-index-frd.md`, in the position
`plugin/skills/spec/references/frd-template.md` defines ("append the marker
`(manual)` to the end of the criterion text") — at the end of the SHALL
sentence, before each criterion's `*Example:*` sub-bullet, which is part of
the criterion's illustration rather than its text. What the three criteria
require is unchanged. They are now legitimately exempt from the citation
obligation per `specs/standards/testing-standards.md` lines 266-268, which
is what the blueprint's AC Coverage table (`manual` on all three rows)
already assumed.

**2. AC-SPEC-009.7 — and the two defects that stood in its way.** The bead
said the determinism was already implemented in `cli/core/corpus` and that
my job was the assertion. Half true. Probing before writing the test:

- `check --json` output *was* byte-identical between an LF and a CRLF
  working tree — the criterion's normative text ("the same findings in the
  same order") held.
- The **index** was not. Span offsets moved (`offset: 11` → `12`,
  `length: 158` → `163`) and `input_hash` changed entirely, because both are
  functions of the file's bytes and a CRLF checkout genuinely has different
  bytes. That is the criterion's own worked example ("a corpus checked out
  with CRLF line endings on Windows yields byte-identical JSON output")
  failing.

Fixed at the single choke point that makes it a small change:
`readUnder` in `cli/core/corpus/corpus.go` now normalizes CRLF to LF, and
`scanCandidates` is the only walk in the package — both `Build` and
`Fingerprint` read through it, so the index's spans and the warm-cache
hash can never disagree about what a file is made of. It is a no-op on an
LF checkout, so no committed golden moved (verified by diffing pre- and
post-fix output on the same corpus).

**3. The vacuous snapshot harness.** With the fix in, I ran a negative
control — reverted the normalization and expected the new portability test
to fail. **It passed.** `cli/cmd/snapshot_test.go` resolved each case's
directory as a path relative to the package (`../testdata/cases/<name>`)
and then `os.Chdir`'d into a fresh `t.TempDir()` before reading
`expected/checks.log` and `expected/manifest.json`. After the chdir that
relative path resolved against the temp dir, missed, and hit the
`os.IsNotExist(err) { return }` branch that exists so a case can carry only
one of the two artifacts. **Every artifact comparison in the entire
snapshot suite was silently skipping.** Only the exit-status assertion was
live. Confirmed directly: replacing `index-default`'s committed
`manifest.json` with `{"corrupt":true}` and running `TestSnapshotCases`
reported `ok`.

Fixed with `filepath.Abs(dir)` before the chdir. This was not in scope, but
AC-SPEC-009.7's entire evidence rested on those comparisons being live, so
the bead could not be delivered around it. After the fix every committed
golden still matches — the vacuum had not masked any drift.

Then the negative control behaves: with the normalization reverted, four
cases fail under CRLF (`check-only`, `index-default`, `index-out-custom`,
`index-out-stdout`); with it restored, all pass. Corrupting either kind of
golden now fails its case in both suites.

**4. The portability test** — `cli/cmd/portability_test.go`, citing
`// AC: AC-SPEC-009.7`. It replays *every* existing snapshot case a second
time from a working tree it has itself rewritten to CRLF, holding the
result to the same committed artifacts. Reusing the existing cases rather
than adding a fixture means zero new golden-maintenance surface and no
second regeneration path. `runSnapshotCaseWith` in `snapshot_test.go` is
the seam (a `materialize func(src, dst string) error` parameter); the check
logic is shared, not copied, so the two runners cannot drift apart. Also
carries two tests of the CRLF fixture machinery itself and a guard against
a zero-case run reporting success.

The file's own header states plainly which half of the claim it is: the
*cross-platform* half is the CI matrix comparing three operating systems to
one committed set of expected bytes, which no single test process can
observe; the *cross-checkout* half is what this file does.

**5. `.gitattributes`, CI, and the release pipeline.** Detailed below.

### Implicit decisions, and why

- **A separate `.github/workflows/cli.yml` rather than more jobs in
  `checks.yml`.** `checks.yml` is one Linux runner needing only bash and
  python3; this needs a Go toolchain and three operating systems, and its
  failures mean something different. Two workflows keep the two signals
  legible. `checks.yml` was not touched.
- **No `paths:` filter on `cli.yml`.** A path-filtered workflow that is
  required for merge simply never reports on a PR outside its paths, which
  blocks the merge rather than passing it. Running the matrix on a docs-only
  commit is the price of avoiding that. Stated in the workflow's header.
- **`.gitattributes` with `* text=auto eol=lf`.** Forced by putting
  `windows-latest` in the matrix: Git's `core.autocrlf` default there would
  rewrite the committed `expected/*.json` goldens on checkout, and a
  repository whose expected artifacts arrive as CRLF cannot compare them to
  anything. This does not weaken AC-SPEC-009.7 — it is what makes it
  testable, since the CRLF checkout is reproduced synthetically on every
  platform by the portability test. Verified it causes no churn in this
  (already-LF) tree.
- **Platform matrix: six targets** — `linux`, `darwin`, `windows` × `amd64`,
  `arm64`. Covers `agent-plugins-55q`'s stated need (macOS, Linux, Windows)
  and adds arm64 because it is free with Go cross-compilation and is now the
  default Mac and a common CI runner.
- **`CGO_ENABLED=0`, `-trimpath`, `-ldflags="-s -w"`.** `CGO_ENABLED=0` is
  what makes each artifact one statically linked file with no libc to
  resolve, i.e. AC-SPEC-009.4. `-trimpath` keeps the builder's absolute
  paths out of the bytes. Archives are additionally built with
  `--sort=name --owner=0 --group=0 --numeric-owner --mtime='UTC 2020-01-01'`
  so the container is reproducible too, not just its contents.
- **Distribution: two channels, `go install` first.** The Go module proxy is
  the registry AC-SPEC-009.6 is satisfied by — it is mirrorable on premises
  (GOPROXY, Athens, Artifactory), and it needs no release artifact at all,
  which is a much stronger answer to AC-SPEC-009.5 than "download a tarball"
  because no install-time code runs either way. GitHub Releases are the
  second channel, for a machine with no Go toolchain. No third-party
  actions anywhere in either workflow (`gh` CLI, not `softprops/…`), which
  is the same supply-chain argument applied to the pipeline itself.
- **The entry point moved: `cli/main.go` → `cli/spec/main.go`.** Go names an
  installed binary after the directory holding its main package, so at the
  module root `go install …/cli@latest` would install a binary called `cli`.
  From `cli/spec/` it installs one called `spec`, which is the tool's name
  and the name its own cobra `Use` field already claims. Since `go install`
  is the AC-SPEC-009.6 answer, that name is part of the deliverable rather
  than cosmetic. Nothing referenced `cli/main.go` — checked the specs, the
  scripts and the workflows.
- **Release tags are `cli/vX.Y.Z`, not `vX.Y.Z`.** Forced by the above: the
  Go module lives in the repository's `cli/` subdirectory, and the module
  proxy resolves a subdirectory module's versions only from tags carrying
  that prefix. Channel 1 does not work without it. Recorded in the workflow
  header and in the container blueprint.
- **`no-runtime` job proves AC-SPEC-009.4 by running rather than
  asserting** — the static `linux/amd64` binary is executed inside
  `busybox:latest` (a shell, coreutils, musl, no package manager, no Go)
  against a committed snapshot corpus. The criterion stays `(manual)` per
  the DECISION; this is evidence in addition, not a re-levelling. Also
  asserts static linkage via `file` rather than `ldd`, because `ldd`'s
  wording for a static binary varies by distribution ("not a dynamic
  executable" vs "statically linked") and its exit status is not a signal.
- **The release workflow re-runs the gates.** A tag can be pushed at a
  commit whose `cli.yml` run never completed; a released binary that was
  never tested is worse than a slower release.
- **Container blueprint over ADR.** Recorded build flags, the two
  distribution channels, the entry-point/tag-prefix reasoning, and the
  read-path basis of AC-SPEC-009.7 in
  `specs/architecture/container-spec-cli.md` — which is what the bead's own
  final AC asks for. See the `agent-plugins-55q` note below for what was
  deliberately *not* decided.

### How `agent-plugins-55q` was handled

Read it first, as instructed. It asks for "an approved ADR plus a release
workflow producing macOS, Linux and Windows artifacts on a tagged release."
The workflow half is now built. The ADR half is not, and **55q is left
open**.

My choices do pre-empt three of the five questions 55q lists — the
platform/arch matrix, GitHub Releases as the channel, and the fetch story
for an agent session (`go install`, or download-and-unpack). I have recorded
them in the container blueprint as decisions rather than leaving them
undocumented, but they are provisional: 55q can overturn any of them, and
the blueprint text says so.

Two of 55q's questions I deliberately did **not** answer, because answering
them would have been guessing at policy rather than implementing a bead:

- **How binaries are versioned against the plugin version.** The binaries
  currently carry no version string at all, and there is no `--version`
  flag. Filed as **`agent-plugins-8i2`** (`discovered-from` bge.13,
  `related` 55q). Does not block this bead.
- **Whether checksums and signing apply.** `SHA256SUMS` ships with every
  release; nothing is signed. Signing is a key-custody decision, which is
  ADR territory.

### What I could NOT verify

- **Neither workflow was executed.** There is no network path to GitHub
  Actions runners from this environment. Both were validated statically
  (`yaml.safe_load` parses each; every `run:` block passes `bash -n` with
  `${{ }}` expressions neutralized) and by rehearsal of the parts that do
  not need a runner:
  - the six-target cross-compile, the archive/zip packaging and the
    `sha256sum` step were **run end to end locally** and produced six
    correct artifacts plus `SHA256SUMS`;
  - the static-linkage assertion was run locally (`file` reports
    `statically linked`);
  - the CLI was confirmed to work against a **read-only** corpus, which is
    what the container step mounts.
- **The `busybox` container step could not be run** — a Docker client is
  present in this container but there is no daemon
  (`/var/run/docker.sock` absent). The step is reasoned-correct and its
  inputs were verified, but it has never executed.
- **`go test ./...` has never run on macOS or Windows.** That is precisely
  what the new matrix is for, and it is the one part of AC-SPEC-009.7's
  evidence I am handing to CI rather than to a local run. If a case fails
  on the Windows leg on first run, the likely suspects are `os.OpenRoot`
  behavior and path handling in `cli/core/corpus`, not the portability test
  itself.
- **`gh release create` was not exercised.** No token, no repository to
  release into.

### Surprises

- The bead's premise that "the determinism AC-SPEC-009.7 asserts is already
  implemented" was **half wrong**, and the half that was wrong was invisible
  from the findings output — `check --json` was already identical across
  line endings while the index was not. A findings-only assertion would have
  passed and certified nothing.
- The snapshot suite has been asserting nothing but exit codes since
  `agent-plugins-bge.12` landed. That is the second time in this bead that
  a negative control caught something a green test run reported as fine. I
  would not have found it if I had trusted the passing test.
- Both of these were found by the same habit — deliberately breaking the
  implementation to confirm the test notices. Worth institutionalizing.

### Beads filed

- **`agent-plugins-0i6`** (P2, bug, `discovered-from` bge.13) — the
  residual half of the harness defect: `checkChecksLog` and `checkManifest`
  still treat a *missing* golden identically to "this case carries only the
  other artifact", so a renamed or deleted expected file still passes
  silently. A case should declare which artifacts it carries. Does not
  block this bead; the path-resolution defect that made it universal is
  fixed here.
- **`agent-plugins-8i2`** (P2, `discovered-from` bge.13, `related` 55q) —
  `spec --version` and version stamping on released binaries.

### Files changed

- `cli/core/corpus/corpus.go` — CRLF normalization at the read choke point
- `cli/cmd/snapshot_test.go` — absolute case path (the vacuum fix) + the
  `runSnapshotCaseWith` seam
- `cli/cmd/portability_test.go` — **new**, AC-SPEC-009.7 evidence
- `cli/spec/main.go` — **moved** from `cli/main.go`
- `.gitattributes` — **new**
- `.github/workflows/cli.yml` — **new**
- `.github/workflows/release.yml` — **new**
- `specs/features/spec-index/spec-index-frd.md` — `(manual)` markers
- `specs/architecture/container-spec-cli.md` — build, distribution,
  entry-point and reproducibility record
- `AGENTS.md` — "What CI runs", and the `.gitattributes` rationale

### Gate results

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `cd cli && gofmt -l .` | clean (no output) |
| `scripts/check-skills.sh` | PASS — `0 error(s), 1 warning(s)` (the known-red baseline, unchanged) |
| `cd cli && go vet ./...` | pass |
| `cd cli && go build ./...` | pass |
| `scripts/check-skills.sh --strict` | exit 1 on the pre-existing 859-line warning — baseline, no new findings |
| `scripts/sync-shared-references.sh --check` | all 11 current |
| `scripts/sync-strata-docs.sh --check` | all 3 match |
| `cd cli && go test ./...` | all packages ok |
| `scripts/generate-schemas.sh --check` | up to date |
| `scripts/validate-corpus.py` (CI) | 24 documents, 0 findings |
| `spec check` (self-application) | the one expected `plan` finding on the blueprint (`agent-plugins-tff`), nothing new |

- The build produces the platform matrix by cross-compilation from a single

title: triage-rfc: rule for versioning a changed file that has no version property (RFC P2)
description:
## Problem

`triage-rfc` step 5 instructs the agent to bump versions, and every
verb presupposes a predecessor. It gives no rule for a changed file
that carries no version property at all.

`.claude/skills/triage-rfc/SKILL.md:182-190`:

    - Bump the version of every changed template (instruction-block
      `Version:`), skill (frontmatter `version`), and standard
      (frontmatter `version`) per [[template-authoring-standards]].
      **Bump each file exactly once for the whole triage, no matter how
      many proposals changed it** — ...

## Evidence (inlined — do not rely on the RFC being at hand)

Observed in the triage run of 2026-08-01, model claude-opus-5.

`plugin/skills/spec/references/c4-guide.md` and
`plugin/skills/spec/references/ears-guide.md` had no `version` field —
the absence was itself one of the things that run was fixing. With no
rule available, the agent wrote `version: "0.2"` into `c4-guide.md`,
reasoning that the file was also receiving a content change and so
should land above its initial value, then reversed itself in a second
edit within the same run to `version: "0.1"`, on the ground that `0.2`
implies a `0.1` that a reader could diff against and none ever existed.
Both guides shipped `0.1`. The reversal is two consecutive edits to one
line in that session.

This is not cosmetic. Step 1's provenance check is version-keyed
(SKILL.md:66-67: "compare the cited skill/template/standard versions
against the current ones"), so a version implying a predecessor that
never existed makes the "already fixed?" question unanswerable for that
file.

Source: rfcs/inbox/triage-rfc/rfc-self-triage-rfc-evidence-completeness.md,
proposal P2 (severity snag, origin self, runs_observed 1).
design:
Append to the version-bump bullet in step 5, after the existing
sentence ending "verify the bump after the final change to that file,
never before.", continuing the same 5-space bullet-body indentation:

     WHEN a changed file carries no version property at all, do not
     bump — add one at `0.1`, and let this triage's change land inside
     that first version. A higher initial value implies a predecessor a
     reader could diff against; for a file that has never been
     versioned there is none, and step 1's provenance check would then
     be asking about a version that never existed. Place the property
     per [[frontmatter-standards]].

Do NOT bump the skill version in this bead.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The step-5 version bullet states that a file with no version property gets 0.1 rather than a bump
- [ ] It gives the reason (a higher initial value implies a predecessor that never existed)
- [ ] It points at [[frontmatter-standards]] for placement
- [ ] Every line added is at most 80 characters
- [ ] The skill frontmatter version is NOT changed by this bead
notes: Tier: light. tier_reason: a single append to the end of one existing bullet with the wording supplied; no other step references it and no cross-file coordination is needed. No C4 component is affected.
close_reason: Step 5 version bullet now covers a changed file with no version property (add 0.1, do not bump).

title: triage-rfc: admit triage-originated changes to step 4 and the Resolution (RFC P3)
description:
## Problem

`triage-rfc` step 4 and the Resolution format both assume every change
originates as a proposal in a received RFC, so a change triage itself
originates has no id, no table row and no outcome slot.

`.claude/skills/triage-rfc/SKILL.md:127-128`:

    4. **Present the recommendation and STOP for approval.** One table:
       proposal, classification, one-line rationale, files touched.

`SKILL.md:225-228` (the Resolution bullet) is likewise per-proposal:
"per-proposal outcome (adopted / adopted-with-refinement + the
refinement / deferred + bead id / rejected + rationale)".

## Evidence (inlined — do not rely on the RFC being at hand)

Observed in the triage run of 2026-08-01, model claude-opus-5.

That run adopted one change no RFC proposed: adding a `version`
property to `plugin/skills/spec/references/c4-guide.md` and
`ears-guide.md`. It was not a proposal — both RFCs had recorded it
under *Considered and Not Proposed*, RFC 0007 explicitly asking for "a
sweep of all guides rather than two one-line fixes".

With no rule to follow, the agent invented a row id `X1` outside the
`P` numbering, annotated it "(your call — not a proposal)", and then at
Resolution time invented a section heading "**Also adopted, outside
this RFC's proposals**" because no per-proposal row could hold it. Two
inventions in one run for one change.

The same gap recurred immediately: the following triage run took a
change reported directly by the human (see the sibling bead on the
already-implemented wording), which likewise had no id or row until one
was improvised.

Source: rfcs/inbox/triage-rfc/rfc-self-triage-rfc-evidence-completeness.md,
proposal P3 (severity snag, origin self, runs_observed 1).
design:
Two edits.

   classification, one-line rationale, files touched." and before
   "Implement nothing before the human approves", insert at 3-space

   A triage MAY originate a change no RFC proposed — one the evidence
   implies, or an item an RFC recorded under Considered and Not

title: triage-rfc: make already-implemented vs reject-already-addressed distinguishable (triage T1)
description:
## Problem

`.claude/skills/triage-rfc/SKILL.md:120-126` defines the
`already-implemented` classification and distinguishes it from
`reject — already addressed` with a single clause: "which is for a
proposal whose premise no longer holds". A human reader of the skill
reported that this does not convey the distinction, because in BOTH
cases the change is already present in the tree, so "the premise no
longer holds" appears to describe both.

Current text at SKILL.md:120-126:

    - **already-implemented** — the proposal is sound and its change is
      already present in the tree, landed by earlier work rather than by
      this triage. Distinct from `reject — already addressed`, which is
      for a proposal whose premise no longer holds: this one was right
      and nothing about it is being turned down. Record it in the
      Resolution as "adopted — already implemented", name where the
      change lives, and bump nothing.

## Evidence (inlined — do not rely on the RFC being at hand)

Reported directly by the repository owner on 2026-08-01, quoting
SKILL.md:122 and stating: "This does not make it clear (to me) what the
distinction between `reject - already addressed` and `adopted - already
implemented`."

This is a triage-originated work order (id T1), not a proposal from a
received RFC. It has no reporting RFC; the reporter is the human gate.

The distinction that the text should convey, and currently does not:
both outcomes mean the change is already in the tree, but they differ
in whether triage is ruling on the proposal's MERITS at all.
`adopted — already implemented` affirms the proposal was correct;
`reject — already addressed` takes no position, because the thing the
proposal targeted no longer exists. The consequence is load-bearing at
step 2, which reads prior Resolutions during dedupe: "adopted" means
settled, do not relitigate; "rejected — already addressed" means only
that the evidence was stale, so the same idea with fresh evidence gets
a fresh hearing.
design:
Replace the `already-implemented` bullet at SKILL.md:120-126 with:

   - **already-implemented** — the proposal is sound and its change is
     already present in the tree, landed by earlier work rather than by
     this triage. Record it in the Resolution as "adopted — already
     implemented", name where the change lives, and bump nothing.

     The test against `reject — already addressed` is whether triage is
     ruling on the proposal's merits at all. Use **already-implemented**
     WHEN you would have adopted it had the tree been untouched: the
     proposal was right, and this triage says so. Use **reject —
     already addressed** WHEN there is nothing to rule on — the text it
     quotes is gone or rewritten, so its premise fails and triage takes
     no position on whether the idea was ever good.

     The difference is load-bearing at step 2, which reads prior
     Resolutions. "Adopted" tells a future triage the idea is settled
     and should not be relitigated; "rejected — already addressed"
     tells it only that the evidence was stale, so the same idea backed
     by fresh evidence gets a fresh hearing.

Keep the bullet in place in step 3's list; do not reorder the
classifications. Do NOT bump the skill version in this bead.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The already-implemented bullet states the merits test (would you have adopted it had the tree been untouched)
- [ ] It states what reject — already addressed means instead (nothing to rule on; premise fails)
- [ ] It names the step-2 dedupe consequence for both outcomes
- [ ] Every line added is at most 80 characters
- [ ] The skill frontmatter version is NOT changed by this bead
notes: Tier: light. tier_reason: a single self-contained bullet replacement with the full text supplied and no interaction with other steps; the only judgment is preserving list indentation. No C4 component is affected.
close_reason: already-implemented bullet now states the merits test, what reject-already-addressed means instead, and the step-2 dedupe consequence for both.

title: No merge strategy for .beads/issues.jsonl — beads created on two branches will conflict
description:
`.beads/issues.jsonl` is the only carrier of issues between sessions and branches in this project (see the 'How beads persist in THIS project' section of CLAUDE.md). There is no `.gitattributes` in the repo, so git merges it as ordinary text.

Two branches that each create beads produce overlapping line-level edits in one file. Git will report a conflict, and the natural resolutions are both wrong: taking one side drops the other branch's issues, and a careless union can duplicate ids or interleave a partial record.

The failure is silent in the worst case — a conflict resolved by 'keep mine' loses issues that were correctly exported and committed, which is exactly the loss the export discipline exists to prevent.

## Options to evaluate
- A `.gitattributes` union merge driver for the file. Cheap, but union can produce two lines with the same id when both branches touched one issue, so it needs an id-dedupe pass afterwards.
- A custom merge driver that parses JSONL, keys by id, and prefers the higher `updated_at`. Correct, but needs a script every clone can run.
- Regenerate from the database after merge rather than merging the file: resolve by taking either side, then `bd import` both versions and `bd export` fresh. Uses beads' own conflict handling.
- Whether beads upstream ships a documented driver for this — check before building one.
acceptance_criteria: A documented, tested procedure for merging two branches that both added beads, with no issue lost and no duplicate id in the resulting .beads/issues.jsonl

title: ADR: release and distribution of CLI binaries
description:
The user confirmed (2026-07-31) that the CLI is internal for now but needs a CI workflow producing release artifacts for macOS, Linux and Windows.

Reconciled at the retirement of feature-spec-validation-cli (agent-plugins-bge.16). Left OPEN deliberately — this is a note, not a close.

The BUILD delta (agent-plugins-bge.13) shipped answers to three of the five questions in this issue's description: the platform/arch matrix, cross-compilation from a single source, and GitHub Releases as the channel. What remains genuinely undecided and still belongs here is (a) how an agent session obtains the binary, given this repository is distributed by clone via .claude-plugin/marketplace.json — a session needs either a fetch step or a build step, and neither is chosen; and (b) whether checksums or signing apply.

So the scope of this issue has narrowed rather than closed. Whoever picks it up should rewrite the description against what bge.13 actually shipped before deciding, rather than re-deciding the settled three. Its sibling agent-plugins-8i2 (spec --version and version stamping on released binaries) is open for the same reason and should probably be decided in the same sitting.

title: Index: model references as a separate edge collection, not only object properties
description:
Architectural input for the index-schema ADR (not yet written). Raised in PR #4 review of the FRD, 2026-07-31, explicitly flagged as 'not a comment for the FRD, but an architectural one for later'.

## The proposal

The index should collect the domain's model objects — specs
('documents'), systems, containers, components, and eventually features
— AND separately build a collection of REFERENCES that behave like
edges in a graph rather than like members of the objects they connect.
Each reference carries the file and span where it occurs.

Rationale given: this makes references queryable independently of the
objects. 'What points at adr-007?' becomes an edge query rather than a
scan over every object's properties.

This does not mean relationships never live inside objects. Some
belong there — a 'component' object might carry an injected
'container' property naming its parent. The proposal is specifically
about references that occur INSIDE document bodies: those are better
modelled as edges.

## Why it is not in the FRD

The FRD (docs/frds/FRD-spec-validation-cli.md) states WHAT the index
must contain, and AC-SPEC-002.1 and AC-SPEC-002.5 already require
outbound and inbound references. HOW the index is shaped — one
collection of objects with embedded arrays, versus objects plus a
separate edge collection — is a schema design decision, and the FRD
deliberately defers index schema and versioning to an ADR.

## Why it matters more than it looks

AC-SPEC-002.2 makes the index schema a published API with a version
identifier, and AC-SPEC-002.3 requires a workspace identifier so
indexes from separate repositories merge into one graph. An edge
collection is materially easier to merge across repositories than
embedded arrays, because edges from repo A pointing at objects in repo
B are just rows — whereas embedded arrays require rewriting the source
object. Getting this wrong is expensive to change after publication.

## Related decisions already made

- Reference relationships are DERIVED from body wikilinks, not
  hand-maintained frontmatter (settled in review; see
  docs/plans/spec-validation-cli-brief.md section 3).
- A 'span' carries a byte offset and length plus line/column, so an
  edge can record exactly where in the source the reference occurs
  (FRD Terminology, revised 2026-07-31).
design:
Input to the index-schema ADR; not standalone work. The ADR must decide:

1. Objects-with-embedded-arrays vs objects-plus-edge-collection vs both.
2. IF both, which relationships live where, and how duplication between
   the two representations is prevented from drifting.
3. Whether edges are typed (references / parent / supersedes / composes)
   or uniform with a 'kind' discriminator.
4. How edges behave across a workspace boundary when the target object
   is not in this repository's index.

Do not implement ahead of that ADR — the index schema is a published
API under AC-SPEC-002.2 and changing it later is the expensive case.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The index-schema ADR records a decision on object-vs-edge representation, with this proposal weighed in Alternatives Considered.
- [ ] The decision addresses cross-repository merge, since that is the case that most distinguishes the options.
- [ ] IF edges are adopted, the FRD's AC-SPEC-002.1 and AC-SPEC-002.5 are re-examined for consistency with the chosen shape.
notes: Subsumed by the reference-integrity feature: ADR-018 takes exactly this decision (references as one top-level edge collection on SpecIndex, both directions derived) and work order agent-plugins-9kb.1 (delta MODEL) implements it. Close or re-scope when agent-plugins-9kb.1 lands; the feature's final DoD item agent-plugins-9kb.10 closes it against the ADR.
close_reason: Superseded by agent-plugins-9kb.1 (MODEL) and ADR-018. index.strata declares a top-level references list of Reference rows on SpecIndex — each carrying path, text, slug, anchor, origin, position and resolution — and both directions are derived from that one collection (corpus.Corpus.InboundReferences / OutboundReferences). This is exactly the separate edge collection dgn asked for; no reference is modelled as an object property on an entry.

title: work-order-template.md frontmatter is not valid YAML
description:
plugin/skills/spec/references/work-order-template.md has frontmatter that fails yaml.safe_load: 'mapping values are not allowed here', line 28 col 23 — the placeholder 'tier_reason: <one line: what about this order drove the tier>' contains a colon-space inside an unquoted scalar, which YAML reads as a nested mapping.

Any tool that parses the corpus (a frontmatter indexer, a schema validator, an Obsidian plugin) fails on this file. skill-authoring-standards already records the sibling failure mode: unparseable SKILL.md frontmatter is invisible in review and only shows up when loaded for real.

Fix: quote placeholders containing ': ' in template frontmatter. Sweep every template for the same pattern, not just this one.
acceptance_criteria: Every template under plugin/skills/*/references/ parses with yaml.safe_load; a regression check covers it

title: standards-template: slug is independent of filename (RFC P3)
description:
## Retro

Implemented in the bead-bonanza orchestrator's own loop (no `Agent` tool
exists in this session), as part of a two-bead shared-surface batch with
agent-plugins-8bx.

**Changed**

- `plugin/skills/spec/references/standards-template.md` — appended five
  lines to the Slug instruction text, inside the HTML instruction
  comment block that opens at line 11 and closes at line 80, so an
  author deletes the note along with the block. The note states that the
  slug is independent of the filename and cites
  cross-document-references.md as the source — not
  template-authoring-standards, per the citation correction the bead
  recorded from triage.
- Instruction block `Version: 1.1` -> `Version: 1.2`.
- `plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` — already at 0.8.0 from
  agent-plugins-fiu; the idempotent bump was a no-op, as the bead's
  Design directed.

**Implicit decisions made**

- Citation form: plain prose `cross-document-references.md` rather than
  `[[cross-document-references]]` or a backticked path. The bead's
  Design permits either. Plain prose matches the surrounding
  instruction-block style, which uses no backticks anywhere, and avoids
  planting wikilink syntax inside a comment block that reference
  tooling would then see in every document authored from the template.

**Constraints honored**

- The `Sections (complete each, then delete its instruction block)` line
  at standards-template.md:15 is present and unreworded — it is the only
  thing clearing this 224-line file past the >100-line
  table-of-contents gate in check-skills.sh.
- The standards row of the References table in
  `plugin/skills/spec/SKILL.md` (now line 256) is unchanged;
  template-authoring-standards.md was not added to it.

**Gates**

- `scripts/sync-shared-references.sh` re-run (standards-template.md is
  under spec/references/), then `--check` — PASS, 11 vendored
  references current.
- `scripts/dogfood-install.sh` — re-materialized `.claude/skills/`.
- `scripts/check-skills.sh` — PASS, exit 0.
- 80-column check on every added/changed line — clean.

**Not done (forced by the orchestrator's no-commit rule)**

No commit, no push. `scripts/bb-close-bead.sh` was deliberately not used
because it commits; close, export and stage were done manually in the
skill's prescribed order.
design:
One edit. Append to the Slug instruction text at
`plugin/skills/spec/references/standards-template.md:29-32`:

    The slug is independent of the filename. A reference resolves
    against this document's frontmatter slug, never its path, so a file
    may be named for how humans will look for it while the slug carries
    the registry-conforming identifier.

Placement: inside the existing HTML instruction comment block that opens
at `standards-template.md:11` and encloses the Slug heading, so that an
author deletes this text along with the rest of the block. It must NOT
land in the document body.

CITATION CORRECTION — found during triage; the source RFC misattributes.
The RFC credits the sentence "A reference resolves against the target
document's `slug` — never a file path" to
`template-authoring-standards.md`. The wording is verbatim correct but
the location is not: it lives at
`plugin/skills/spec/references/cross-document-references.md:44-45`,
verified by grep during triage. IF the appended text cites a source, it
SHALL cite `cross-document-references.md` (or
`[[cross-document-references]]`), never `template-authoring-standards`.

Version bumps:
  - `plugin/skills/spec/references/standards-template.md` — the
    instruction block's "Version: 1.1" (line 13) -> "Version: 1.2"
    (MINOR).
  - `plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` "0.7.0" -> "0.8.0" (MINOR).
    Shared with agent-plugins-fiu and agent-plugins-8bx — set the value
    idempotently; do not bump a second time if it already reads 0.8.0.

DO NOT add `template-authoring-standards.md` to the standards row of the
References table at `plugin/skills/spec/SKILL.md:244`. The RFC weighed
that under "Considered and Not Proposed" and rejected it as the more
expensive of two fixes — it enlarges a bundle the skill deliberately
keeps small.

Keep every changed line at or under 80 characters.
`standards-template.md` is 218 lines and clears the >100-line
table-of-contents gate at `scripts/check-skills.sh:132-136` only via its
"Sections (complete each..." line (line 15). Do not remove or reword
that line.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The note that the slug is independent of the filename appears in
      standards-template.md's Slug instruction text.
- [ ] It sits inside the HTML instruction comment block (so it is
      deleted with the block by an author), not in the document body.
- [ ] If the note cites a source, that source is
      cross-document-references.md / [[cross-document-references]] — not
      template-authoring-standards.
- [ ] The standards-template.md instruction block's Version reads 1.2.
- [ ] The "Sections (complete each..." line at standards-template.md:15
      is still present and unreworded.
- [ ] The standards row of the References table at
      plugin/skills/spec/SKILL.md:244 is unchanged.
- [ ] plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json version reads "0.8.0".
- [ ] Every line added or changed is at most 80 characters.
- [ ] scripts/check-skills.sh exits 0.

metadata.tier_reason: append 4 supplied sentences inside an existing HTML comment block, bump one version string. The single correctness trap (cite cross-document-references, not template-authoring-standards) is stated explicitly in Design and checked in acceptance, so no judgement is left to the agent.

title: spec: state where a new document is written (RFC P2)
description:
## Retro

Implemented in the bead-bonanza orchestrator's own loop (no `Agent` tool
exists in this session), as part of a two-bead shared-surface batch with
agent-plugins-x8t. Dependency respected: agent-plugins-fiu landed first
and had already set the shared `version: "1.4"` line.

**Changed**

- `plugin/skills/spec/SKILL.md` — Authoring Workflow step 1 now names a
  destination for a newly authored document: the project's spec root,
  defaulting to `docs/`, overridable by the project's `AGENTS.md` or
  `CLAUDE.md`, in a type-specific subdirectory (`docs/adrs/`,
  `docs/standards/`, `docs/blueprints/`), with a WHEN clause deferring
  to an established location for that type.
- Frontmatter `version` — already `"1.4"` from agent-plugins-fiu, so
  left alone exactly as the bead's Design instructed.
- `plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` — already 0.8.0 from
  agent-plugins-fiu; the idempotent bump was a no-op.

**Implicit decisions made**

- Rewrapping: the replacement text was re-wrapped to 80 columns rather
  than copied at the bead's display wrapping, per the Design's
  instruction. The emphasis span `**Write it under the project's spec
  root**` is a single span whose source happens to break across two
  lines — markdown renders that as one bold run. The bead's warned-about
  transcription artifact (the span split into three fragments) was not
  reproduced.
- Backticked paths: `docs/adrs/` and friends carry no file extension, so
  the check-skills.sh backticked-path resolver (which matches only
  `.md`/`.json`/`.sh`/`.py`) does not try to resolve them; `AGENTS.md`
  and `CLAUDE.md` are on that check's IGNORE list. Verified by running
  the gate, not by assumption.

**Gates**

- `scripts/sync-shared-references.sh --check` — PASS.
- `scripts/dogfood-install.sh` — re-materialized `.claude/skills/`.
- `scripts/check-skills.sh` — PASS, exit 0.
- 80-column check on every added/changed line — clean.

**Not done (forced by the orchestrator's no-commit rule)**

No commit, no push. `scripts/bb-close-bead.sh` was deliberately not used
because it commits; close, export and stage were done manually in the
skill's prescribed order.
design:
One edit. Replace step 1 at `plugin/skills/spec/SKILL.md:188-189` with:

    1. **Pick the template** from `references/` (table below) and copy
       it as the starting point for the new document. **Write it under
       the project's spec root** — `docs/` unless the project's
       `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` names another — in a subdirectory for
       its type (`docs/adrs/`, `docs/standards/`, `docs/blueprints/`,
       …). WHEN the project has an established location for that type,
       follow it; the frontmatter index does not depend on location,
       but humans do.

Transcription note: the bold span above is
`**Write it under the project's spec root**` as ONE emphasis span. An
earlier transcription of this bead split it into three fragments
("**Write it under**** the ****project's spec root**"); that was a
transcription artifact, not the intended markup. Do not reproduce it.

Rewrap to fit 80 columns rather than copying the wrapping shown above.

Version bumps:
  - `plugin/skills/spec/SKILL.md` frontmatter `version: "1.3"` -> "1.4"
    (MINOR). Shared with agent-plugins-fiu, which is wired to land
    first; if it already reads "1.4", leave it.
  - `plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` "0.7.0" -> "0.8.0" (MINOR).
    Shared with agent-plugins-fiu and agent-plugins-x8t — set the value
    idempotently; do not bump a second time if it already reads 0.8.0.

Do not hardcode a layout onto projects that already have one. The
`AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` escape hatch is the substance of the change,
not decoration — a project with an established spec root must keep it.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Step 1 of the Authoring Workflow in plugin/skills/spec/SKILL.md
      names a destination for a newly authored document.
- [ ] That text preserves the escape hatch: a project whose AGENTS.md or
      CLAUDE.md names another spec root wins over the docs/ default.
- [ ] The text directs a type-specific subdirectory rather than a flat
      spec root.
- [ ] The emphasis markup renders as a single bold span reading "Write
      it under the project's spec root".
- [ ] Every line added or changed is at most 80 characters.
- [ ] plugin/skills/spec/SKILL.md frontmatter version reads "1.4".
- [ ] plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json version reads "0.8.0".
- [ ] scripts/check-skills.sh exits 0.

metadata.tier_reason: rote single-paragraph substitution: exact target line range (SKILL.md:188-189), exact replacement text supplied, plus one version-string bump. No design decisions left open, and scripts/check-skills.sh in acceptance is the safety net that makes the cheap call safe.

title: Evaluate pinning index schema_version with == instead of a regex pattern
description:
`schemas/index.strata:345` declares the index schema version as a pattern:

```strata
schema_version: String ~= /^1\.0$/
```

Strata also supports pinning a scalar to a single value with `==`
(`String`, `Bool`, integer types), which makes the property a constant —
documented at `.claude/skills/strata/references/language-reference.md:450-476`:
"Pin a `String`, `Bool`, or integer type to a single value with `==`. The
property becomes a constant."

The two are equivalent for validation here (`^1\.0$` admits exactly `1.0`),
but they differ in what is generated. A pattern yields a validated `String`
field; `==` yields a constant. Because the schema uses the pattern form, the
emitted value has to live somewhere else — `cli/core/specindex.SchemaVersion`,
a package that exists partly because `scripts/generate-schemas.sh` rebuilds
`cli/core/specmodel/` from scratch on every run and so cannot hold
hand-written constants.

Raised by the strata author in review of PR #16: "Strata does support `==`
constraints for scalars (strings, integers, booleans) which are effectively
constant values. It might not be what you needed but FYI."

Note the skill already documented this — `language-reference.md:451` has
carried it all along. The gap was not missing information; the architecture
blueprint simply asserted "Strata has no notion of a constant", which was
false. That claim is corrected in this PR; this bead is the substantive
follow-up.
design:
Evaluate, do not assume it is an improvement.

**In favour.** `schema_version: String == "1.0"` states the intent directly
(this IS the version, not a value matching a shape), and if the Go emitter
renders it as a constant it removes `cli/core/specindex.SchemaVersion` and the
test that guards the pattern/value agreement
(`cli/core/specindex/specindex_test.go:29,91`) — one fewer place for the two
to drift.

**Against, and what to check first.**

1. **What does the Go emitter actually generate for `==`?** Build a scratch
   `.strata` with `foo: String == "1.0"`, run `strata build --target rust` and
   `--target go`, and read the output. If it emits a plain field plus a
   validation rule rather than a constant, this buys nothing and the bead
   closes as declined.
2. **Does it change the JSON Schema?** `==` most likely emits `const` where the
   pattern emits `pattern`. Confirm against
   `cli/core/schema/*.schema.json` and check nothing consuming those schemas
   depends on `pattern`.
3. **Does it change decode behaviour for a wrong version?** Today an index
   carrying `schema_version: "2.0"` fails the pattern. Confirm `==` rejects it
   the same way and with a comparable message — the CLI relies on that
   rejection to refuse an index it cannot read.
4. **Regeneration cost.** Any change to `schemas/index.strata` requires
   `scripts/generate-schemas.sh` and re-committing every generated artifact.
   Cheap, but it must land in one change.

**If adopted**, update `specs/architecture/module-document-core.md` in the same
change — it currently explains why the constant lives in a separate package,
and that explanation stops being true.

**If declined**, record the reason in the blueprint so the next reader does not
re-raise it.

title: SKILL.md: invert the TaskCreate default so the run checklist is the default and a task list is the exception
description:
Two small correctness defects in `bead-bonanza/SKILL.md`, both found comparing
the skill against the current Claude Code documentation and this container's
actual environment.

**1. The `TaskCreate` default is inverted (`SKILL.md:124`).** It reads: "This
skill defaults to `TaskCreate`/`TaskUpdate` for orchestrator-side progress
visibility. If the project's `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md` explicitly bans
`TaskCreate` ... skip it."

Defaulting to that tool is wrong on three counts: it duplicates the durable
tracker the whole skill is built around (`bd`), its list is session-scoped and
dies with the container, and **it may not exist at all** — a subagent in this
cloud session has no `TaskCreate`, `TaskUpdate` or `TodoWrite` tool. The role
it could uniquely play (in-conversation visibility distinct from durable
tracking) is already filled by the Run checklist the skill copies into its
response at `SKILL.md:34-52`, which is strictly better here: it survives in the
transcript, a human can read it, and it creates no second dependency graph.

**2. Phase 0 does not check `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL`.** Subagent model
resolution order is `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL` env var → per-invocation
`model` → frontmatter → main conversation. The env var **overrides** the
per-invocation parameter. If it is set in a cloud environment, every tier
assignment in the dispatch plan is silently ignored and the Phase 4 escalation
table — which the skill calls "the run's only direct evidence about whether
grooming's routing is calibrated" (`SKILL.md:485-487`) — becomes fiction.

It is NOT set in this container (verified), so this is a latent trap rather
than an observed failure.
design:
**1. Invert the TaskCreate rule.** Make the Run checklist the default and the
task list the exception:

> **Progress visibility.** The Run checklist copied into your response is the
> default and is sufficient. Some projects additionally offer `TaskCreate`/
> `TaskUpdate`; use them only where the project has no durable tracker of its
> own, and never alongside one — two dependency graphs is a correctness hazard,
> not redundancy. Note that a subagent in a cloud session may have no task tool
> at all.

**2. Add the env-var check to Phase 0**, alongside the existing no-delegation
fallback check:

> **Check `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL`.** If it is set, it overrides the
> per-invocation `model` on every dispatch, so tier routing does not happen and
> the Phase 4 escalation table means nothing. Say so once in the dispatch plan
> and omit the escalation table from the final report rather than printing a
> table that cannot be true.

Both edits are small and touch only `SKILL.md`. They should ride along with the
restructure bead rather than being a separate pass over the same file — hold
this until that one is in flight, or fold it in.

Two further native affordances were identified as worth adopting but are NOT
part of this bead; file separately if wanted:
- `SendMessage` to a still-live subagent for skip reconciliation and mid-flight
  correction, instead of the current re-dispatch path.
- `skills: [groom-beads]` frontmatter on the grooming subagent, which injects
  the full skill body rather than relying on the subagent to invoke it.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] SKILL.md makes the copied-in run checklist the default progress-visibility mechanism
- [ ] TaskCreate/TaskUpdate are described as an exception for projects with no durable tracker, never alongside one
- [ ] The text notes that a subagent in a cloud session may have no task tool at all
- [ ] Every downstream reference to the Phase 0 TaskCreate step (Phase 1, Phase 3 step 2, Operating principles) is updated to match
- [ ] SKILL.md states the consequence of CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL being set: no tier routing, and the escalation table is omitted rather than printed
- [ ] The bd-based task tracking the project mandates is untouched
notes:
## Scope narrowed 2026-08-10

The second half of this bead — checking `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL` in Phase 0 —
has moved into the pre-flight script bead, which is where every other Phase 0
environment probe now lives. The consequence this bead documented still stands
and belongs in SKILL.md: WHEN that variable is set it overrides the
per-invocation `model` on every dispatch, so tier routing does not happen and
the Phase 4 escalation table means nothing; the plan says so once and the report
omits the table rather than printing one that cannot be true. Keep that
sentence here; the detection is the script's.

This bead therefore covers the TaskCreate inversion only.

metadata.tier_reason: One rule inverted plus a mechanical sweep of its downstream references; the second half moved to the pre-flight bead.

title: contract-specs-configuration.md's internal surface claims required-sections/block-tag registration that corpus.Profile does not deliver
description:
[[contract-specs-configuration]]'s "internal surface: profile registration"
section states that a profile supplies "the section hierarchy it
requires, and the named section sets a span query can select. It
additionally supplies the fenced block tags to extract and any rule that
cannot be expressed as data — the record-XOR-blueprint-link invariant and
supersession integrity are the two current examples," and illustrates it
with a `Section` struct.

The actual `corpus.Profile` interface (cli/core/corpus/profile.go, as
widened by 9kb.2/XPT) has exactly four methods: Schema, DocumentTypes,
Conventions, Lifecycle. `DocumentTypeRules` carries SlugPattern, Numbered,
ReferenceProperties, TypedReferenceProperties, and Pairings — no
required-sections tree, no block-tag registration, no custom-invariant
hook. profile.go's own package comment confirms this is intentional:
"Element records and required sections are later capabilities, and each
will widen this interface further." A repo-wide search
(`RequiredSection`, `BlockTagRegistration`, `type Section struct`) finds
those identifiers only in cli/core/specmodel/specmodel.go (the generated
spec-index data model) and nowhere in a live Go interface consumed by the
CLI.

So the contract currently describes a surface larger than what
`corpus.Profile` actually delivers today. This predates the
reference-integrity feature and is out of scope for agent-plugins-9kb.9,
whose Design section only asked for the four additive enumerations
(reference-bearing properties, typed references, pairings, lifecycle).
Revise the Required Sections / block-tag / invariant paragraph to
describe current behaviour accurately — either as a stated future
capability (matching profile.go's own "later capabilities" framing) or
by removing the claim if no such registration path exists at all, per
c4-guide.md's rule that a contract misdescribing its own surface is
worse than one that is silent.

title: RFC-0012 P6: mark depends_on aspirational
description:
Adopted at triage of rfcs/inbox/spec/rfc-0012-document-relationship-vocabulary.md (P6) on 2026-08-06. Option (b) taken, per the RFC's own recommendation.

## Problem
SystemBlueprint.depends_on appears on 0 corpus documents, so it reads as a
maintained relationship the corpus does not track. But it is the one
relationship with no other home: a system->system dependency is neither
composition nor a contract, and a top-level system has no parent to own it
under adr-009. It clears the standard's third test, so it is kept.

## Change
schemas/frontmatter.strata: annotate the depends_on doc-comment as
aspirational — recorded on the system's own Context view, unused in the
corpus so far, and explicitly NOT paired (the 'depended-on-by' direction is
derived from the index's inbound edges). Then run generate-schemas.sh.

Do not drop the property; do not add a pairing.

## Acceptance
- generate-schemas.sh --check clean
close_reason: Landed in the RFC-0012 triage on 2026-08-06. See the Resolution in rfcs/retired/rfc-0012-document-relationship-vocabulary.md.

title: Confirm the POSIX-semantics rename support matrix on Windows
description:
cli/core/corpus/sharing_windows.go falls back to SetFileInformationByHandle with FileRenameInfoEx and FILE_RENAME_POSIX_SEMANTICS when MoveFileEx refuses to replace a file readers hold open. Two support questions behind that are unresolved, and neither is answered by Microsoft's own documentation — the Flags field description on the FILE_RENAME_INFO page is empty, as is the FileRenameInfoEx entry in FILE_INFO_BY_HANDLE_CLASS.

1. Minimum Windows version. The Windows 10 1607 SDK headers (10.0.14393.0) already gate both FILE_RENAME_FLAG_POSIX_SEMANTICS and FileRenameInfoEx on _WIN32_WINNT_WIN10_RS1, which points at 1607/Server 2016. Secondary sources say 1709. Cygwin behaves as if 1809 (has_posix_rename_semantics first appears in wincap_10_1809) though that is confounded by it also passing FILE_RENAME_IGNORE_READONLY_ATTRIBUTE, which genuinely is 1809.

2. Filesystem. Every implementation surveyed (Cygwin, git, Rust) restricts POSIX rename to local NTFS and excludes remote/SMB. No authoritative statement was found about ReFS in either direction.

The code does not depend on an answer: an unsupported filesystem or OS reports ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER, the fallback returns the original MoveFileEx error, and behaviour is exactly what it was before the fallback existed. So this is a documentation and confidence task, not a defect.

Work: establish the real floor for both, from Microsoft sources if they can be reached (learn.microsoft.com and devblogs.microsoft.com are both blocked by this environment's egress proxy — the SDK header evidence above came from a header mirror). Then either state the supported matrix in a comment in sharing_windows.go, or add runtime feature detection if the floor turns out to be above a version the project intends to support. Windows CI covers only windows-latest, so a version floor below that is untested by construction — note that either way.

title: ContainerBlueprint declares no version property while ModuleBlueprint does
description:
Discovered during agent-plugins-bge.15, which could not satisfy its own
acceptance criterion "version bumped on each" for the container blueprint.

`ModuleBlueprint` declares a `version` property; `ContainerBlueprint` does not,
and the generated schema sets `additionalProperties: false`. So adding
`version:` to `specs/architecture/container-spec-cli.md` fails the corpus
check. bge.15 bumped the two module blueprints 0.1 -> 0.2 and updated the
container's `updated_at` only, and reported the gap rather than forcing it.

Verified against the generated schema:
    ContainerBlueprint  version property: False
    ModuleBlueprint     version property: True

This is an authoring decision, not a defect to patch blindly. Either
containers legitimately carry no version (and every instruction telling an
agent to bump one is wrong for containers), or the asymmetry is an oversight
in `schemas/frontmatter.strata` and ContainerBlueprint should gain the
property like modules have. SystemBlueprint and ComponentBlueprint should be
checked at the same time — the answer probably applies to all C4 levels
uniformly.

Blocks nothing in the current feature. Same class as agent-plugins-tff: a
workflow instruction that the project's own schema cannot express.

title: Tracker Reconciliation's agent-plugins-6n4 note assumes a broader corpus root than the resolved specs/ self-application gate
description:
# agent-plugins-mvx — Tracker Reconciliation's agent-plugins-6n4 note assumes a broader corpus root than the resolved specs/ self-application gate

## Description

specs/features/spec-index/spec-index-blueprint.md's Tracker Reconciliation
says of agent-plugins-6n4 (work-order-template.md is not valid YAML):

    out-of-scope (coordination): work-order-template.md is not valid
    YAML. The CO parse-failure path records it and the profile
    self-application gate reports it; this feature surfaces the defect
    but does not fix the document.

agent-plugins-bge.14 resolved (comment, 2026-08-04, author confirmation)
that the self-application gate's corpus root is specs/ (27 markdown
documents), not docs/. agent-plugins-6n4's file is
plugin/skills/spec/references/work-order-template.md — outside specs/
entirely. Verified by running corpus.Build against specs/ per bge.14:
the built index and its one exclusion (specs/adrs/README.md,
no-frontmatter) contain no entry or exclusion for anything under
plugin/skills/, and no exclusion or finding correlates with 6n4's file.

So, as scoped, the self-application gate literally cannot report 6n4 —
the blueprint's Tracker Reconciliation sentence was accurate only under
a broader (or pre-reorg) notion of corpus root, and is now stale in the
same way the Definition of Done's docs/ anchor was. bge.14 could not
satisfy its own fourth acceptance criterion ("agent-plugins-6n4 is
confirmed as surfaced by the gate") to the letter for this reason; see
its retro for how that was handled instead.

This is filed for whoever verifies the Definition of Done and retires
the blueprint (agent-plugins-bge.16) to reconcile: either correct the
Tracker Reconciliation sentence to say the self-application gate does
not cover this file (6n4 stays open via some other regression check —
its own AC already asks for one, generically), or make an explicit,
reviewed decision to widen the gate's corpus root. Not blocking
bge.14 — that bead's own job (wire the gate, triage what it finds) is
complete regardless of how this text is reconciled.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The blueprint's Tracker Reconciliation entry for agent-plugins-6n4 no longer claims the self-application gate reports it, and states the actual position: 6n4's file is outside the specs/ corpus root, so the gate cannot surface it as scoped.
- [x] agent-plugins-6n4 remains classified out-of-scope; its disposition is unchanged.
- [x] No other Tracker Reconciliation entry makes a claim contradicted by the resolved specs/ root — the whole section is checked, not just this entry.
- [x] spec check over specs/ reports no new finding as a result of the edit.

## Retro

**Approach.** Read the entire Tracker Reconciliation section (9 entries:
agent-plugins-1ao, -h6c, -igc, -2l2, -47r, -dgn, -6n4, -5nz/-vg1) in
specs/features/spec-index/spec-index-blueprint.md and checked each
sentence for a claim that assumes a corpus root or file location that the
specs/ reorg (and bge.14's confirmation that the self-application gate's
root is specs/, not docs/) would falsify. Rewrote only the 6n4 entry,
which is the one entry making a specific, checkable claim about what a
scoped tool ("the profile self-application gate") does — every other
entry's classification and rationale is either root-agnostic (an ADR
status, a naming decision, a deferred-scope note) or already correct.

**Entry-by-entry verdicts:**
1. `agent-plugins-1ao` (out-of-scope, parent) — no root or file-location
   claim; describes this feature's own delivery umbrella. Unchanged.
2. `agent-plugins-h6c` (out-of-scope, deferred follow-up) — no root
   claim; describes when contract promotion happens. Unchanged.
3. `agent-plugins-igc` (resolved) — no root claim; states the cache-key
   decision. Unchanged.
4. `agent-plugins-2l2` (resolved) — no root claim; states the
   index-vs-manifest naming decision. Unchanged.
5. `agent-plugins-47r` (out-of-scope, relied upon) — no root claim;
   references `[[adr-016]]`'s review status. Unchanged.
6. `agent-plugins-dgn` (out-of-scope) — no root claim; describes a
   reference-modeling scope cut ("this feature indexes no references").
   Unchanged. (Note: the underlying bead's own body cites
   `docs/frds/FRD-spec-validation-cli.md`, which is stale — the FRD now
   lives at `specs/features/spec-index/spec-index-frd.md` — but that
   staleness is in the bead's OWN description, not in this blueprint's
   Tracker Reconciliation entry text, which makes no path claim at all.
   Out of this bead's scope: the AC asks to check the blueprint's
   section, not to correct every discovered-from bead's body.)
7. `agent-plugins-6n4` (out-of-scope, coordination) — **stale, corrected**.
   Was the only entry asserting a specific tool behavior ("the profile
   self-application gate reports it") that the resolved specs/ root
   falsifies, since the file lives under `plugin/skills/`, outside
   specs/.
8. `agent-plugins-5nz`, `agent-plugins-vg1` (out-of-scope) — no root or
   gate-behavior claim; describes these as "reference-feature and
   corpus-data concerns this feature neither resolves nor regresses."
   Unchanged. (Note: `vg1`'s own bead body lists `Files:
   docs/blueprints/{container-spec-cli,...}.md`, also stale — those
   blueprints now live under `specs/architecture/` — but again that is
   the bead's own body, not a claim in this blueprint's Tracker
   Reconciliation text.)

**Implicit decision: what to do about the two OTHER stale bead bodies
found while checking (dgn's `docs/frds/...` path and vg1's
`docs/blueprints/...` paths).** The bead's own AC scopes the check to
"the blueprint's Tracker Reconciliation entry" and "the whole [blueprint]


**Files touched:**
- `specs/features/spec-index/spec-index-blueprint.md` — corrected the
  agent-plugins-6n4 Tracker Reconciliation entry
